Accordion.use: A vertical stack of sections that each open and close, for FAQs, settings groups and long forms. Five looks (`variant`), a chevron or plus indicator and opt-in `keepMounted` panels.
instead: one panel visible at a time and the labels always shown
show or hide a block you control with your own state

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between the triggers and into open panel content
Opens or closes the focused section (native `<button>`)
Move focus to the next or previous trigger and wrap around; disabled triggers are skipped
Focus the first or last trigger

keyboard.text: The list is vertical, so the arrow keys do not swap in RTL. Only a root passed `orientation="horizontal"` uses ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, and those swap in RTL (the root `dir` comes from the document or the nearest `DirectionProvider`).

screenReaders.text: Each `AccordionTrigger` is a `button` with `aria-expanded` inside an `<h3>`, so sections appear in the heading outline. The panel is a `region` labelled by its trigger. A closed panel is removed from the tree (or hidden with `keepMounted`). In `type="single"` without `collapsible`, the open trigger gets `aria-disabled`. The chevron and plus are `aria-hidden`; a `leadingIcon` is not, so pass an `aria-hidden` icon.

motion.text: The panel animates its height and opacity (`animate-accordion-down` and `animate-accordion-up`) and the indicator turns with `chevron-turn`. The reduced-motion net sets the panel animations to 1 ms and ends the transitions, so sections still change state, only instantly.

ssr.text: Closed sections render only their triggers; sections open through `defaultValue` or `value` render their content in the server HTML. The root `dir` is read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so in an RTL document the first server paint has `dir="ltr"` on the accordion until hydration settles it.

gotchas: `type` is required by Radix: `"single"` (add `collapsible` to allow closing the open item) or `"multiple"`. Without `collapsible`, the open item cannot be closed by clicking it.
On `AccordionContent`, `className` lands on the inner padding div, not on the Radix panel; other props (`style`, `data-*`, `forceMount`) go to the panel.

`keepMounted` on `Accordion` keeps every closed panel in the tree, hidden with `data-[state=closed]:hidden`, so inputs keep their state; `AccordionContent keepMounted` overrides it per panel, and `forceMount` wins over both.
`AccordionTrigger icon` overrides the root indicator for one section, and `icon={false}` hides it. The `FAQ` export of this module defaults to `icon="plus"`, the root to `"chevron"`.

AlertBanner.use: A full-width announcement bar for the top of an app or page, with an icon, a message, an optional action and an optional dismiss button. Solid or soft fill, optionally sticky.
instead: a notice inside a form, panel or page body
a transient message that leaves by itself
the user must answer before going on

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves through the `leading` and `trailing` controls, the action and the dismiss button
Follows the action link, or presses the action or dismiss button
Presses the action or dismiss button (not a link)

keyboard.text: The banner itself is not focusable and no arrow key does anything, so RTL changes no key. In RTL the arrow glyph of an `action` object is mirrored and the dismiss button stays on the end edge, which is then the left. Dismissing does not move focus: the banner just unmounts.

items: `tone` `warning` and `destructive` render `role="alert"`, which is announced when the banner is inserted. Every other tone is a `role="region"`, which is not announced on insertion, so do not rely on it for urgent news.
Both carry `aria-label="Announcement"`. Pass your own `aria-label` to rename it. Passing `role` removes the default label, so add one yourself.
The icon is `aria-hidden`; the arrow after an `action` label is too. The dismiss button is named by `dismissLabel` (default "Dismiss banner").
An `action` object renders an `<a>` when it has `href`, otherwise a `<button type="button">`. Any other node you pass as `action` is rendered as is.

motion.text: Dismissing plays `animate-out` (a 200 ms fade and a small slide up). Under reduced motion the slide is removed and the fade stays; the banner unmounts on `animationend`, with a 250 ms timer as a fallback. The hover nudge of the action arrow is a transition and ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: An open banner renders its full markup on the server; it uses only state, and the timer starts in an effect. With `defaultOpen={false}` or `open={false}` it renders nothing on both sides.

gotchas: With `open` set, the banner is controlled: the close button calls `onOpenChange(false)` and `onDismiss`, but it stays until you pass `open={false}`. Without `open`, it hides itself.
It stays mounted for the exit (`data-state="closed"`), so `open` going back to `true` mid-exit brings it straight back.
`variant` is a deprecated alias of `tone` (`brand` is `primary`); `tone` wins when both are set. `inverse` is the dark high-contrast bar.
`appearance="soft"` changes nothing for `neutral` and `inverse`. `message` wins over `children`. `icon={false}` removes the icon.

AnimatedNumber.use: A number whose digits roll to their new values when `value` changes, in tabular figures. Formatting uses `Intl.NumberFormat` (currency, percent, compact), and the first render shows the value without motion.
instead: a number inside a StatCard (it has an `animate` option that uses this)

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: The formatted value is rendered once as visually hidden text, and the rolling digit columns are `aria-hidden` and `select-none`, so a screen reader reads the number once and copy and paste do not pick up the columns. It is not a live region: pass `aria-live="polite"` (props go on the root `span`) to have changes announced. It has no role or label of its own, so say what the number is in the surrounding text.

motion.text: The digits roll through a CSS transition on `transform` and a new digit column fades in with `animate-fade-in`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the net ends the transition in 1 ms and stops the fade, so a change shows at once.

ssr.text: The first render is the final value with no motion and no browser API, so the markup is stable. It is formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat`, though: without `locale` the server's runtime locale and the browser's can format the same number differently (`1,234` against `1.234`) and hydration will warn, so pass `locale` where the HTML is rendered on a server.

slots: `animated-number`: the root `span` (also with `animate={false}`, where it holds plain text)
`animated-number-digit`: one rolling digit column (`data-digit` is its value)
`animated-number-text`: a separator, sign, currency symbol or unit
gotchas: Numbers only: `value` is a `number`. A value that is not finite (`NaN`, `Infinity`) shows as one static piece of text. Format anything else yourself.

Columns are keyed from the decimal point outward, so a digit stays in its column when one is added (99 to 100 keeps the nines and fades in the new hundreds place). Only added columns fade in, never the first render.

`animate={false}` renders plain formatted text with no columns, which suits dense tables and lists; `duration` is in milliseconds and defaults to the fill speed token (`--sutra-duration-fill`, 500 ms).

`locale` also picks the digit glyphs (Arabic-Indic, Devanagari and so on), and a bad `locale` or `format` falls back to the default format instead of throwing. An inline `format` object is fine: it is compared by its contents.

AppStoreBadge.use: A link styled as the "Download on the App Store" or "Get it on Google Play" badge. `store` picks the logo and text (`apple`, `google-play`, `microsoft`, `galaxy`), `theme` the colours and `size` the height.
instead: a normal action or a button-styled link with your own label
a plain link in running text

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the link
Follows the link (a native `<a>`, so Space does nothing)

keyboard.text: No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

screenReaders.text: A native `<a>` named by `aria-label`, which defaults to the badge text, for example "Download on the App Store" or "GET IT ON Google Play" (the Google Play eyebrow is written in capitals). The visible text is `aria-hidden` and the logos are decorative, so pass `aria-label` for a more specific name ("Get Sutra for iPhone"); the test pins that it replaces the default.

motion.text: On hover the badge lifts 1px with a shadow, and on press it scales to 0.98. These are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms: the lift and press still happen, without the glide.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The Galaxy mark takes a `useId` for its gradient, which is stable between server and client.

slots: `mark`: the wrapper around the store logo
`eyebrow`: the small line above the name ("Download on the")
gotchas: Pass `href`. Without it the `<a>` has no link role and cannot be focused, and the type does not require it.

The text, the four logos and the colours (`dark` black badge for light backgrounds, `light` white badge) are fixed brand art: not themed, not localized, and `size` only offers `sm` (40px), `md` (48px, default) and `lg` (56px).
The badge is a link, not a button: for an `onClick` without navigation use `Button`.
Extra props go on the anchor (`target`, `rel`, `onClick`), so add `rel="noopener"` yourself with `target="_blank"`.

AspectRatio.use: A box that keeps a fixed width-to-height ratio (a preset like `"16/9"` or a number) for images, video, embeds and placeholders, with optional rounded corners and frame.
instead: a content surface that grows with its content
a loading placeholder with a set size

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: Adds no role or name: it is a plain `div` around its content. Give the image its `alt`, the video its controls and captions, and the iframe a `title`.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API. The ratio is a padding-bottom on a wrapper (not measured in script), so the box has its final height on the first paint and the page does not jump when the media loads.

gotchas: The width comes from the parent (`w-full`); the height follows from the ratio. `ratio` is a preset (`16/9`, `4/3`, `1/1`, `21/9`, `3/4`, `9/16`) or a number as width over height, default 16/9.

Radix renders an outer wrapper and puts your `className`, `style` and other props on the inner box, which is absolutely positioned to fill it. Size and position the box through its parent, not with `className`.
`cover` (default true) makes a direct `img` or `video` child fill the box with `object-cover` and an `iframe` child fill it; it does not reach images nested deeper.
`rounded` clips the content to the box radius; `framed` adds a muted background and border, which suits a placeholder before the media loads.

AssistantOrb.use: The face of a voice assistant, in one of eight looks a user can pick (glass orb, waveform, mala, Sutra string, ink drop, thread rings, dot graph, halftone). It shows idle, listening, thinking and speaking (plus error and muted) by shape, and follows a live audio level.
instead: bars for a plain input level, no assistant state
a task is loading and nothing is being said
the whole mic button with timer and transcript

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Put it beside a real control (the mic button) and keep that control's name in step with the state. A style picker built from `assistantOrbVariants` should be a radio group (`RadioGroup` with `RadioCard`), so the arrow keys move through the looks.

items: The orb is `role="img"` named for its state ("Assistant is listening") in every look. `label` replaces the name, `label=""` makes it decorative (`aria-hidden`), which is right when a caption beside it already says what is going on (the assistant bar and picker demos do this). The canvas inside is always `aria-hidden`.
The name is not a live region and the orb never announces a change. Announce state changes in a status text of your own (`role="status"`, polite), as the demos do.

A state never relies on motion alone: each look has its own shape per state (the glass orb a ring, an arc or two rings; the string a plucked thread, a turning bead, outgoing waves, a snapped or slack thread; the mala an equaliser, one counted bead, a broken thread, hollow beads; and so on), even at 32 px.

motion.text: `prefersReducedMotion()` (system setting or `<html data-motion>`) stops everything: no frame loop is ever requested, the stylesheet ends the CSS animations, and the live `level` is ignored. The glass orb keeps the still pose of its state (size, saturation, rings, arc); the waveform and the ink looks draw one still frame per state (a fixed moment chosen so the states differ most), redrawn when the state or the theme changes. `paused` freezes the animation where it is without changing the look; a look paused from the start shows the still pose.

ssr.text: The markup is the same on the server and the client. The canvas looks (waveform and the six ink looks) are blank until mount, when they are sized and drawn. The server assumes left-to-right, so a right-to-left page mirrors the travelling motion after hydration.

slots: `assistant-orb`: the root of every look (`data-variant`, `data-state`, `data-paused`, `data-offscreen`; the string adds `data-form="bar" | "square"`; the canvas looks draw on a `data-part="canvas"` child).
gotchas: `level` (0 to 1) is smoothed inside (fast attack, slow release), so feeding it every frame from `useAudioLevel` re-renders nothing; the canvas looks keep a second of history so beads, rings and waves can follow the level of a moment ago. Idle, error and muted ignore it, thinking counts a fifth. Every loop stops off screen, while `paused` and under reduced motion. `useAssistantOrbState(flags)` picks the state by priority: error, speaking, thinking, listening, muted, idle.

`size` is the box of the round looks (default 128) and the height of the bars, waveform and string (default 64, three times as wide; `className="w-full"` stretches them). A numeric size under 48 gives `string` a square box drawn as the Sutra logo; any `string` box under 1.8:1 draws that form. Small sizes keep the state shapes: eight mala beads below 64 px, two ring loops below 120 px (a 2 px line at 32, 7 px at 240), a coarser halftone, fewer graph nodes.

Colours come from the tokens: primary and chart hues in the stock look, one ink in the paper style, `--destructive` for an error, `--muted-foreground` when muted. Gaps are cut out of the canvas, so the looks sit on any surface. Right-to-left mirrors the travel (the string's slide, the mala's swell and count, the graph's turn), never the Sutra bead itself.
The canvas looks cap the pixel ratio at 2. The ink drop is the heaviest (a metaball field each frame): keep one large ink drop on screen rather than many.

Avatar.use: A person's picture with an initials fallback, an optional presence dot and a verified badge. `AvatarLabelGroup` adds a name and a supporting line beside it.
instead: a square tile for an app, provider or tool, not a person
several avatars overlapping with a +N count
a full row with media, title and actions

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Wrap it in a `Button` or a link when it should be clickable.

items: With `name` or `alt` the fallback is a `role="img"` whose `aria-label` is `alt` (or `name` when `alt` is not given; `alt=""` leaves it unlabelled); the loaded `` gets `alt` or `name` as its alt text. With neither, the fallback is an unlabelled `RiUserLine` icon (`aria-hidden`), so a nameless avatar is silent.
`status` renders a `role="img"` dot labelled with the status word ("online", "offline", "busy", "away"). `verified` adds a check icon (`aria-hidden`) with sr-only text "Verified".

`AvatarLabelGroup` shows the name and supporting text as plain text, and the avatar it generates is decorative (`alt=""`), so the name is heard once; its status dot is still announced. Pass `avatarProps={{ alt: "…" }}` to name it anyway. On a plain `Avatar`, `alt=""` likewise drops the image alt and the fallback label.

motion.text: Static, apart from the loaded image fading in with `animate-fade-in`, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` turns off.

ssr.text: Without `src` the initials render in the server HTML. With `src` the server output is an empty frame: Radix Avatar only renders the image after it has loaded in the browser, and `Avatar` delays the fallback by 500 ms (`delayMs`) so a fast image does not flash initials. The frame has a fixed size, so nothing shifts when the image arrives.

gotchas: Initials come from `initials(name, initialsOptions)`: first and last word by default, so "Maya" gives "M". Pass `initialsOptions={{ singleWord: 2 }}` for "MA".

The fallback colour is derived from `name` with `colorForSeed`, so one person has one colour everywhere. `color` overrides it, `colorful={false}` turns it off, and a custom `fallback` node also skips the seed colour. `variant="solid"` fills with the full colour and sets the initials in white or dark ink, whichever contrasts more (about 4.5:1 or better; colours that are not hex keep white).
Passing `children` replaces the built-in image and fallback entirely: compose `AvatarImage` and `AvatarFallback` yourself, then `src`, `name`, `fallback` and `color` are ignored.
Inside an `AvatarGroup`, `size`, `shape` and `ring` come from the group, but a prop set on the avatar wins. The status dot and verified badge sit at the logical end corner, so they flip in RTL.

AvatarGroup.use: An overlapping row of avatars that collapses extra people into a "+N" bubble and can end with a dashed add button.
instead: a list row for each person
show the full list of the hidden people on click

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the add button (only rendered with `onAdd`)

keyboard.text: The avatars and the +N bubble are not focusable. The row is a flex row, so it mirrors in RTL; no key changes.

items: The root is `role="group"`. It has no name of its own, so pass `aria-label` ("Team") when the group means something.
The overflow bubble is a `role="img"` labelled "N more" (its text reads "+N", or "99+" above 99). The add button is labelled "Add member"; change it with `addLabel`.
Each avatar keeps the rules of `Avatar`: labelled by `name` or `alt`, silent without either.

motion.text: Each avatar lifts 2px on hover with a 200 ms transform transition, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: The group is plain markup (no browser API), so it matches on server and client. Avatars with `src` follow `Avatar`: the server HTML holds an empty frame and the picture or fallback appears after mount.

gotchas: `max` slices the children; `total` only changes the count, it does not add avatars. The bubble shows `total - visible` (or `children - visible`), so with `max={2} total={250}` and two children it reads "99+" and is labelled "248 more".
Only React elements count as avatars: strings and `null` are dropped, and a fragment is one child.
The group gives its avatars `size`, `shape` and a background `ring`; an avatar with its own `size` or `shape` prop keeps it, which breaks the even overlap.
The overflow bubble is not interactive. For "click +N to see everyone" put the group in a trigger yourself.

Badge.use: A compact label for a category, tag, status word or count. Four fill styles, three sizes, optional icons and a remove button.
instead: a status with a ready-made dot, icon or spinner and a default label
a filter or selection token that toggles
a small caption above a heading

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to the remove button, which only exists with `onRemove`

keyboard.text: The badge itself is not focusable and has no direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A plain `<span>`: no role, so its text is read inline. Colour carries no meaning for assistive technology, so put the meaning in the text ("Paid", not just a green badge).
The remove button is labelled "Remove" by default. Several badges would all read the same, so pass `removeLabel` with the item ("Remove beta").
`variant="dot"` draws its dot as an `aria-hidden` span. Icons you pass as `leadingIcon` or `trailingIcon` are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons.

motion.text: Static. The only motion is a colour transition, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: `tone` (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, plus legacy aliases like `brand`, `danger`) wins over `color` when both are set. The categorical hues `gray`, `blue`, `purple`, `pink` and `orange` exist only on `color`.
`variant="dot"` is always a neutral bordered pill: the colour only tints the dot, so `variant="dot" tone="success"` is not a green pill.
Long text is truncated (`max-w-full` plus `truncate`), so give the badge a width limit from its parent rather than expecting it to wrap.
`color` is kept for older call sites (the types say "legacy"); new code should pass `tone`.

BatteryLevel.use: A battery reading for a device: a glyph or small bar plus the percentage, warning when low, destructive when critical, with a charging bolt.
instead: a status word or dot, not a number

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: The root is a `role="img"` named from `formatBatteryLevel`: "42% battery", "42% battery, charging", "18% battery, low", "7% battery, critically low", or "Battery level unknown". `label` replaces the whole sentence ("Case battery unknown"). The visible percentage sits inside the image role, so it is not read separately.
The charging bolt is `aria-hidden`; the word "charging" comes from the label.
`loading` with no `value` renders placeholders with `aria-busy` and sr-only text "Loading battery level…" (no image role); `loading` with a `value` keeps the reading and only adds `aria-busy="true"`.

motion.text: The fill animates its width over 500 ms and the loading placeholder pulses, both with `motion-reduce:` variants that switch them off.

ssr.text: Plain markup computed from the props, no browser API, so server and client output match.

slots: `battery-level-fill`: the filled part of the glyph or bar (its width is the percentage; the `text` variant has none)
gotchas: Thresholds are inclusive: `low` (default 20) and `critical` (default 10) are the values at or below which the tone changes, so exactly 20 reads "low" and exactly 10 reads "critically low". The value is clamped to 0 to 100.
The fill colour is chosen in this order: critical, low, charging (success), then `accent`, then the default foreground. `accent` only applies in the normal range.
`showValue={false}` hides the percentage for `icon` and `bar`, but the `text` variant always shows it (otherwise it would render nothing).
A missing, `null` or `NaN` `value` is an unknown reading: a dash and an empty glyph, not 0%.

BottomTabBar.use: Mobile bottom navigation: icon over label tabs at least 44 px tall, count and dot badges, an optional raised centre action and safe-area padding. It hides itself from a breakpoint up. `AdaptiveTabs` shows the same items as inline pills on wide screens and as this bar on phones.
instead: site navigation in a top bar
switch between a few views of one thing

head: Key
Action
rows: Each tab (and the centre action) is its own tab stop
Press a button tab. A link tab follows on Enter only

keyboard.text: It is navigation, not a tablist: there is no arrow-key roving, and no key depends on direction, so RTL changes nothing except that the tabs run right to left.

items: A `nav` named "Primary" (`aria-label`; `AdaptiveTabs` names its two navigations "Sections" and "Sections tab bar") holding a list. The selected tab has `aria-current="page"`; there is no `aria-selected` or `tab` role.
A badge is `aria-hidden`; a hidden "(3 new)" or "(new)" follows the label instead, so the tab reads "Inbox (3 new)". The icon is not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons.
The centre action is a plain button named by `primaryAction.label`. A disabled link loses its `href` and gets `aria-disabled`.
With `AdaptiveTabs` both navigations are in the page and CSS (`display: none`) hides one, so only one is exposed at a time.

motion.text: The active pill grows in over 200 ms, a tap scales the centre action, and a changing badge pops (`animate-pop`). The global net ends the transitions in 1 ms and stops the pop.

ssr.text: Plain markup from props; showing or hiding by breakpoint is CSS (`md:hidden`), so the server and client HTML match.

slots: `indicator`: the active pill behind the icon
gotchas: `position="fixed"` (default) pins the bar to the viewport bottom and hides it from `md` up (`hideAbove`, `"never"` keeps it): give the page bottom padding, and use `static` or `sticky` for previews and frames. The safe-area padding needs `viewport-fit=cover`.

A click selects the tab at once, even for links. In a router app control `value` from the current route (and `onValueChange` for the rest), or the highlight and the page can disagree after back and forward.

A tab is a `<button>`, an `<a>` when it has `href` (through `renderLink` for a router link, which receives `className`, `aria-current`, `onClick` and `data-state`), or your element with `asChild`. Pass `items` or `BottomTabBarItem` children, and `label` is required text.

`primaryAction` is inserted in the middle of the tabs (after the first half), so use an even number of items. `badge` is a number (shown as `99+` above 99) or `true` for a dot; `0` and `false` hide it.

Breadcrumbs.use: The path to the current page as a trail of links. `Breadcrumbs` takes an `items` array and can fold the middle crumbs into a menu with `maxItems`; the parts build custom trails.
instead: switching between sibling views of one page
browsing a hierarchy rather than showing where you are

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between the crumb links and the ellipsis button; the current page and separators are not focusable
Follows the focused link (a native `<a>` does not activate on Space)
On the ellipsis button: open the hidden-crumbs menu; ArrowUp and ArrowDown move through it, Enter follows a link, Escape closes it

keyboard.text: There are no left and right arrow keys, so nothing swaps in RTL. The trail itself follows the reading direction: it flows right to left in an RTL document, and the default chevron separator is mirrored (`slash` and `dot` are not).

screenReaders.text: `Breadcrumb` is a `<nav>` landmark labelled "Breadcrumb" by default (translate it with `aria-label`), holding an ordered list. The last crumb is a `<span aria-current="page">`, not a link, even when its item has an `href`. A middle crumb without an `href` is plain text with no `aria-current`. Separators are `aria-hidden` list items with `role="presentation"`. The ellipsis button is named "Show N more"; a plain ellipsis (no `items`) is hidden from assistive technology entirely.

motion.text: Static: hover colours are transitions that end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The only popup is the ellipsis menu, which keeps its fade and loses its movement like every `DropdownMenu`.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API: server and client output match. The ellipsis menu is closed, so only its button renders on the server.

gotchas: `maxItems` collapses only when `items.length > maxItems` and `maxItems` is at least 2. It keeps `itemsBeforeCollapse` (default 1) crumbs first and `itemsAfterCollapse` last (default `maxItems - itemsBeforeCollapse - 1`, at least 1); if those two cover every item, nothing collapses.
Hidden crumbs without an `href` appear in the menu as disabled rows, because there is nowhere to go.
For client-side routing pass `renderLink` (it receives `href`, `className` and `children`) on `Breadcrumbs`, or `BreadcrumbLink asChild` around your router link when composing the parts yourself.

`separator` on `Breadcrumb` (`chevron`, `slash`, `dot`) sets every separator; a `variant` on one `BreadcrumbSeparator`, or children, override it. Parts need a `Breadcrumb` ancestor only for the shared `size` and `separator` defaults.

BreakdownList.use: Legend rows for a breakdown: colour marker, optional icon, label, right-aligned value and optional percent. Rows can become toggle buttons that hide or isolate series.
instead: a general row with media, title and actions

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between the rows (only when rows are buttons, see `interactive`)
Toggles the focused row's series hidden or shown
Isolates the row: hides all the others, or shows everything if it is already isolated

keyboard.text: Alt-click and a double-click on a row isolate it too. The rows are a vertical list with no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A `ul` of `li` rows: pass `aria-label` ("By container"), since the list has no name of its own.
Interactive rows are `<button aria-pressed>`: pressed means the series is shown. Hidden rows are also struck through and dimmed, and their percent reads a dash.
The colour marker and the icon are `aria-hidden`; the label names the row. Colour is never the only cue, because the label and value are text.
The row `title` is "Click to toggle · Alt-click or double-click to isolate".

motion.text: Static; the hover background is a colour transition, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup computed from the props with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: Rows are plain text unless `interactive` is true, which it is by default only when `onHiddenSeriesChange` is passed. `hiddenSeries` controls the hidden keys; `defaultHiddenSeries` starts them uncontrolled.
`key` defaults to the label when it is a string, otherwise the row index, and hidden state is stored by key.

Percent is `share` when given, else `value / total`, where `total` defaults to the sum of the visible rows: hiding a series changes the other rows' percentages. `valueText` replaces the formatted value.
`color` is a token name (`primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `muted`) or any CSS colour.

Button.use: The standard action. Ten variants and five text sizes plus five square icon sizes, with built-in loading and leading and trailing icon slots.
instead: the action is inline in running text or navigates
a primary action with a menu of alternatives
a set of loose on/off buttons

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` or `loading` button is not focusable

keyboard.text: With `asChild` the child element keeps its own keyboard behaviour: a link activates on Enter only, not Space. Left and Right arrows have no meaning, so nothing changes in RTL.

items: A native `<button type="button">` unless you pass `type`; the name comes from its text. The `icon-*` sizes have no text, so pass `aria-label`.
`loading` sets `aria-busy="true"` and disables the button; the spinner has its own accessible label (`spinnerProps={{ label }}` changes it, `label=""` makes it decorative).
Icons passed as `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon` are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons (Remix icons are decorative when you do).
With `asChild` and `disabled` or `loading`, the child gets `aria-disabled`, `data-disabled` and `tabIndex={-1}`, and clicks are swallowed in the capture phase.

motion.text: The press effect (`active:scale-[0.98]`) and the colour fades are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The `loading` spinner keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

ssr.text: Renders plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The module is a client module in the build (`"use client"`), which is only a boundary: it still renders to HTML on the first server pass.

gotchas: `loading` replaces `leadingIcon` with the spinner but keeps `trailingIcon`, and it also disables the button: do not combine it with your own `disabled` state expecting a different look.
`type` defaults to `"button"`, not the browser's `"submit"`: pass `type="submit"` for form submit buttons.
Use `asChild` for links (`<Button asChild><a href>`); it makes the link look and act inert while disabled or loading, but it is still an anchor, not a button.

`variant="link"` drops the height and padding (`h-auto px-0`); size classes then only change the text. It keeps a 24px-tall hit area (an invisible `::after`), so a stand-alone link button is still a valid tap target.

ButtonGroup.use: Buttons joined into one segmented row or column. Without `type` it is a set of plain actions; with `type="single"` or `type="multiple"` the items become pressable toggles.
instead: a main action plus a menu
a view switch where one option must always be selected

head: Key
Action
rows: Plain group: each item is a tab stop. Toggle group: one tab stop for the whole group, on the active item
Activates a plain item, or toggles a pressable one
Toggle group, horizontal: move focus between items and wrap around
Toggle group, `orientation="vertical"`: move focus between items and wrap around

keyboard.text: In RTL the horizontal arrows follow the reading order: the group passes the document direction to Radix, so ArrowLeft moves to the next item. A plain group has no arrow-key handling.

items: Without `type` the container is `role="group"` of native buttons; name it with `aria-label`. `aria-orientation` is not used on a group, the orientation is `data-orientation`.
`type="single"`: the container is a radio group and each item is `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`. `type="multiple"`: items are buttons with `aria-pressed`.
`ButtonGroupSeparator` is `role="separator"` with the opposite orientation of the group.
An icon-only item (`iconOnly`) has no text, so pass `aria-label`.

motion.text: Only colour and shadow transitions (150 ms), which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. Nothing moves.

ssr.text: Plain markup. In toggle mode the root `dir` is written by `useRootDirection`, so the server HTML says `ltr` and an RTL document settles after hydration; the layout itself is logical and does not change.

gotchas: A toggle item needs `value`; without it the item falls back to the empty string, so two items without a value select together.

`size` on the group is passed to every item, and an item's own `size` wins. Only `sm`, `md` and `lg` exist here; use `iconOnly` plus `aria-label` for a square icon item instead of Button's `icon-*` sizes.
`attached` (default true) removes the item shadows and gives the group one shadow and joined radii; `attached={false}` spaces items with a gap and gives each its own shadow.
`type="single"` is Radix's single toggle group: pressing the selected item again clears the value. Use `SegmentedControl` when one option must always stay selected.

Calendar.use: An inline month grid for picking one date, several dates or a range. A styled `react-day-picker` v9, so every DayPicker prop works (`mode`, `selected`, `onSelect`, `numberOfMonths`, `captionLayout`, `locale`, `weekStartsOn`).
instead: one date from a field with a popover
a range from a field with presets

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves into the grid on one day (the last focused, else the selected, else today) and out again; the other days are not tab stops
Same weekday in the previous or next week
First or last day of the week

keyboard.text: In RTL, ArrowLeft goes forward and ArrowRight goes back (DayPicker reads the `dir` that `Calendar` passes down), and the previous and next month chevrons mirror. Up, Down, PageUp and PageDown do not change.

items: The grid is `role="grid"` named by the month and year, with `aria-multiselectable` in `multiple` and `range` mode. Days are `gridcell`s with `aria-selected`; each day button is named by its full date, prefixed "Today, " and suffixed ", selected" when they apply.

The month label is a polite `role="status"` region, so changing month is announced. The previous and next buttons are named "Go to the Previous Month" and "Go to the Next Month" (English; pass DayPicker `labels` to translate them, and `locale` for dates and weekdays).
With `captionLayout="dropdown"` the month and year are native `<select>`s named "Choose the Month" and "Choose the Year", laid over a visual label.
Without `mode` and `onDayClick` the days are plain cells, not buttons.

motion.text: Day hover and selection fade with short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing else moves; DayPicker's month `animate` option is off unless you pass it.

ssr.text: The grid renders on the server. "Today" comes from the clock at render time, so a server in another time zone, or one that rendered a day earlier, can mark a different day than the client and trigger a hydration warning; pass `today` to pin it. The reading direction is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL document. Dropdown layouts default `startMonth` and `endMonth` from the current year, so they differ across a year change.

gotchas: `captionLayout="dropdown"`, `"dropdown-months"` and `"dropdown-years"` get a default range of 100 years back and 10 years forward; pass `startMonth` and `endMonth` to change it (react-day-picker needs a range to offer year choices).
`showOutsideDays` defaults to `true`, so the days of neighbouring months show muted; outside days are never the Tab target. Pass `showOutsideDays={false}` for blank cells.

In `single` mode a second click on the selected day clears it unless you pass `required`; `selected` with `onSelect` is the controlled pair, and with no `onSelect` DayPicker keeps the selection itself.

Two or more `numberOfMonths` sit side by side only while the column is wide enough; they wrap and stack in a narrow container. The ref goes to the root element, and a `dir` you pass overrides the detected direction.

CalendarHeatmap.use: A GitHub-style activity calendar: one cell per day, in week columns over the last year (`mode="year"`) or in a single month with previous and next buttons (`mode="month"`), with a total and a "Less to More" legend.
instead: a plain grid of values that are not days
choose a date rather than read activity
daily values read off an axis

head: Key
Action
rows: One day cell holds the tab stop; the month buttons are separate stops
The same weekday in the previous or next week
The previous or next day in the week column
The same weekday in the first or last week shown
The first or last day shown
On a day: calls `onCellClick(date, value)` when it is set. On "Previous month" or "Next month" (month mode): changes the month

keyboard.text: The whole calendar is a forced `dir="ltr"` island: time runs left to right and the arrows never swap in RTL; the month buttons keep previous on the left.

items: A `grid` named by `label` (default "Activity in the last year" or "Activity in October 2026") with seven `row`s, one per weekday. Each row header holds the long weekday name as hidden text; the visible short names are `aria-hidden` (every other row in year mode).
A day is named "15 sessions on Oct 3 (Saturday, October 3, 2026)"; days with no data read as 0. `formatTooltip` changes the first part. Month labels, day numbers and the tooltip are `aria-hidden`.
In month mode the title ("October 2026") is `aria-live="polite"`, so navigating announces the new month. The total line ("19 sessions in the last year") and the legend are plain text.

motion.text: Cell colour fades over 300 ms with a transition that the global net ends within 1 ms. Nothing else moves.

ssr.text: Without `endDate` (year) or `defaultMonth` (month) the range starts from `new Date()`, and day keys, month names and numbers use the local time zone and the runtime locale, so the server HTML can differ from the browser's. Pass `endDate` or `defaultMonth` and a `locale` to make both sides agree.

gotchas: Year mode shows exactly the 53 week columns that end on `endDate` (default today) and is fixed width (cell size plus gap, 14 px per week by default), so in a narrow box it scrolls sideways from the oldest week; it does not scroll to the newest.

Several entries on the same day are summed, and entries outside the range are ignored (and left out of the total). `max` defaults to the largest day (at least 1), so one huge day washes out the rest: set `max`.
`date` strings are local calendar days (`YYYY-MM-DD`); a datetime string or a `Date` is bucketed by its local date.
`month` (any date in the month) makes month mode controlled and needs `onMonthChange`; use `defaultMonth` for uncontrolled. `weekStartsOn` is 0 (Sunday, default) or 1 (Monday).

Card.use: The standard surface for grouped content: a bordered, raised box you compose from a header (title, description, action), a body and a footer.
instead: a titled tray around a list of rows
a single row with media, title and actions
the same content in a modal
a ready-made figure with a label and trend

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. A card is not clickable by itself; put a link or button inside (`CardAction`, `CardFooter`), or make the title a link.

items: `Card` has no role. `as` picks the element: `article`, `section`, `aside`, `li` or `div`. A `section` is only a named `region` landmark when it has `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and an `li` needs a `ul` or `ol` parent.
`CardTitle` is a plain `div` unless `as` is `h2`, `h3` or `h4`, so it is not a heading by default. Pick the level that fits the page outline.
`CardDescription` is a `p` and is not linked to the card: add `aria-describedby` on the card yourself if it should be read with it.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

slots: `card`: the root, with `data-size` set to `sm` for the small size
`card-header`: the title row; two columns when it holds a `card-action`
`card-description`: the muted line under the title
`card-action`: the control at the end of the header
`card-footer`: the footer, with `data-variant` set to `plain` or `panel`
gotchas: The parts carry the padding (from `--card-pad`): do not add `padded` to a card made of parts, or the padding doubles. `padded` is for a flat card with your own content.
`size="sm"` shrinks the padding, gap and text through CSS variables on the card (`--card-pad`, `--card-gap` and the text sizes), so every part inside follows it.
`CardHeader` switches to two columns with a `CardAction` through a CSS `:has()` rule; the action sits at the inline end, so it flips in RTL.
`CardFooter variant="panel"` is a muted band with a top border flush with the card edges; the default `plain` footer is just spaced content.

Carousel.use: A scroll-snap strip of slides with previous and next buttons, dots, arrow and Home and End keys, and optional autoplay. Swiping, trackpad and wheel are native scrolling; the slide in view is `value`.
instead: decide on cards one by one
pick a value by scrolling a wheel
plain scrolling content with no slide state

head: Key
Action
rows: Strip (it is focusable), then play or pause, previous, each dot, next. Slides that are fully off-screen are `inert`, so their links and buttons are skipped (a slide showing even a sliver stays interactive)
On the strip or on any control: next or previous slide. Stops at the ends unless `loop`
Press the focused button or dot

keyboard.text: Keys with Alt, Ctrl or Meta are ignored, and so are keys pressed inside a slide, so an input in a slide keeps its arrows. In RTL the keys follow reading order: ArrowLeft is next and ArrowRight previous (the test pins it). The arrow glyphs are mirrored, the strip is scrolled by on-screen distance, and the `progress` bar fills from the right.

items: The root is a `<section aria-roledescription="carousel">` named by `label`. Pass `label`: a section with a name is a `region` landmark, without one it has none.
The strip is a focusable `group` named "Slides". Each slide is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="slide"` named "n of N".

Dots are buttons named "Go to slide n", the current one has `aria-current="true"`. Previous and next are disabled at the ends unless `loop`. `labels` replaces the English strings (the strip, previous, next, play, pause, dot and slide names).
A polite `role="status"` says "n of N" after a button, dot, key press or a free scroll. A slide that autoplay changes by itself is not announced.
`loading` sets `aria-busy` and renders a skeleton with hidden "Loading…" text, which `labels` does not cover.

motion.text: Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the strip jumps to a slide instead of scrolling smoothly, the `progress` bar is not drawn, and autoplay stays off until the user presses play. The dot size and colour changes are transitions that the net ends in 1 ms. The snap itself is the browser's scrolling.

ssr.text: The server renders every slide, the strip and the controls. A starting slide other than the first is scrolled into view after mount, the slide in view is read from an `IntersectionObserver` in an effect, and the preference for autoplay is read in the browser: the server markup of an `autoplay` carousel shows "Pause slide show" and flips to "Start slide show" after hydration for a reduced-motion user.

slots: `carousel-track`: the scrolling strip that holds the slides
`carousel-controls`: the row with play or pause, arrows and dots
gotchas: Slides that do not intersect the strip at all are `inert` (set from the same observer that tracks the slide in view, so they are not inert on the server or before the first report): Tab and the accessibility tree skip their content, and a keyboard user reaches them with the arrows, Home, End or the dots. If nothing reports as showing, no slide is made inert.

`value` follows the strip as well as the buttons, because the slide with the largest visible share wins, so `onValueChange` also fires on a free swipe. Controlled, the parent decides: a press only reports the index.

`autoplay` is `true` for 5 s or a number of ms (at least 1000). It pauses while the pointer or focus is inside and restarts its interval afterwards. Without `loop` it stops on the last slide. A play or pause button shows only with more than one slide.
Each child is one slide (the children of a fragment count one by one), `basis-full` wide unless `slideClassName` says otherwise (`basis-4/5` lets the next one peek). One slide shows no controls.

ChartContainer.use: The frame every Sutra chart is built on, and the parts to build a chart of your own. `ChartContainer` measures its width, gives the drawing an accessible name and a hidden data table; `ChartTooltip` and `ChartLegend` are the readout card and the series toggle.
instead: a standard line, area or bar chart (they already use this frame)

head: Key
Action
rows: On an interactive `ChartLegend` entry: hide or show that series
On a legend entry: show only that series, or restore all if it is already the only one

keyboard.text: `ChartContainer` handles no keys itself: pass `tabIndex` and `onKeyDown` to step through points (the cartesian charts do exactly that). The frame has `dir="ltr"`, so keys you map to arrows keep their physical meaning on an RTL page. `ChartLegend` is outside the island and follows the page direction. `ChartTooltip` is not focusable.

items: The frame is `role="img"` named by the required `label`; everything drawn inside is inside an image, so put data in the `table` prop: a visually hidden `<table>` after the frame (caption is the label, first column becomes row headers).
Mark the SVG you draw `aria-hidden`, as the built-in charts do.
An interactive legend is a `group` named "Toggle series" of buttons with `aria-pressed`; without `onHiddenChange` it is a `list` named "Legend" of `listitem`s. Swatches are `aria-hidden`.
`ChartTooltip` has no role and is not announced; add your own live region for keyboard use.

motion.text: No motion of its own. The legend colours fade with a transition that the global net ends in 1 ms. Motion in your own marks is your choice (use `motion-safe:`).

ssr.text: The first render, on the server and before hydration, passes `defaultWidth` (600) to a `children` function; the real width is measured after mount with a layout effect and `ResizeObserver` and the children re-render. A plain node as `children` is unaffected. The sr-only table and the legend render on the server.

gotchas: Props are spread after the defaults, so a `dir`, `role` or `aria-label` you pass replaces the island's `dir="ltr"`, `role="img"` or the label: do not pass `dir` unless the chart really should mirror.
`ChartTooltip` is absolutely positioned inside the nearest positioned ancestor and does not use a portal; you place it with `style`. It is `pointer-events-none`, so it cannot be hovered or clicked.
`ChartLegend` is controlled: keep the `hidden` keys in state and update them in `onHiddenChange`. Its `marker` is `square`, `line` or `dot`.
`height` sizes the frame (default 240), not the legend; a `table` row's first cell is rendered as a `th scope="row"`.

Checkbox.use: A yes or no box with an indeterminate state. `CheckboxField` adds a label and description, `CheckboxCard` makes a whole bordered card the target, and `CheckboxGroup` binds several boxes to one `string[]` value with an optional select-all.
instead: a setting that applies at once

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between boxes; every box is its own tab stop, a group has no roving focus. A disabled box is skipped
Toggles the focused box (an indeterminate box becomes checked)

keyboard.text: Enter does nothing: Radix cancels it, as the checkbox pattern has no Enter key. Clicking the label or, for `CheckboxCard`, anywhere on the card toggles it. No arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A `<button role="checkbox">` with `aria-checked` set to `true`, `false` or `mixed` (for `checked="indeterminate"`). `required` becomes `aria-required` and `invalid` becomes `aria-invalid`; both are inherited from a surrounding `Field` when you do not pass them.

`CheckboxField` and `CheckboxCard` name the box through a `<label htmlFor>`; the description is added to `aria-describedby`. A bare `Checkbox`, and a `CheckboxField` with neither `label` nor `description`, has no name: pass `aria-label`.
`CheckboxGroup` is `role="group"` named by its `label` (or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`), described by `description` and the surrounding `Field`, and sets `aria-invalid` when `invalid`.
The check and dash icons are `aria-hidden`.

motion.text: The tick pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-50`, and the box scales on press (`active:scale-90`) and fades its colours. Under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and ends the transitions in 1 ms; the tick still appears.

ssr.text: A single `Checkbox` renders the same on both sides, including `checked` and `defaultChecked`. In a `CheckboxGroup` the items register themselves in an effect, so on the server `CheckboxGroupSelectAll` is disabled and unchecked and takes its real state (checked, mixed, enabled) after mount. A surrounding `Field` also adds the `aria-describedby` for its description and error after mount.

slots: `checkbox-indicator`: the span holding the check and dash icons, mounted only while checked or indeterminate
`checkbox-field`: the row of box, label and description
gotchas: `CheckboxGroup` value is the list of checked item values, and `onValueChange` receives the whole new list; items you toggle are appended in click order. Use `name` on the group to post one entry per checked item (with each item's `value`) in a form.
`CheckboxGroupSelectAll` acts only on enabled items, is mixed while some are checked, and is disabled when no item is enabled or registered.

`CheckboxGroupItem` takes `value` (the group item key) and not `checked` or `onCheckedChange`; the group owns them. `disabled` on the group disables every item, and a group `invalid` is passed to each item.
`size` is `sm` (14px) or `md` (16px); the click target stays at least 24px square through the hit area.

Checklist.use: A subtask list with checkboxes, inline editing, add and delete, drag or keyboard reordering, an "n/m" count with a thin progress bar and a hide-completed toggle. It is the ready-made use of `ReorderableList`.
instead: your own rows with a manual order
guided setup steps with status and actions
ordered stages with a current one
a few options for a form

head: Key
Action
rows: Through each row: drag handle, checkbox, the item text (a button), delete button; then the hide toggle and the add field
On the item text: edit it in place. On a handle: pick the row up (then arrows move it, Space or Enter drops, Escape cancels)
In the edit field: save (empty text deletes the item). In the add field: add the item
In the edit field: discard the change. While a row is picked up: cancel

keyboard.text: Leaving the edit field saves it. Up and down are the only arrows, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A `group` named by `label` (default "Checklist") with the "2/5" count next to it. The bar is a `progressbar` named "2 of 5 done".

Each checkbox is named by the item text; the text button is "Edit <text>", the delete button "Delete <text>", the editing input "Edit <text>"; the add field is named by `addPlaceholder` ("Add an item"). Reordering is announced by the `ReorderableList` live region ("Picked up Pack. Position 3 of 5...").
"Hide completed" is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`; it becomes "Show completed (3)". With everything hidden, "All done." is plain text.

motion.text: Rows glide when reordered (`flip`) and hover fades are transitions; under `prefers-reduced-motion` the glide is off and the global net ends the rest in 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup from `items` or `defaultItems`. New ids come from `createId` only when an item is added, so rendering is deterministic.

gotchas: Each entry is `{ id, text, done }`. Control it with `items` and `onItemsChange`, which receives the whole new list after an add, edit, toggle, delete or reorder; ids for new entries come from `createId` (time based by default).

The delete button is hidden until the row is hovered or focused, so on a touch screen it is invisible (it still works when tapped). Set `editable={false}` to drop add, edit and delete; `reorderable={false}` drops the handles and renders a plain list.
With "hide completed" on, reordering only rearranges the unfinished slots: completed items keep their positions.
`hideCompleted` can be controlled with `onHideCompletedChange` (or start hidden with `defaultHideCompleted`); the toggle only appears once at least one item is done.

Chip.use: An interactive pill: a toggleable filter, a removable tag or a selectable option. `ChipGroup` makes single or multiple selection out of several chips.
instead: a static label that is not clicked
a bar of on/off buttons in one control
two to four options that switch a view
pick many tags from a long list

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between chips. The remove button is `tabIndex={-1}`, so it is skipped
Toggles a selectable chip, or runs `onClick` (native `<button>`)
With `onRemove`, removes the focused chip instead of the browser default

keyboard.text: There is no arrow-key roving inside a `ChipGroup`: every chip is its own tab stop. No key depends on direction, so RTL changes nothing.

items: The chip is a `<button>` named by its text. A chip counts as selectable when it has `selected`, `defaultSelected`, `onSelectedChange`, or a `value` inside a `ChipGroup`; then it carries `aria-pressed`. A plain chip has no `aria-pressed`.
`ChipGroup` is a `role="group"` with no name: pass `aria-label`. Single selection is still a set of toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`), not radios.
The remove button is labelled "Remove" unless `removeLabel` says more ("Remove React"). The check mark is `aria-hidden`.
Icon-only content needs an `aria-label` on the chip itself (extra props go to the inner button).

motion.text: Colour changes, the press scale and the check mark sliding open are transitions, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match, including selected state from `defaultSelected` or `defaultValue`.

gotchas: `className` and `wrapperClassName` both style the outer pill (a span); every other prop, including `aria-*` and `onKeyDown`, goes to the inner `<button>`.

A chip in a `ChipGroup` needs a `value`; without one it is a plain chip that ignores the group. In the group the default tone is `primary`, outside it `neutral`; a chip's own `tone` or `variant` wins over the group's.
`type="single"` lets the selected chip be clicked off (`onValueChange(null)`); pass `allowDeselect={false}` to keep one selected. `type="multiple"` calls `onValueChange` with the whole list.
`color` is deprecated: use `tone`. The remove button does not toggle the chip and stops the click; a disabled chip disables it too.

CloseButton.use: The icon-only "X" for dismissing a dialog, alert or toast, and, with `shape="pill"`, the small round remove mark inside a chip, tag or badge.
instead: a labelled action (use an `icon-*` size for other icons)
a removable label, it has `onRemove` built in
a removable or selectable chip, it has `onRemove` built in
the close part of a Dialog

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` button is skipped

keyboard.text: Left and Right arrows have no meaning, so nothing changes in RTL. The X glyph is symmetric and is not mirrored. A parent can take the button out of the tab order: `Chip` does this for its remove button.

items: A native `<button>` with `type="button"` unless you pass `type`, so it never submits a form by accident.
The accessible name is `aria-label`, which defaults to the English "Close". Pass a specific one ("Remove filter", "Close settings") when it does not close a whole dialog or when the UI is localized.
The default X icon is `aria-hidden`. If you pass `children`, they replace the icon and you must hide a decorative icon yourself.

motion.text: The press effect (`active:scale-95`) and the colour fades are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The `pill` shape has no press effect.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so the server and client output match.

gotchas: `shape="pill"` carries no focus ring, no press effect and no `disabled` styling: it assumes the chip, tag or badge around it supplies them. Used on its own, add `focusRing` through `className`.
`shape="control"` (the default) has a 24px hit area, 44px under a coarse pointer, even at the small sizes. `pill` keeps the 24px minimum for its 16px `3xs` size.
`variant` only sets colours: `ghost` (default), `subtle`, `inverse` for dark surfaces, `current` (inherits the text colour, dimmed until hover) and `muted`. `current` is meant for pills.
`size` runs from `3xs` (16px) to `lg` (36px), default `md` (32px); the icon scales with it.

CodeBlock.use: Syntax-highlighted code with an optional header (file name or language, wrap toggle, copy button), line numbers and highlighted lines. `CodeBlockTabs` switches between snippets (npm, pnpm, yarn, or several files); `InlineCopy` is a one-line command with a copy button.
instead: any single value with a copy button that is not a command
a short code span inside a sentence

head: Key
Action
rows: The wrap toggle and copy button in the header, then the code area, which is a tab stop because it scrolls
On the copy button: copy. On the wrap toggle: switch wrapping
`CodeBlockTabs`: move between tabs and show that snippet at once; wraps from the last to the first

keyboard.text: The whole block is a `dir="ltr"` island, so the tab arrows do not swap in RTL.

items: The code is a `<pre tabindex="0"><code>` (focusable so it can scroll) with no role or label. Line numbers are `aria-hidden` and not selectable, so neither screen readers nor copy-paste see them.
`highlightLines` is a colour and a bar only; it is not announced. The language and file name are plain header text.

The copy button is named "Copy code" (`InlineCopy`: "Copy command") and a polite live region announces "Copied to clipboard"; the wrap toggle is "Toggle line wrap" with `aria-pressed`. The `$` prompt of `InlineCopy` is hidden from assistive technology and is not copied.
`CodeBlockTabs` is a Radix `tablist` of `tab`s and a `tabpanel` per snippet.

motion.text: The copy icon swaps with a 200 ms transition, the tab underline slides in over 200 ms and the header buttons fade, all transitions that the global net ends within 1 ms. Nothing else moves.

ssr.text: Highlighting is a pure function of `code` and `language`, so the server renders the full tokenized markup with no browser API. The clipboard is touched only on click.

gotchas: Highlighting is a small built-in tokenizer for `ts`/`js`/`tsx`/`jsx`, `json`, `css`/`scss`, `html`/`xml`/`svg`, and `bash`/`sh`/`shell`. Other languages (python, go, rust) render as plain text, so use another highlighter inside your own `pre` for them.
`theme="dark"` (default) is an always-dark surface from the `--code-*` tokens, also in a light app; `"light"` follows the app theme. `InlineCopy` defaults to `"light"`.

With no header (no `filename`, `language`, `actions` or `showWrapToggle`, or `hideHeader`), the copy button floats in the corner and is visible only on hover or keyboard focus, so touch users never see it: give the block a `language` or `filename`.

`code` wins over `children`; a trailing newline is removed. `wrap` is controllable only on `CodeBlock` (`wrap`, `defaultWrap`, `onWrapChange`, toggle with `showWrapToggle`); `CodeBlockTabs` takes a plain `wrap` and `highlightLines` per tab.

Collapse.use: Opens and closes a block of your own content with a height animation from your own `open` state, with no measuring. For filter rows, wizard steps and expandable regions that have no built-in trigger.
instead: a ready trigger, `aria-expanded` wiring and uncontrolled state
a group of sections with arrow-key navigation
content that should block the page

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The trigger is yours; closed content is `inert`, so Tab skips everything inside it until it opens.

screenReaders.text: `Collapse` adds no role, name or `aria-expanded`: put `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on your own trigger (pass an `id` to `Collapse` for it). The root carries `data-state="open"` or `"closed"`. Closed content is `inert`, which removes it from focus and the accessibility tree while it stays mounted (unless `unmountOnExit`). Nothing is announced when it opens.

motion.text: The grid track animates from `0fr` to `1fr` with an opacity fade (`fade={false}` skips the fade). The reduced-motion net ends the transition in 1 ms, so the block still changes state, just at once; `transitionend` still fires, so `unmountOnExit` unmounts as usual.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API at render. A closed `Collapse` renders its children `inert` and collapsed, or nothing at all with `unmountOnExit`; an open one renders them. The first render is not animated.

slots: `collapse`: the root grid that animates its rows
`collapse-content`: the clipping wrapper around the children (`contentClassName`)
gotchas: It is controlled only: `open` is required and there is no `onOpenChange`; drive it from your state, or use `Collapsible` for a trigger and uncontrolled state.
Put padding on a child, not on `contentClassName`: padding on the clipping wrapper keeps its height when closed, so the block never reaches zero.

`unmountOnExit` removes the children after the `grid-template-rows` transition ends, with a 600 ms timer as a fallback when no `transitionend` arrives (hidden tab, `display: none` ancestor). Reopening before that cancels the removal.
Children stay mounted while closed by default, so effects, inputs and iframes inside keep running; use `unmountOnExit` to drop them.

Collapsible.use: A single show and hide section with its own trigger button and an animated height. Controlled or uncontrolled, with `default`, `surface` and `ghost` looks.
instead: several related sections with arrow-key navigation and one-open-at-a-time
you already have a trigger and state and only need the height animation
a small floating panel instead of pushing content down

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the trigger; a disabled trigger is skipped

keyboard.text: The trigger is the only stop; there are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. Closed content is `inert`, so Tab never lands inside it.

screenReaders.text: `CollapsibleTrigger` is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the content wrapper. The panel has no `region` role or label of its own (unlike `AccordionContent`). The turning chevron is `aria-hidden`. Closed content is `inert`. With `asChild` the child gets the same attributes plus a click handler, so pass a real button or give your element its own role and keyboard handling.

motion.text: The height and opacity transition is the one from `Collapse`, and the chevron turns with `chevron-turn`; the reduced-motion net ends both in 1 ms.

ssr.text: Renders the same markup on server and client with no browser API. A closed section (the default) renders no content; `defaultOpen` or `open` renders it. With `keepMounted` the closed content is in the HTML, collapsed and `inert`.

slots: `collapsible-content`: the animated panel (this replaces `Collapse`'s own `collapse` slot name; the inner `collapse-content` wrapper remains)
gotchas: This is not the Radix Collapsible: it is built on `Collapse` and is not a drop-in for `@radix-ui` props. `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` work as usual, and a controlled `open` stays put until you change it.
`CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent` throw outside a `Collapsible`.
Closed content is removed after the close animation by default; `keepMounted` on the root, or on one `CollapsibleContent` (which overrides the root), keeps it mounted and `inert`.
`className` on `CollapsibleContent` goes to the inner padded box; other props (`id`, `style`) go to the outer `Collapse`, and overriding `id` breaks the trigger's `aria-controls`.

Combobox.use: A searchable select for long lists: an input-like trigger and a popover with a search box. Single or `multiple` (chips), `creatable`, async through `filter`, `inputValue` and `loading`.
instead: a short list that needs no search
free-form tags with no fixed list
two to four options that switch a view

head: Key
Action
rows: On the trigger: open the list and focus the search box
In the list: move the highlighted option, looping at the ends. Ctrl+N, J, P and K do the same
Highlight the first or last option
Pick the highlighted option (or the "Create" row). Single mode closes; `multiple` stays open and toggles
Close and return focus to the trigger

On the trigger, `multiple`: remove the last chip. With `confirmBackspace` the first press marks it and the second removes it; a held key never confirms. With `clearable` and single mode it clears the value
On the trigger with `clearable`: clear every selection
Leaves the trigger; the chip remove buttons and the clear button are not tab stops (`tabIndex` -1)

keyboard.text: `openOnFocus` also opens the list on keyboard focus, not on a pointer press or when focus returns. The list is vertical, so RTL swaps no keys.

items: The trigger is a `div role="combobox"` with `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-disabled` when set. It is named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel` (a `<label htmlFor>` cannot name a div, so the wrapper points at the label id). The selected labels are its text.

The popover is a `role="dialog"` with the same name, or the `placeholder` as a fallback. Inside, the search box is a combobox with `aria-activedescendant`, the list is a `listbox` (`aria-multiselectable` when `multiple`, `aria-busy` while `loading`) and each row is an `option`.

Chosen options carry `aria-checked="true"` (and `data-checked`, for styling): in `multiple` mode every option is `true` or `false`, in single mode only the chosen one has it. The check icon is decoration. In cmdk `aria-selected` means highlighted, not chosen.

The empty message sits in a polite live region next to a hidden listbox. The `confirmBackspace` prompt ("Press Backspace again to remove ...") is a polite live region on the trigger. The loading text is not a live region.
Chip remove buttons are named "Remove" plus the label; the clear button uses `clearLabel`.

motion.text: The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the net removes the movement. A chip you just added eases in only under `motion-safe:`, so it appears at once with reduced motion. The loading spinner keeps turning.

ssr.text: The trigger renders on the server with its selected labels or placeholder (labels come from `options`). The popover is portalled, so with `open` or `defaultOpen` the list appears after hydration.

slots: `combobox-empty`: the polite region that holds the empty message
`combobox-loading`: the loading row shown while `loading` and no option is visible
`combobox-announcer`: the screen reader prompt, rendered only with `confirmBackspace`
gotchas: Single mode: `value` is a string and `""` means nothing selected; `multiple` takes and returns `string[]`. Picking the selected option again does not unselect it (and does not call `onValueChange`); use `clearable`.
There is no `name` prop and no hidden input, so the value does not post with a native form: read it from `onValueChange`.

`filter={false}` shows `options` exactly as given, for server search: drive it with `inputValue` and `onInputValueChange` (the text clears when the list closes) and debounce the fetch yourself. A selected value keeps its label after it leaves the results.

`creatable` adds a "Create" row only when the query matches no label (case-insensitive) and `loading` is off; the string `onCreate` returns is selected instead of the typed text. `emptyText` is a deprecated alias of `emptyState`.

CommandDialog.use: A command palette: a top-anchored modal with a search field and a filtered, keyboard-driven list of commands (built on cmdk). `Command` and its parts also work inline without the dialog; `CommandPaletteFromRegistry` fills it from the registered shortcuts, and `useCommandMenuShortcut` opens it with Ctrl or Cmd+K.
instead: a modal with your own content
pick a value for a form field
the button that opens a palette
a short list of actions on a button

head: Key
Action
rows: Open or close it, when `useCommandMenuShortcut` is used (the letter is its second argument)
Highlight the next or previous item; wraps around (`loop`)
Jump to the next or previous group
Jump to the last or first item
First or last item (they do not move the text caret)
Close; focus returns to what had it before, also when opened by a hotkey
Stays inside the dialog; the search field is its only tab stop

keyboard.text: The list is vertical, so the arrows do not swap in RTL. The panel centres itself with logical offsets, and shortcut chips sit at the inline end.

items: The dialog is `role="dialog"` named by the hidden `title` (default "Command menu"), with a hidden `description`. Focus is on the search field, a `combobox` with `aria-activedescendant` pointing at the highlighted `option` of a `listbox`; options carry `aria-selected`.
An explicit `aria-label` on `CommandInput` wins over the title as its name. Group headings are `aria-hidden` and the group is labelled by them.
With no match, the empty listbox is hidden and `CommandEmpty` is announced from a polite live region beside it, never from an empty listbox. A `forceMount` item stays as a real option.
`CommandLoading` is a `progressbar` named by its `label` ("Loading..."); its children are `aria-hidden`.

motion.text: The panel fades and zooms in from the top (`animate-in`), and the list height and the highlight animate with 150 ms transitions. The global net removes the movement and ends the rest in 1 ms.

ssr.text: A closed dialog renders nothing on the server or the client (the panel is portalled), and one that is `open` on first render appears after hydration. `useCommandMenuShortcut` only attaches its listener in an effect. An inline `Command` renders on the server, but `CommandEmpty` appears only after the list has mounted.

slots: `command-empty`: the live region beside the list that holds `CommandEmpty`
gotchas: `CommandDialog` has no trigger: control it with `open` and `onOpenChange` (or `defaultOpen`). `useCommandMenuShortcut(setOpen)` toggles; inside a `ShortcutProvider` it registers as "Command menu" and works from inputs, otherwise it uses its own document listener and skips events another handler already prevented.

The dialog sets `loop` and `vimBindings={false}` on its `Command` (so Ctrl+K can close it); a bare `Command` keeps cmdk's defaults, where Ctrl+N, J, P and K move the highlight. Pass your own through `commandProps`.
Filtering is cmdk's fuzzy match on each item's `value` (or its text); `onSelect` receives that value. Use `shouldFilter={false}` in `commandProps` for server-side results.
`CommandPaletteFromRegistry` lists shortcuts registered with `useShortcut`, so it is empty without a `ShortcutProvider`. It closes first and runs the command on the next tick so focus can return.

Container.use: Centres page content and caps its width, with responsive horizontal padding (16, 24 and 32 px). Sizes `sm` to `xl`, or `full` for no cap.
instead: vertical or horizontal flow inside it

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: A plain `div` with no role. For a landmark, pass `asChild` and a `main`, `section` or `nav` child (`<Container asChild><main>...</main></Container>`): the child keeps its own role and gets the container styles. A `section` is only a landmark when it has a name.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: `size` sets `max-width`: `sm` 48rem, `md` 64rem, `lg` (default) 80rem, `xl` 90rem, `full` none. The padding is always applied, including on `full`.
It is `mx-auto w-full` with the padding built in, so nest it once per page region; a `Container` inside another one adds its padding twice.
`className` is merged last: a `px-0` or a `max-w-*` of yours wins over the size.

ContextMenu.use: A menu of actions that opens at the pointer on right-click or touch long-press over an area, for rows, canvases, files and cards. It shares its rows and styling with `DropdownMenu`.
instead: a visible trigger button opens the menu
choosing a value for a field

head: Key
Action
rows: Move the highlighted row; focus stops at the ends unless you pass `loop` to `ContextMenuContent`
Highlight the first or last row
Typeahead: highlights the next row whose text starts with it
Activate the highlighted row, or toggle or pick a checkbox or radio row; the menu closes
On a sub-menu trigger: open it (Enter and Space do too)
Inside a sub-menu: close it and return to its trigger
Does nothing while the menu is open

keyboard.text: The trigger is a plain `<span>` with no tab stop, and Radix opens the menu only from a `contextmenu` event (right click) or a 700 ms touch or pen press. Keyboard users cannot reach it from Tab, so offer the same actions elsewhere (a `DropdownMenu` button). In RTL ArrowLeft opens a sub-menu and ArrowRight closes it.

screenReaders.text: The panel is `role="menu"`; rows are `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` with `aria-checked`, groups are `role="group"`, and a disabled row gets `aria-disabled`. The trigger area gets no role or hint, so a screen reader user is not told a context menu exists: describe it or add a visible alternative. The sub-menu trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`. The check and chevron icons are `aria-hidden`; the radio dot is an empty span.

motion.text: The panel fades and zooms in from the pointer with the `animate-in` utilities; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. Rows highlight instantly.

ssr.text: The trigger span renders on the server; the menu does not exist until a `contextmenu` event, and its panel is portalled after mount. Nothing differs between server and client.

gotchas: A touch long-press opens the menu after 700 ms and cancels if the finger moves; mouse users need the right button (the `contextmenu` event).
`modal` defaults to true: while the menu is open, pointer events outside it are blocked and focus is trapped. Pass `modal={false}` on `ContextMenu` to keep the page interactive.

Unlike `DropdownMenuContent`, `ContextMenuContent` has no `sideOffset` or `align` defaults: the menu opens at the cursor. `ContextMenuTrigger` renders a `<span>`: pass `asChild` to use your own element, and make it a block or give it a size so the whole area responds.
`shortcut` is display only, `tone="destructive"` replaces the deprecated `variant`, and with `asChild` on `ContextMenuItem` the `icon`, `description` and `shortcut` props are ignored.

CopyButton.use: Copies a value to the clipboard, swaps its icon to a check mark and announces "Copied to clipboard". `CopyField` wraps it in a read-only row for commands, ids, keys and URLs.
instead: the user types or edits the value (CopyField is read-only)

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the copy button. A `disabled` one is skipped

keyboard.text: `CopyField` itself is a `role="group"` that is not focusable: only its copy button is. No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

items: The `icon` variant has no visible text, so `label` is its `aria-label` and `title`; after a copy both become `copiedLabel` for `timeout` ms (default 1600).
The `button` and `ghost` variants show `label` or `copiedLabel` as text and set no `aria-label`.
A visually hidden polite live region next to the button says "Copied to clipboard" after a successful copy. The text is fixed English and does not follow `copiedLabel`.
`CopyField` is a `group` named by `label`, and its button is named "Copy <label>" ("Copy" without a label). The `prefix` is `aria-hidden` and is not copied.
An `aria-label` you pass lands after the built-in one and wins, so the name stops changing to "Copied" (the live region still announces).

motion.text: The icon swap (the copy glyph shrinks away, the check grows in) is an opacity and scale transition, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms, so the swap is instant. The timer for the copied state is unaffected.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API at render (`navigator.clipboard` is read in the click handler), so server and client output match.

gotchas: A failed write (permission denied, an insecure context, no `navigator.clipboard`) shows nothing: no copied state, no `onCopied`, no error. Handle the fallback yourself if the page may not be served over HTTPS.
`value` may be a function, read at click time, so it can copy what is current. One that throws is swallowed and nothing is copied. An `onClick` that calls `preventDefault` cancels the copy.
It renders two siblings, the button and the live-region span, so a parent with `gap` or `:last-child` rules sees both. `ref` is the button.

`CopyField` truncates the value and puts the full text in `title` (`truncate={false}` wraps it instead), shows it in `<code>` unless `mono={false}`, and `copyButtonProps` passes props, such as `variant`, to the inner button.

Countdown.use: Time left until a moment, as days, hours, minutes and seconds boxes or a compact "2h 14m" line. It fires `onComplete` once at the deadline and can switch to a warning tone for the last stretch. Use it for sales, expiring codes and session timeouts.
