instead: a changing number without a clock
the remaining time as data for your own layout

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: The root is `role="timer"` with an `aria-label` such as "Time remaining: 2 hours 14 minutes" (up to three units, seconds shown only under a day), or "Time is up" once finished. The digits, colons and unit captions are `aria-hidden`, so the label is all that is read.

A timer is not a live region by default, so nothing is announced while it ticks; the label is current when someone reads it. Add `aria-live` only if you want announcements, and expect chatter once a second.
`data-urgent` and the warning colour are visual: put an explicit message next to the countdown if the last stretch matters.

motion.text: The optional `flip` entrance (`animate-in` with a small slide) is skipped when the reduced-motion preference is on (read live). Without `flip` the digits change in place, so the component never moves.

ssr.text: The remaining time is computed from `Date.now()` during the first render, so the server's snapshot differs from the browser's first render by the time between them (seconds in the label and digits change on the first tick after mount). Pass a deadline far enough ahead, or hide the countdown until mounted, if a mismatch warning matters.

gotchas: `target` is a `Date` or epoch milliseconds. The display recomputes from the wall clock on every tick, so it does not drift when the tab was in the background.

`onComplete` fires once per `target`, also when the target is already past on mount. When finished, the zeros stay unless you pass `completeContent`, which replaces the digits (the root still has role `timer` and "Time is up").

`format="compact"` shows the two largest units ("2h 14m", "45s"); `segments` hides the days box when there are no whole days and `hideSeconds` drops the seconds box (and ticks once a second instead of four times).
`urgentBelow` (milliseconds) only sets the warning tone and `data-urgent` during the last stretch while time remains; it does not change the label.

DataTable.use: A table built from `columns` and `data`, with click-to-sort headers, optional row selection with select-all, skeleton loading rows and an empty state. A generic component: it is typed by your row type.
instead: compose the markup yourself or when the layout is custom
a list of rows with media and actions

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves through the scroll box (only while the table overflows it), the sort buttons, clickable rows, the checkboxes and controls inside cells
On a sortable header, cycles that column: ascending, descending, unsorted
On a checkbox, selects or clears the row (or all rows, in the header)
On a focused row (only with `onRowClick`): calls `onRowClick`

keyboard.text: With `onRowClick`, each row is a tab stop and Enter or Space on the focused row calls it (a key press on a button or link inside the row keeps its own meaning). Without `onRowClick` rows are not focusable. There is no arrow-key movement. `align` is logical (`left` is the start side), so columns flip in RTL.

items: A native `table`; headers are `th scope="col"`. A sortable column (`sortable: true`) holds a button and carries `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending`, `none`); a column that is not sortable has neither.

With `selectable`, the header checkbox is labelled "Select all rows" and every row checkbox is labelled "Select row" unless you pass `rowLabel`, for example `(row) => "Select " + row.name`; without it the boxes are not told apart by name. The select-all box shows the mixed state when some rows are selected.
`loading` puts `aria-busy="true"` on the table and fills the body with `aria-hidden` skeleton rows. No "Loading" text is announced, so add your own status message.
Empty `data` shows one full-width cell with "No results", or your `emptyState`. `caption` renders a `<caption>` under the table.

motion.text: Row hover and checkbox ticks are transitions that the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The loading skeletons use a shimmer with `motion-reduce:animate-none`.

ssr.text: The table renders fully on the server, including sorted and selected rows from `defaultSort` and `defaultSelectedRowIds`. Two small things settle after mount: the mixed (indeterminate) state of the select-all box is a DOM property set in an effect, and string sorting uses the runtime's default locale, so a server and a browser with different locales can order special characters differently.

gotchas: Sorting happens in the browser and cycles asc, desc, then none (`onSortChange(null)`). Set `manualSorting` when the server sorts: the data order stays yours and the headers still report the sort. Empty values (`null`, `undefined`, "") stay last in both directions, text compares case-insensitively with numeric order ("item2" before "item10"), and ties keep the original order. `sortValue` gives a column its own sort key.

Selection is stored by row id: `getRowId` defaults to `row.id` (string or number), else the row's index in `data`, so supply `getRowId` when data is filtered or reordered. Select-all picks every row in `data`, not only the visible page; from a partial selection it clears the rows instead.
`onRowClick` is on the `<tr>`: clicks from buttons or links you put in a cell bubble to it unless you `stopPropagation` (the selection checkboxes already do).

`columns[].key` must be unique and reads `row[key]` unless `cell` is given. The `ref` is a plain prop (React 19) that reaches the `<table>`; `className` styles the outer box and `tableClassName` the table.

DatePicker.use: An input-like button that opens a calendar popover to pick one date. Picking a day sets the value and closes the popover. For a range or a date with a time, use the sibling pickers.
instead: a from and to range with presets

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves to the trigger, the clear button (when `clearable` and a date is set) and, while open, through the calendar
On the trigger: open the calendar (native button)
Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End
In the calendar: move the focused day by day, week, month or year (see Calendar)
On a day: pick it and close the popover
Close without changing the value; focus returns to the trigger

keyboard.text: The trigger is a plain button, so ArrowDown does not open it. In RTL the Left and Right arrows swap inside the calendar and the previous and next month chevrons mirror.

items: The trigger is a native `<button>` that shows the formatted date, or the `placeholder`. The popover is a `role="dialog"` named by `aria-label`, falling back to the placeholder and then "Choose date"; a `FieldLabel` or `aria-labelledby` names the trigger, not the dialog.
`required` only sets `aria-required`, `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` and a surrounding `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled`, `required` and `invalid` when you do not pass them.
A given name (`aria-label`, a `FieldLabel`, `aria-labelledby`) replaces the button text as its accessible name, so the chosen date is not part of that name. The clear button is named "Clear date".
The calendar inside is a labelled grid with day buttons named by their full date (see Calendar).

motion.text: The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the reduced-motion net removes the movement and ends the transitions in 1 ms. The calendar itself only has short hover transitions.

ssr.text: The trigger renders on the server and the popover is portalled, so it appears only after mount. A trigger with a `value` or `defaultValue` is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the runtime's default locale and time zone unless you pass `locale` or `formatDate`, so a server and a browser that differ can print different text and trigger a hydration warning. The portalled layer does not inherit a subtree `dir` or `data-style`; set them on `<html>`.

gotchas: `locale` formats the trigger text and also sets the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday (through `Intl`); `formatOptions` only formats the trigger. The calendar's aria labels ("Go to the Next Month", the day names read by a screen reader) stay English: they are not derived from `locale`.
`className` goes to the wrapper `div` around the trigger, not to the button; `contentClassName` styles the popover.
Clicking the day that is already selected clears the value (`onValueChange(undefined)`) and leaves the popover open; `clearable` adds an explicit button.

With `name` a hidden input posts the local day as `YYYY-MM-DD` (empty when none). `required` blocks nothing in a native form. `startMonth` and `endMonth` limit navigation, `disabledDates` takes react-day-picker matchers.

DateRangePicker.use: An input-like button that opens a two month range calendar with a presets sidebar and an Apply and Cancel footer. The value changes only when the user applies.
instead: a few fixed periods with no calendar

head: Key
Action
rows: Through the trigger, the clear button, then (open) the presets, the calendar, Cancel and Apply
On the trigger: open; on a preset or a day: choose it; on Cancel or Apply: run it
Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End
In the calendar: move the focused day (see Calendar)
Close and discard the draft; focus returns to the trigger

keyboard.text: The trigger is a plain button, so ArrowDown does not open it. In RTL the Left and Right arrows swap inside the calendar and the month chevrons mirror. The preset column is vertical, so it has no arrow keys.

items: The trigger is a native `<button>` showing the applied range or the `placeholder`. The popover is a `role="dialog"` named by `aria-label`, then the placeholder, then "Choose date range". `required`, `invalid`, `id` and `aria-describedby` work as on `DatePicker`, including the values a surrounding `Field` supplies.
The presets are buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that matches the draft range has `aria-pressed="true"`.
The footer text (the draft range, or "Select a start date") is a polite live region, so each click on a day is announced there.
A given name (`aria-label`, a `FieldLabel`) replaces the button text as the accessible name, so the applied range is not part of it. The clear button is named "Clear date".

motion.text: The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the net removes the movement. Preset and day hovers are short transitions that end in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The trigger renders on the server and the popover is portalled, so it appears after mount. A trigger with a range is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the runtime's default locale and time zone unless you pass `locale` or `formatRange`, so server and browser text can differ.

gotchas: Nothing is committed until Apply: clicking days, presets or closing with Escape or an outside click leaves `value` alone, and the next open starts from the committed value. `clearable` clears at once, with no Apply.
Apply is disabled until a start day is picked, and a range with only a start is applied as a one day range (`to` equals `from`).

`presets` replaces the defaults (`defaultDateRangePresets`: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month); `presets={[]}` hides the sidebar. Each `getRange` runs when a preset is chosen and when the popover renders, so relative ranges stay current. `numberOfMonths` defaults to 2.

`locale` formats the trigger and footer text and sets the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday; its aria labels stay English. With `name`, two hidden inputs post `name[from]` and `name[to]` as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

DateTimePicker.use: An input-like button that opens a calendar plus a time field, to pick a local day and time together. The value is wall-clock time in the user's zone, like `datetime-local`, as a `Date` or a `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"` string.

head: Key
Action
rows: Trigger, clear button, then (open) the presets, the calendar, the hour, minute and day period segments and Done
On the trigger: open; on a preset: choose it and close; on a day: pick it; on Done: close
Arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End
In the calendar: move the focused day (see Calendar)
In a time segment: step, type or clear it (see TimePicker)
Close the popover; focus returns to the trigger

keyboard.text: The trigger is a plain button, so ArrowDown does not open it. In RTL the calendar's Left and Right arrows swap; the time segments stay in a left to right group with fixed Left and Right.

items: The trigger is a native `<button>` showing the formatted date and time, or the `placeholder`. The popover is a `role="dialog"` named by `aria-label`, then the placeholder, then "Choose date and time". `required`, `invalid`, `id` and `aria-describedby` work as on `DatePicker`.

The time field is a group named by the visible "Time" text (`timeLabel`) with spinbutton segments for hour, minute and, with `granularity="second"`, seconds, plus an AM/PM segment on a 12-hour clock. The presets are plain buttons in a group named "Presets".
A given name (`aria-label`, a `FieldLabel`) replaces the button text as the accessible name, so the chosen moment is not part of it. The clear button is named "Clear date".

motion.text: The popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in`; the net removes the movement and ends transitions in 1 ms. The time field has no motion of its own.

ssr.text: The trigger renders on the server and the popover is portalled, so it appears after mount. The trigger text is formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the runtime's default locale and time zone unless you pass `locale`, `formatOptions` or `formatDateTime`, so server and browser can print different text and trigger a hydration warning. The portalled layer does not inherit a subtree `dir` or `data-style`; set them on `<html>`.

gotchas: Changes apply at once: picking a day, or stepping the time, calls `onValueChange(date, { localValue })` and the popover stays open until Done, Escape or an outside click. Picking a preset sets the value and closes. Clicking the selected day does not unselect it.
A day picked before any time is set uses the time typed so far, else `defaultTime` (`"00:00"`). A time typed before a day exists is held until a day is picked.
`min` and `max` disable days outside them, clamp the result, and limit the time on the boundary day; strings without a zone are read as local time.

With `name` a hidden input posts `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` (with `:ss` for seconds, empty when none). `locale` formats the trigger, sets the time field's clock and segment order, and sets the calendar's month and weekday names, digits and first weekday (its aria labels stay English).

Dialog.use: A modal that interrupts the page for one focused task. Centred on screens from `sm` up, a bottom sheet below. `AlertDialog` and `ConfirmDialog` are the variants for confirmations that must be answered.
instead: a side or edge panel that keeps the page context
a touch-first bottom sheet you drag
a small floating panel that does not block the page
ask for a confirm or a prompt from code

head: Key
Action
rows: Cycle focus inside the dialog (it is trapped while open)
Close the dialog (`AlertDialog` closes on Escape too, but not on an outside click)
Activate the focused button, including the close button

keyboard.text: Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to whatever had it before, even when the dialog was opened without a `DialogTrigger` (a hotkey, a menu item, controlled `open`). There are no arrow-key or direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing.

screenReaders.text: Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` (`alertdialog` for `AlertDialog`), `aria-labelledby` from `DialogTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `DialogDescription`, and hides the rest of the page from assistive technology while it is open. Always render a `DialogTitle` (it may be visually hidden); `ConfirmDialog` requires `title` for that reason. The built-in close button is labelled "Close". The mobile grabber bar is `aria-hidden` decoration.

motion.text: The panel fades and zooms in (from the bottom edge on mobile) with the `animate-in` utilities; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide and keeps the fade.

ssr.text: A closed dialog renders only its trigger on both server and client, so there is nothing to mismatch. The content is portalled into `<body>` after mount: a dialog that is `open` on first render appears after hydration, not in the server HTML. The portalled layer does not sit inside a subtree `data-style` or `dir`: put them on `<html>`.

gotchas: `AlertDialog` ignores outside clicks (no dismiss by clicking the backdrop), `Dialog` does not: use `AlertDialog` when the user must choose.
`ConfirmDialog onConfirm` may return a promise: the confirm button shows a spinner and closing is blocked until it settles, and throwing keeps the dialog open.
A dialog opened from a menu item that then unmounts cannot return focus to it (the opener is gone), and Radix's default applies; keep the opener mounted when focus matters.
`size` only sets the maximum width from `sm` up; below that every dialog is full width.

DialogProvider.use: Mount once near the root to ask for a confirmation, a line of text or a choice from code with promises. `useDialogs()` returns `confirm`, `prompt` and `choose`; `useConfirm()` is `confirm` alone. One dialog shows at a time and the rest queue.
instead: a confirmation you render in place with a `trigger` or controlled `open`
a blocking message with your own buttons

head: Key
Action
rows: Cycle focus inside the dialog (trapped while open)
In `prompt`: submit the field (the form validates, then resolves the text)
In `choose`: move between the options (the radio group; Enter does not pick, Tab on to Confirm)

keyboard.text: `confirm` opens with focus on Cancel, so a stray Enter does not confirm; `prompt` focuses and selects the field; focus returns to whatever had it when the first dialog of a run opened, once the queue is empty. The radio group reads the document or `DirectionProvider` direction, so its left and right arrows follow reading direction in RTL.

screenReaders.text: `confirm` is a Radix `alertdialog` named by its title (default "Are you sure?") and described by `description`; `prompt` and `choose` are `dialog`s named by `title` (a `prompt` without one uses a string `label`, else "Enter a value"; `choose` falls back to "Choose an option"). The `prompt` field is named by `label`, or by the title through `aria-label` when there is no `label`; a validation message sits in `FieldError`, sets `aria-invalid` and is linked as the field's description, and focus returns to the field. `choose` is a labelled radio group. The rest is `ConfirmDialog` and `Dialog` behaviour (the page is hidden from assistive technology while open).

motion.text: The dialogs are the standard ones: a short fade and zoom (a slide from the bottom on small screens), and the reduced-motion net removes the movement and keeps the fade. The pending spinner on the confirm button keeps turning.

ssr.text: The provider renders only its children on the server: no dialog exists until `confirm`, `prompt` or `choose` is called, which happens in handlers or effects on the client. The dialogs themselves are portalled after mount.

gotchas: `useDialogs` and `useConfirm` throw outside a `DialogProvider`. Unmounting the provider resolves every open and queued dialog as cancelled (`false` or `null`), so no `await` hangs.

`confirm`'s `onConfirm` may be async: the button shows a spinner and the dialog cannot be dismissed meanwhile. If it throws, the dialog stays open and the error is swallowed, so show your own message from the `catch`.

`prompt` trims and requires a value by default (`trim` and `required` default to true; `required: false` can resolve `""`). `validate` keeps the dialog open only when it returns a non-empty string (the message); returning `false` accepts the value.

`choose` resolves the picked option's own `value` (any type) and starts on `defaultValue`, else the first enabled option; disabled options cannot be picked. Cancel resolves `null` for `prompt` and `choose`, so test for `null` before using the answer.

DirectionProvider.use: Tells Sutra and its Radix primitives which way text runs. Mount one at the app root to follow `<html dir>` live, or give it `dir` to force a subtree (a chart that stays `ltr` inside an RTL page). Read the value with `useDirection()`.
instead: read the direction in your own component
pass the direction into a wrapped Radix root

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction of its own. It decides which way horizontal arrow keys go in what sits below it: Radix primitives (Tabs, sub-menus, radio groups, a horizontal Accordion) and Sutra components such as `TabDropdown` swap ArrowLeft and ArrowRight in RTL, while vertical lists do not.

screenReaders.text: No role, name or state. With `dir` it renders one `<div dir="rtl">` (or `ltr`) with `display: contents`, so the text direction is exposed to the browser and assistive technology without adding a box. Extra HTML attributes pass through to that element, so set `lang` on it when the subtree is in another language. Without `dir` it renders nothing.

motion.text: Static: it renders no motion.

ssr.text: With `dir` the markup is the same on the server and the client: the `display: contents` element carries `dir`, and every `useDirection()` inside it reads that value. Without `dir`, `useDirection()` returns `ltr` on the server and the real `<html dir>` value after hydration, so in an RTL document the server HTML of wrappers that write a `dir` attribute (Tabs, Accordion, ScrollArea, RadioGroup) says `ltr` until hydration.

slots: `direction-provider`: the `display: contents` element, only when `dir` is set
gotchas: Without `dir` it renders no element (children only) and follows `<html dir>` live, so it does not set `<html dir>` or `lang` for you: do that on the document.

With `dir` a `className` that needs a box (padding, background, border) has no effect, because the element is `display: contents`; put those on a child. A nested provider wins over an outer one, which is how a subtree forces `ltr` inside an RTL page.

A forced `dir` reaches the subtree only. Dialogs, sheets, drawers, popovers, tooltips and hover cards are portalled into `<body>` outside that element, so their `rtl:` styles follow `<html dir>`; menus carry their own `dir` attribute from the provider.
`dir` takes `"ltr"` or `"rtl"` only (no `"auto"`).

DonutChart.use: A ring split into segments for the parts of a whole, with the total (or a value you choose) in the centre, a legend that hides and shows segments, and a tooltip with name, value and share.
instead: the same parts as one horizontal bar
only the legend rows, no ring
compare many categories or values that are not parts of a whole
parts with a hierarchy or many tiles

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the ring; leaving it clears the active segment
Next visible segment, clockwise; wraps from the last to the first
Previous visible segment; wraps from the first to the last
Clears the active segment and its tooltip
On a legend entry: hide or show that segment. With Alt: show only that one, or restore all

keyboard.text: There is no Home or End. The ring is a `dir="ltr"` island, so the arrows never swap in RTL. The legend is outside it and follows the page direction, so `legend="right"` puts it at the inline end (visually left in RTL).

items: The ring is a focusable `role="img"` named by `label`, by default "Donut chart: alice 40, bob 35" listing every segment, hidden ones included. The SVG and the centre text are not read separately.
A visually hidden table follows it: columns are the `index` key, the `valueKey` and "Share"; a hidden segment shows "hidden" as its share. Shares are of the visible total.
Stepping with the keyboard writes "alice: 40 (40%)" into a polite live region. Hovering shows the tooltip but does not announce.

The chip legend is a `group` named "Toggle series" of `aria-pressed` buttons; with `legendValues` or `iconFor` it becomes a `list` named "Legend" whose rows are the same toggle buttons. With `loading`, the root has `aria-busy` and one hidden "Loading donut chart…".

motion.text: Segments carry `motion-safe:transition-all duration-500` (`animate`, default true), which eases the hover dimming and colour changes; the arc shape is a `d` attribute, so it changes at once when data or the hidden set changes, and under `prefers-reduced-motion` nothing eases. The loading ring pulses with `animate-pulse` and carries `motion-reduce:animate-none`. There is no entrance animation on mount.

ssr.text: The ring is drawn from `size` alone, so the server HTML already contains the segments, centre text and legend; nothing waits for mount. The one thing that can differ is number text: values and shares go through `Intl` with the runtime default locale, so pass `valueFormatter` when the server and the browser locale differ.

slots: `chart-segment`: one ring segment (hidden segments are not rendered)
gotchas: Values below 0 or that are not finite numbers count as 0. When the visible total is 0 the ring is one muted track and the centre shows 0.
The centre defaults to the formatted total of visible segments, so it changes when you hide one; `centerValue={null}` removes it, `centerLabel` alone still shows.
Segment keys are the `index` text; a repeated name gets `#1`, `#2` suffixes, which is what `hiddenSeries` and `onHiddenSeriesChange` contain for the repeats.

`legend={false}` removes the only toggle control (segments then cannot be hidden by keyboard or pointer unless you control `hiddenSeries`). `legendInteractive={false}` keeps the legend as a plain list.

Drawer.use: A touch-first bottom sheet with a grabber, drag-to-dismiss and optional snap points (`snapPoints` as fractions of the viewport height). Modal, with scroll lock and focus return. Header, title, body and footer are the Sheet parts with drawer spacing.
instead: a panel from any edge that is not dragged
a centred modal for one decision or task
a small floating panel that does not block the page

head: Key
Action
rows: Cycle focus inside the drawer (trapped while it is modal)
On the handle button (only with two or more `snapPoints`): go to the next snap point and wrap to the smallest
Activate the focused button, including `DrawerClose` and the close button from `showClose`

keyboard.text: Dragging is pointer-only. Without snap points the handle is a decorative `aria-hidden` bar, so keyboard users close with Escape or a `DrawerClose` button. There are no direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing. Focus returns to the `DrawerTrigger` on close (Radix), and for a drawer opened without a trigger (a hotkey, controlled `open`) to the element that had focus when it opened, as `SheetContent` does; a `preventDefault()` in your `onCloseAutoFocus` still wins.

screenReaders.text: Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` with `aria-labelledby` from `DrawerTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `DrawerDescription`, and hides the rest of the page while it is open. Always render a `DrawerTitle` (it may be visually hidden). The handle button with snap points is named "Expand sheet" or "Collapse sheet" depending on the current snap point; the grabber bar itself is `aria-hidden`. The close button from `showClose` is labelled "Close".

motion.text: The sheet slides up from the bottom with `animate-in` and the drag release settles with a 320 ms translate transition. The reduced-motion net removes the slide, keeps the fade and ends the settle transition in 1 ms. Dragging follows the pointer and is not affected.

ssr.text: Only the trigger renders on the server. The sheet is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a drawer that is `open` on first render appears after hydration. The viewport height used for snap points is read only inside the portalled content.

slots: `drawer-content`: the sheet panel (`data-dragging` while dragged, `data-snap` with snap points)
`drawer-handle`: the grabber, a button with two or more snap points, else a decorative bar
`drawer-header`: the pinned header; it is draggable
gotchas: A release past 80 px of drag, or a fast flick down (above 500 px/s), dismisses the drawer; with snap points a flick moves one snap point and only the smallest one dismisses. A drag never starts on text fields, sliders, `[data-drawer-no-drag]` elements, or inside a scroll area that is scrolled down.
`dismissible={false}` disables Escape, scrim clicks and drag-to-dismiss, but `DrawerClose` and a controlled `open` still close it. It stays draggable between snap points if there are two or more.

`snapPoints` are clamped to 0.05 through 1 and sorted. The panel is as tall as the largest one, and an uncontrolled drawer reopens at `defaultSnapPoint` or the smallest. `snapPoint` makes it controlled with `onSnapPointChange`.
Drawer parts must be inside `<Drawer>` (they throw otherwise). `showHandle` is on and `showClose` off by default, and the panel is at most `max-w-2xl`, centred, on wide screens.
Drawer.example:
import { Button, Drawer, DrawerBody, DrawerClose, DrawerContent, DrawerDescription } from "@sutra/ui"; import { DrawerFooter, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerTrigger } from "@sutra/ui"; export function Example() { return ( Share this trip Anyone with the link can view your itinerary.

Lisbon, 4 to 9 May. Four travellers, two rooms.

 ); }

DropdownMenu.use: A menu of actions that opens from a trigger button. Rows take an `icon`, `description`, display-only `shortcut` and `tone="destructive"`, plus checkbox and radio rows and nested sub-menus.
instead: the menu chooses a value for a form field
the menu opens from a right-click on an area
a primary action with a menu of alternatives
rich content or a form rather than a list of actions

head: Key
Action
rows: On the trigger: Enter and Space toggle the menu, ArrowDown opens it (a left click opens it too)
Move the highlighted row; focus stops at the ends unless you pass `loop` to `DropdownMenuContent`
Highlight the first or last row
Typeahead: highlights the next row whose text starts with it
Activate the highlighted row; a checkbox or radio row toggles or picks, and the menu closes
On a sub-menu trigger: open it (Enter and Space do too)
Inside a sub-menu: close it and return to its trigger
Does nothing while the menu is open (Radix blocks it)

keyboard.text: In RTL the sub-menu keys swap: ArrowLeft opens a sub-menu and ArrowRight closes it, and the sub-menu opens to the left. `DropdownMenu` passes the document or `DirectionProvider` direction to Radix (an explicit `dir` prop wins). Focus returns to the trigger when the menu closes.

screenReaders.text: The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`. The panel is `role="menu"` labelled by the trigger; rows are `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` (with `aria-checked`), groups are `role="group"` and the separator is `separator`. `DropdownMenuLabel` is a plain text div that is not linked to its group, so give `DropdownMenuGroup` an `aria-label` to name it. A disabled row gets `aria-disabled`. Icons and the sub-menu chevron are decoration (the chevron is `aria-hidden`; an `icon` you pass is not hidden for you). The `shortcut` text is read as part of the row name. An icon-only trigger needs `aria-label`.

motion.text: The panel fades and zooms in from the trigger with the `animate-in` utilities and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. Row highlight changes are instant by design.

ssr.text: A closed menu renders only its trigger on both server and client, so nothing can mismatch. The panel is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a menu with `defaultOpen` or `open` on first render appears after hydration. The panel carries its own `dir` (the document or `DirectionProvider` direction), but it is portalled outside a subtree `data-style`: set that on `<html>`.

gotchas: `shortcut` is only a label: it does not bind any key. Wire the real shortcut yourself.
`DropdownMenuItem` closes the menu on select; call `event.preventDefault()` in `onSelect` to keep it open (use `onSelect`, not `onClick`, for keyboard and pointer alike).

`tone="destructive"` replaces the deprecated `variant="destructive"` (`tone` wins when both are set). With `asChild` the row styling applies but `icon`, `description` and `shortcut` are ignored: you render the content.
`DropdownMenuContent` already wraps itself in a portal (`sideOffset` 6, `align="start"`), so `DropdownMenuPortal` is only for custom compositions. Radix `loop` defaults to off.

Dropzone.use: A drag-and-drop area that also opens the file picker on click, Enter or Space. It checks type, size and count and calls `onDrop(accepted, rejections)`; with `directory` it takes whole folders. It only collects files: you upload them.
instead: a compound uploader that owns the file list and validation (put FileUploadDropzone in it)
a button that opens the picker, with no drop area

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the zone (one tab stop; a `disabled` zone is skipped)
Open the file picker (a folder picker with `directory`)

keyboard.text: Only a key pressed on the zone itself counts: keys from a `children` control inside it do not open the picker. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. Dragging has no keyboard path; the picker is the keyboard way to add files.

items: The zone is a `div role="button"` named by its visible prompt ("Click to upload or drag and drop") or by `aria-label` if you pass one. The hint (for example "Images, PDF · up to 10 MB") is added to `aria-describedby` next to any `aria-describedby` you pass. `disabled` sets `aria-disabled`.
The real `<input type="file">` is a sibling that is `aria-hidden`, off the tab order and visually hidden, so it is never a second control; `name` and `inputRef` go to it.
While a dropped folder is being read the zone has `aria-busy`. During a drag the prompt text is swapped for "Drop to upload" or "Some files aren't supported"; that swap is not a live region.
Rejections are reported only through `onDrop`: nothing is announced for you, so show the messages (each rejection carries `errors[].message`) in your own status or list.
Where `directory` cannot work, the reason ("This browser can't choose folders. Choose files instead.") is shown and added to the description.

motion.text: The icon lifts and the border, background and ring change with transitions on drag, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing loops.

ssr.text: Without `directory` the zone renders the same on both sides. With `directory` the server (and the hydration pass) assumes folders are unsupported, so the HTML says "Click to upload" and shows the "can't choose folders" reason; after hydration a supporting browser switches to "Click to choose a folder" and drops the reason.

gotchas: `onDrop` is `(accepted, rejections)` and runs for every drop or pick, also when everything was rejected or `accepted` is empty. A rejection is `{ file, errors: [{ code, message }] }` with codes `file-invalid-type`, `file-too-large` and `too-many-files`. It does not run while `disabled`.

The red drag state only reflects what the browser reveals mid-drag: MIME types (and `multiple={false}` with several files). Extension rules such as `accept=".pdf"` and `maxSize` are checked at drop. `multiple={false}` keeps the first file and rejects the rest.

`currentCount` counts files you already hold against `maxFiles`. Without `name` the picker input is cleared after each pick, so the same file can be chosen again. With `name` the accepted files stay on the input through `DataTransfer` (picks and drops; a rejected pick is not kept), so a native form post sends them: the earlier ones are kept while `currentCount` is above 0 and the input is emptied when it returns to 0. Where `input.files` cannot be set it is cleared as before.

`directory` walks dropped folders and sets each file's `relativePath` (read it with `getFileRelativePath`); every file is validated on its own and counts toward `maxFiles`. `compact` is a deprecated alias of `density="compact"`. The helpers `validateFiles`, `isFileAccepted` and `describeFileConstraints` are exported for your own checks.

EmojiReaction.use: A reaction pill (emoji and count, pressed when you reacted), a bar of them with an add-reaction picker, and the standalone searchable emoji picker. In the paper style every emoji reads as ink on paper: the solid hand-drawn art of the built-in set (or its tint or outline variant), which moves on hover and pops and plays when a reaction is added.
instead: draw a hand-drawn emoji anywhere, in any style
show an emoji you render yourself with the same ink treatment
a categorical label with no emoji

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between the reaction pills and the add-reaction button; in the picker, through the search field, the category tabs and the grid
Toggles a pill, opens the add-reaction popover, picks the focused emoji
In the picker grid, move by one cell (Left and Right follow the reading direction, so they swap in RTL) or one row (Up and Down)
Closes the add-reaction popover and returns focus to its button

keyboard.text: Type in the search field to filter by name; the grid then shows only the results.

items: A pill is a toggle button (`aria-pressed`) named like "thumbs reaction, 3 people, including you". The emoji and the number inside are `aria-hidden`, so the name is read once.
Picker cells are buttons named by their first two keywords ("grinning face"); the preview row and the empty-result icon are decorative.

The ink version does not change any name or role. The emoji character stays in the DOM inside `data-part="glyph"` (visually hidden when the drawing shows), so copy and paste, find in page and text-based tests still see it.

motion.text: A new reaction pops once (`animate-pop`), which the reduced-motion net shortens to 1 ms. With the ink drawings, a pill's emoji also plays its motion once on hover and focus and when the reaction is added (also from the picker), and a picker cell plays on hover and focus; reduced motion keeps the still drawing (`inkMotion={false}` turns it off everywhere). Switching to ink is not animated. The picker hover scale is a transform transition and also ends under reduced motion.

ssr.text: The markup is the same on the server and the client. The paper style needs a one-ink filter for glyphs without art: the first glyph that mounts adds a hidden `svg#sutra-emoji-ink` to `<body>` in an effect, so before hydration a paper page shows an unfiltered colour glyph for a moment.

gotchas: Every emoji sits in `span[data-slot="emoji"]` (see `EmojiGlyph`) with `data-part="glyph"` and, for emoji with art, `data-part="ink"`: style those, not the text. Ink follows the style: in `[data-style="paper"]` everything is ink, elsewhere colour. `ink` on the pill, the bar or the picker forces it (`true`) or keeps colour in the paper style (`false`), the same as `FileFormatIcon mono`.

`inkVariant` picks the drawing the ink shows on the pill, the bar and the picker: `solid` (the default, filled with the features cut out), `tint` (solid plus a tint for the secondary parts) or `outline` (monoline). `inkMotion` (default on) moves it; `EmojiReaction playKey` pops and plays from outside, which the bar uses for a reaction added from the picker. An emoji with hand-drawn art (`hasInkEmoji`: every emoji of the built-in picker set) shows the drawing in the ink; any emoji outside the set (a dinosaur, a flag) shows the colour glyph filtered to one ink, so fine detail goes soft at small sizes. Ink on a black background is inverted to light, so set `data-style` on `<html>` for portaled popovers.

The glyph is wrapped in a `span` (`inline-block`, `leading-none`, the size class), so a test that looked for the emoji as a bare text node of the button should look in the glyph part. Text-only searches such as `getByText("👍")` still work.
Reaction state is controlled with `reacted` or uncontrolled with `defaultReacted`; the bar owns the counts, and a count that falls to 0 removes the pill.

EmptyState.use: The placeholder for an empty list, search result or first-run screen: an icon or illustration, a title, a description and actions. `variant="welcome"` is the large greeting at the start of a chat or workspace.
instead: a quiet one-line message inside a screen that is working or empty
a notice about something that needs attention
the welcome variant preconfigured for chat

keyboard.text: Not focusable itself: no keyboard interaction. The `actions` you pass (buttons, links) are ordinary tab stops.

items: The root is a `<section>` labelled by the title (`aria-labelledby`), so with a title it is a named `region` landmark. Without a title (only possible in practice for `welcome`) it has no name and is not a landmark.
The title is a real heading: `h3` by default and `h2` for `variant="welcome"`. The level is not configurable, so check it fits your outline.

Built-in illustrations (`search`, `inbox`, `files`, `error`, `success`, `cloud`) are `aria-hidden`, and so is the default inbox icon. A custom `illustration` node or `icon` is used as you pass it: hide decoration with `aria-hidden`.

motion.text: The block rises in with `animate-fade-up`, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` removes.

ssr.text: Plain markup with a `useId` for the heading, so server and client output match. The entrance animation starts when the page paints.

slots: `empty-state`: the root `section`, with `data-variant` set to `default`, `dashed` or `welcome`
gotchas: `icon` is ignored when `illustration` is set. In the `default` and `dashed` variants an empty `icon` falls back to an inbox glyph; in `welcome` there is no default icon and a given one sits in a small card tile.
`illustration` takes one of the six variant names or any node: an unknown string is rendered as text, not looked up.
`actions` sit in a wrapping row under the text; `children` follow them (inside a full-width box in `welcome`).
`size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets spacing and type scale for the non-welcome variants only; `welcome` has its own fixed layout.

Favicon.use: The small icon of a website: an explicit `src`, an icon your `FaviconProvider` resolves for the domain, or a local letter tile. By default it makes no network request.
instead: a letter tile for an app or tool you name yourself
a row that holds a logo, title and description

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: Always decorative: the `img` has `alt=""` and the letter tile is `aria-hidden`. The site name must be visible text next to it (a link label, a source title); a favicon alone tells a screen reader nothing.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: The same markup on server and client for the same props: the letter tile, or an `img` when a `src` or resolver gives a URL. The tile letter and colour are pure functions of `domain`. An image that fails to load switches to the tile through its `onError` handler, which runs in the browser.

gotchas: Without a `FaviconProvider` and without `src`, `Favicon` renders the local tile: no request leaves the page. `FaviconProvider resolve` opts in, and `googleFaviconResolver` sends every rendered domain to Google, so prefer your own resolver for private data. A resolver that returns `undefined` falls back to the tile.
`src` wins over the provider. A failed `img` (`onError`) falls back to the tile and tries again when the URL changes.
There is no default size: set it with `className` (`size-4`, `size-5`). `shape` is `circle` (default) or `square`.
The tile letter is the first letter or digit of `domain` as given, so pass a bare host: `"www.example.com"` gives W. `domainOf(url)` returns a clean host to pass in.

Field.use: Wires one form control to its label, description, hint and error: shared id, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `disabled` and `required`. Controls that call `useField` (Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Switch, the pickers and others) pick it up with no props.
instead: a standalone label with no shared state
group related fields under a legend
a set of radios has its own group label

keyboard.text: Not focusable: `Field` renders layout and text only, so there is no keyboard interaction. Tab goes to the control inside it, and clicking the `FieldLabel` focuses that control.

items: `FieldLabel` is a `<label htmlFor>` pointing at the field `id` (generated, or the `id` you pass to `Field`), and carries a label id that widgets which are not labelable elements use as `aria-labelledby` (Combobox, TimePicker). Its asterisk follows `required` but is `aria-hidden`.

The control gets `aria-describedby` listing the description, hint and error parts that are mounted, in that order, plus any ids you pass yourself; a part with a custom `id` is listed under that id. `invalid` becomes `aria-invalid` on the control.

`FieldError` is `role="alert"`, so it is announced when it appears, and renders nothing when it has no content. Pass `errors` (strings or `{ message }` objects from a form library) instead of children: one message is plain text, several become a list.
`Fieldset` is a native `<fieldset>` and `FieldLegend` a `<legend>`; a `disabled` fieldset disables the controls inside it natively.

motion.text: `FieldError` fades and slides in with `animate-in slide-in-from-top-1`; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and ends the rest in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The label, control and parts render on the server, but each description, hint and error registers itself in an effect, so the control's `aria-describedby` is missing from the server HTML and appears after hydration. The id comes from `useId`, so it matches on both sides.

slots: `field-content`: stacks label, description and error beside a control in a `horizontal` field
`fieldset`, `field-legend`: the native group and its title (`data-variant` is `legend` or `label`)
gotchas: Explicit props on the control win: `useField` takes the control's own `id`, `disabled`, `required` and `invalid` (a true `aria-invalid` also counts) before the field's, and joins `aria-describedby` instead of replacing it.
Showing a `FieldError` does not mark the control invalid: set `invalid` on `Field` (or on the control) for `aria-invalid` and the red border.
`Field` gives one `id` to one control. For a group of controls (radios, checkboxes) use `Fieldset` with `FieldLegend`, or the group's own `label`.
Read the state yourself with `useFieldContext()` (it returns `null` outside a `Field`), or wire a custom control with `useField`.

FileUpload.use: A compound file uploader. `FileUpload` owns the file list, the type, size and count checks and a hidden input; `FileUploadDropzone` and `FileUploadTrigger` (files or a folder) add files, `FileUploadList` and `FileUploadItem` show them with progress, status and remove. It manages the list: you do the upload.
instead: just a drop area with no list or state
one attachment tile in a conversation

head: Key
Action
rows: The dropzone, each trigger and each row's remove button are tab stops
On the dropzone or a trigger: open the file (or folder) picker. On a remove button: remove the file

keyboard.text: Dragging has no keyboard form, so the dropzone and the triggers are the keyboard route. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

items: `FileUploadDropzone` is a `role="button"` named by its text ("Click to upload or drag and drop") and described by its hint (types, size and count limits); it has `aria-disabled` when disabled and `aria-busy` while a dropped folder is read. The real file input is a hidden sibling (`aria-hidden`, not focusable).
Rejected files show in a `role="alert"` list, one message per file (the first problem only, such as "n.txt isn't a supported file type."), until the next add.

The list is a `ul` named "Files". Each row shows the name (the folder path for folder files) and size, a "Complete" or error text with an icon labelled "Uploaded" or "Failed", and a `progressbar` named "Uploading <name>" (indeterminate when `progress` is undefined). The remove button is "Remove <name>".
Where the browser cannot pick folders, `FileUploadTrigger directory` is `aria-disabled` and described by "This browser can't choose folders. Choose files instead."

motion.text: Drag feedback (border, tint, icon lift) and the progress fill use transitions that the global net ends in 1 ms. The tick pops with `animate-pop` when a file finishes, which the net stops.

ssr.text: Without `directory` the markup is the same on both sides. The folder trigger and folder dropzone ask the browser for `webkitdirectory` support with `useSyncExternalStore`: the server and hydration render the "unsupported" state, and the real answer appears after hydration.

gotchas: Nothing is uploaded for you. `onFilesAdded` gives the new `UploadFile`s (`status: "idle"`): start your request there and feed `progress` and `status` back through controlled `files` (or `onFilesChange`). `status` also takes `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed` and `canceled`.

`accept`, `maxSize` (bytes) and `maxFiles` (in total, counting files already listed) are checked on every add; rejections go to `onFilesRejected` and the alert. `multiple={false}` makes each new file replace the previous one.

With `name` the hidden input carries the whole file list (picked, dropped and `defaultFiles`; removing a file removes it) through `DataTransfer`, so a native form post sends the files. Without `name`, or in a browser that cannot set `input.files`, the input is emptied after each pick: read the files from the list or `onFilesAdded`. Picking a file that is already on the input again may fire no change event.
`FileUploadList` renders nothing for an empty list; `FileUploadItem` outside a `FileUpload` needs its own `onRemove`. Read the state anywhere inside with the `useFileUpload` hook.

FilterBar.use: The toolbar above a list or table: a search field, dashed "+ Filter" chips that open a multi-select checklist, a row of removable tokens for the applied filters, and a "Clear all" button. The parts hold no shared state, so you wire them to your own filter state.
instead: pick one or more values for a form field
one value from a short list
a global search and command palette
a field-shaped button that opens it

head: Key
Action
rows: Each control is its own tab stop: the search field, its clear button, each chip, each token's remove button, "Clear all"
In the search field with text: clears it (not during IME composition). In an open chip popover: closes it
On a chip: opens the checklist. On an option: toggles it (the list stays open)
In the chip's search input: moves to the first option. In the list: next option, wrapping to the first
Previous option, wrapping to the last

keyboard.text: The chip checklist opens with the first option focused, or the search input when `searchable` (default above 7 options). The checklist is vertical, so RTL changes nothing; icons and padding use logical sides.

items: `FilterBar` is `role="toolbar"` with no label of its own: pass `aria-label`. It does not implement roving arrow keys, so it is a plain row of tab stops.

A chip is a button named by its label plus the selected values as text ("Status Active Paused", or "Status 3 selected" past `maxDisplay`). It opens a popover with a `listbox` named by the label and `aria-multiselectable`; each option has `aria-selected`; the check box is `aria-hidden`. The search input is named "Search <label>". "No results" is plain text, not a live region.
`FilterBarSearch` is an `<input type="search">` (role `searchbox`) with a "Clear search" button once it has text; give it an `aria-label`, since the placeholder ("Search…") is its only other name.
`FilterBarActive` is a `group` named "Active filters"; each token reads "Status: Active" followed by its remove button.

motion.text: The chip popover fades and zooms in with `animate-in` and the check mark scales in over 150 ms; new tokens fade in. The global net removes the movement and ends the transitions within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup from props (`useId` for the list id). The chip popover is portalled and closed on first render, so nothing is missing on either side.

gotchas: All filter state is yours: `FilterBarChip` takes `value` (string array) with `onValueChange`, `FilterBarSearch` takes `value` with `onValueChange`. Chips do not create tokens: map your state to `FilterBarActive filters`, or render `FilterBarToken`s yourself.

Every token built from `filters` has the remove button name "Remove filter" unless you name them: `removeLabel` on `FilterBarActive` (a string, or a function of the filter such as `(f) => "Remove " + f.id`) or `removeLabel` on a single filter (which wins); `FilterBarToken` children take `removeLabel` too. Setting `onRemove` is what shows the button.

Chip options are strings or `{ value, label, icon, count, textValue }`. Search and the summary use `textValue`, else the label when it is a string or number, else the raw `value`: set `textValue` when `label` is a node.
`FilterPill` is a deprecated alias of `FilterBarChip`. Chip `align` sets the popover alignment (default `start`); `disabled` on the chip prevents opening.

FloatingActionButton.use: One pinned primary action for a screen, round or rounded-square, icon-only or extended with a label. Pass `actions` and it becomes a speed dial that fans a menu of small actions out of the button.
instead: an ordinary action in the page flow
a menu of actions from an ordinary trigger
the action needs a form or a decision

head: Key
Action
rows: On the button: runs `onClick`, and toggles the dial when it has `actions`
With `actions`, on a bottom position: opens the dial and focuses the action nearest the button (already open: focuses it)
In the open dial: the key that points away from the button moves to the next action, the other moves back; both wrap and skip disabled actions
Focus the first (nearest) or last action
On an action: runs its `onClick`, then closes the dial. A link action (`href`) follows on Enter only
While the dial is open: closes it and returns focus to the button, wherever focus is
Moves through the open actions one by one (they are not roving) and does not close the dial

keyboard.text: The dial is vertical, so no arrow key swaps in RTL. The `position` names are physical (`bottom-right` stays at the right edge in RTL).

items: Without `actions` it is a plain `<button type="button">` named by `label` (`aria-label`); with `extended`, the visible `label` is the name and `aria-label` is dropped. The icon is `aria-hidden`.

With `actions` the button gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the list is a `role="menu"` named by `label`, with `menuitem` buttons (links when an action has `href`) wrapped in `role="none"` items.
A closed dial is `inert`, so its actions are neither focusable nor in the accessibility tree. A disabled action is `disabled` (a link gets `aria-disabled`, no `href` and `tabindex="-1"`).
On `*-center` positions the action labels are visually hidden but still read; elsewhere each label shows beside its round icon.

motion.text: The fan-out (each item fades, scales and slides with a 30 ms stagger), the 45 degree turn of the default plus icon, the hover lift and the press scale are all transitions. The reduced-motion net ends them in 1 ms and removes the delays, so the dial opens at once and the lift and press are instant.

ssr.text: No browser API at render: the document listeners attach in an effect and `useId` names the menu. A `defaultOpen` or `open` dial is already open in the server HTML.

slots: `fab`: the positioned wrapper that holds the dial and the button (`containerClassName` styles it; `className` styles the button)
gotchas: `strategy` defaults to `fixed`, pinned to the viewport corner with `z-50`. In a card, a demo or any container use `absolute` (inside a `relative` parent) or `static`, which ignores `position` offsets.
`label` is required and is not shown unless `extended`; there is no tooltip. Default icon is a plus; it turns only when you pass `actions` and no `icon`.
Your `onClick` runs first, and `preventDefault()` in it stops the toggle. `open` and the actions do nothing without a non-empty `actions` array.

Running an action closes the dial and, when focus is still on the action (its handler did not move it), puts focus back on the button, as Escape does; clicking elsewhere closes it and leaves focus where you clicked.

Frame.use: A titled tray around a panel of rows: a header with title, description and action, a panel that holds the rows, and a footer. Four looks, with loading and empty states in the panel.
instead: the row itself (put `Item`s in the panel)

keyboard.text: Not focusable itself: no keyboard interaction. The action in `FrameAction` and the rows in the panel are ordinary tab stops.

items: `FrameTitle` renders an `h3` by default; `as` picks `h2` to `h6`, `p` or `div`, so set it to fit your heading outline.
`FramePanel` is a `role="list"` and needs an `aria-label`. `Item` rows inside it become list items by themselves. Any other row must carry `role="listitem"` itself, or the list has no valid children.
`loading` shows `aria-busy` with sr-only "Loading…" and `aria-hidden` placeholder rows (an icon box and two lines). `emptyState` is wrapped in a `listitem`.
`Frame`, `FrameHeader` and `FrameFooter` add no roles, so the header is not linked to the panel: label the panel yourself.

motion.text: Static: no animation of its own. The loading placeholders are `Skeleton`s and follow the net in `sutra.css`.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The variant styles come from CSS (`group-data-[variant=...]`), so they apply on the first paint.

slots: `frame-header`: title, description and action; wraps on narrow widths
`frame-description`: a line under or beside the title
`frame-action`: a control at the end of the header
`frame-panel`: the raised surface that holds the rows
gotchas: `variant` is `default` (a tray with a raised panel, corners kept concentric), `band` (one card with tinted header and footer bands), `inset` (a soft tray with a roomy, borderless panel) or `plain` (no tray). The header, footer and panel read the variant from the root, so they must sit inside `Frame`.
`FramePanel` draws hairlines between rows by default; pass `divided={false}` for none.
`emptyState` shows only when the panel has no children and `loading` is off. `loadingRows` defaults to 3.
`FrameDescription` is full width, so inside a wrapping header it falls onto its own line under the title and action.

Gauge.use: A radial arc showing one reading inside a range (temperature, load, score), coloured by thresholds, with the value in the middle. `RingMeter` is the compact ring for inline use, such as a context window.
instead: a level against a limit as a bar
a plan limit with a pace
history rather than the current value

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The reading is exposed to screen readers as a meter, with no controls.

items: The root is `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow` (clamped into `min` and `max`), `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. `aria-valuetext` is the formatted value plus `unit` ("62 °C"), "No data" for `value={null}`, "Loading" while `loading` has no value, or whatever you pass as `ariaValueText`.
The name is `label` (referenced with `aria-labelledby`, and kept as hidden text when `children` replaces the visible caption); without `label` it is "Gauge", so pass one when several are on a page.
`data-level` (`ok`, `warn`, `danger`) is a styling hook, not announced: the warn and danger colour is visual only, so put the state in `ariaValueText` when it matters.

`RingMeter` is a `role="meter"` span named by `label` (default "Usage"), always on a 0 to 100 scale, with value text like "92%". Its percentage is shown only from `showValueAbove` (50) upwards, but the value text is always there.

motion.text: The arc animates `stroke-dasharray` and colour over 500 ms with `motion-reduce:transition-none`, so under `prefers-reduced-motion` it jumps to the new value. The loading placeholder uses the `Skeleton` pulse, which the global net stops.

ssr.text: A static SVG computed from the props (arc path, `pathLength` dash), so the server and client markup match. The arc fills clockwise in both directions: nothing mirrors in RTL.

slots: `gauge-fill`: the coloured value arc (absent when empty or at 0)
`gauge-value`: the number and unit in the middle
gotchas: Thresholds are percentages of `min` to `max` and higher is worse (warn at 75, danger at 90). For readings where high is good, pass `thresholds={false}`, or use `colorStops`, which use absolute values, win over thresholds and leave `data-level` at `ok`.

Arc colour order: `colorStops`, then the warn and danger colours, then `tone`, then `accent`, then primary. `color` is a deprecated alias of `tone`, and `tone="neutral"` draws the arc in the foreground colour.
`value={null}` draws an empty track and "—". With `loading`, the placeholder replaces the number only when the value is null; with a value the gauge keeps showing it and just sets `aria-busy`.
The number in the middle is the unclamped `value` through `valueFormatter` (rounded to one decimal by default), while `aria-valuenow` and the arc are clamped to the range.

GlyphSpinner.use: A loading indicator made of a cycling text character (braille dots, arcs, a rotating line), for terminals, agent status lines and anywhere a monospace look fits. A preset of `Spinner` with `variant="glyph"`.
instead: a ring, dots, bars or pulse that scales with `size`
a placeholder in the shape of content that is loading

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: A `role="status"` span with visually hidden text, "Loading" unless `label` says otherwise. The glyph itself is `aria-hidden`, so screen readers do not hear each frame. `label=""` makes it decorative (`aria-hidden`, no role). Name what is loading when several are on the page.

motion.text: It reads `usePrefersReducedMotion` and holds its current frame (frame 0 on first render) instead of cycling. This is the component's own check, not a CSS rule.

ssr.text: Always renders frame 0 first: the preference hook reads `false` on the server and the interval starts after mount, so the server and client markup match.

gotchas: `frames` overrides `variant` when it is not empty; an empty array falls back to `variant`. `variant` is one of `dots` (default), `line`, `arc`, `circle`, `bounce`, `star` or `pulse`, the same sets as `glyphSpinnerFrames`.
`size` (`xs` to `xl`, as on `Spinner`) sets the font size; without it the glyph takes the font size and colour of its parent, so a `text-*` class on `className` or a wrapper also works.
`interval` is milliseconds per frame (default 80) and is clamped to at least 16; `paused` holds the current frame, as does a single-frame `frames` array.
The glyph sits in a `min-w-[1ch]` monospace box, so a custom frame set should use characters of similar width to avoid jitter.

Grid.use: A responsive 12-column page grid that is 4 columns on mobile, 8 on tablet and 12 on desktop. `GridItem` sets how many columns a child spans at each size.
instead: centre content and cap its width
a bordered surface to place in a cell

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: Plain `div`s with no role. The reading order is the DOM order, whatever the spans do visually, so keep the source order meaningful.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup; the column counts come from CSS breakpoints (`md`, `lg`), so there is no script and no mismatch.

gotchas: `GridItem span` counts columns of the 4-column mobile grid and defaults to `"full"`: an item with only `lg={4}` is full width on mobile and tablet too. Give `md` when the tablet layout should differ.
`span` above 4 on mobile makes implicit columns; use `md` (of 8) and `lg` (of 12) for larger spans.
`md` is typed 1 to 8 or `"full"` because the tablet grid has 8 columns (a larger value used to compile and do nothing); `span` and `lg` accept 1 to 12 and `"full"`.
`gap` is `sm`, `md` (default, wider from `md` up) or `lg`.

Heading.use: A heading on the display type scale. The element level (`as`) is independent of the look (`size`), so the outline and the design can differ.
instead: a small caps label above a heading
a section heading with eyebrow, description and actions

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: Renders the element named by `as` (`h1` to `h6`), and the default is `h2`, not `h1`. Pass `as="h1"` once per page; pick levels by document outline, never by size.
`asChild` renders your child element with the heading styles instead; the child then decides the semantics (a `div` child is not a heading unless it has `role="heading"` and `aria-level`).
The text is balanced (`text-balance`) for wrapping only, which has no effect on what is read.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The size steps change at CSS breakpoints, not in script.

gotchas: `size` runs from `display-3xl` down to `display-xs` and then `xl`, `lg`, `md`, `sm`; the default is `display-sm`. The large display steps shrink on small screens (`display-3xl` is `display-lg` on mobile).
`as` only takes `h1` to `h6`; use `asChild` for anything else, including a link inside the heading.
The weight is always semibold and the colour foreground; override with `className` (merged last).

HeatmapGrid.use: A grid of cells coloured by value, in square tiles or vertical fill bars (per-core CPU, per-GPU load, matrices), with a tooltip and keyboard navigation. `HeatmapLegend` is the "Less to More" key that the grid shows with `legend`.
instead: one cell per day over a year or month
values on an axis with exact heights

head: Key
Action
rows: One cell holds the tab stop (the last focused); Tab then leaves the grid
Previous or next cell in the row
The cell above or below; a missing cell is skipped, and at an edge nothing moves
First or last cell of the row
First or last cell of the grid

keyboard.text: The grid is a forced `dir="ltr"` island: columns run left to right and ArrowRight is always the next column, also in RTL.

items: A `grid` named by `label` (default "Heatmap") with `row`s and `gridcell`s. Each cell is named "Core 3: 15%": its label, a colon, then the formatted value, or "no data" for `null`.
The default cell label is "Cell 0" (index from 0), so pass `cellLabel` or a `label` per cell. Colour carries the level visually only; the value is in the name.
The tooltip appears on hover and focus and is `aria-hidden`; the legend is plain text with `aria-hidden` swatches. Cells also expose `data-level` (-1 no data, 0 empty, 1 to `steps`).

motion.text: Cell colour and the focus ring fade over 300 ms and bar fills grow over 500 ms with transitions, which the global net ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Everything is computed from `data` and the props, and the default value text uses `toFixed` rather than `Intl`, so server and client markup are the same. The tooltip only exists after hover or focus.

gotchas: The defaults assume percentages: `min` 0, `max` 100 and a `formatValue` that appends "%". For other units set `min`, `max` and `formatValue`.
`null` is "no data" (transparent, a dashed outline on squares); a value at or below `min` is the muted "empty" step, a different thing.

`scale` defaults to `primary` for squares and `thresholds` for `shape="bar"` (warn at 75 and danger at 90 percent of the range, or `thresholds`); `colorStops` (absolute values) override both. `steps` is the number of intensity steps above empty.
`onCellClick` adds a pointer cursor and the Enter and Space handling, but cells stay `gridcell`s, not buttons. Pass `dir` only if you want to leave the LTR island: props are spread after it.

HoverCard.use: A rich preview that appears when the pointer rests on a link or when it gains focus, for user cards and link previews. Opens after 300 ms and closes after 150 ms by default. The content is supplementary, not interactive.
instead: content the user must be able to click, type in or reach by keyboard
a help icon with a short explanation

head: Key
Action
rows: Focusing the trigger opens the card after `openDelay`; moving focus away closes it after `closeDelay`

keyboard.text: The trigger is an `<a>`, so it is a tab stop only when it has an `href` (or `tabIndex`). Radix sets `tabindex="-1"` on every focusable element inside the card, so keyboard users cannot reach links or buttons in it. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing for keys. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `bottom`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the card on a collision.

screenReaders.text: The card has no role, no label and no `aria-describedby` link to its trigger, and it is portalled to the end of `<body>`: a screen reader user may not find it, and it does not announce when it opens. Treat its content as a duplicate of something reachable elsewhere (the linked page, a profile), never as the only place for information or actions.

motion.text: The card fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The open and close delays are timers and stay.

ssr.text: Only the trigger renders on the server; the card is portalled after mount and only opens from pointer hover or focus. A `defaultOpen` card appears after hydration.

gotchas: Touch never opens it: Radix ignores touch pointers and prevents default on `touchstart`, so a touch user taps the link and navigates. Do not rely on it for mobile.
`HoverCard` sets `openDelay` 300 and `closeDelay` 150, shorter than Radix's own 700 and 300; pass your own values to change them.
Pressing the pointer on the card, or having text selected inside it, stops it from closing when the pointer leaves.
`HoverCardContent` shares `size` (`md`, 18rem), `padded` and `arrow` with `PopoverContent` but has no `disablePortal`.

IdentityAvatar.use: Anyone in a Sutra room drawn as one family: people as a photo or drawn initials, agents and machines as a Sutra mascot head whose face follows their presence, apps as their Bead tile. Presence is a shaped mark in the corner or a bead on a thread round the face; ink in the paper style, the seed tint in the stock style.
instead: a plain person picture with a coloured status dot and a verified badge
the persona builder's generated faces (shapes, visors, uploads)
the assistant itself at any size, with all eight states and its motion
an app icon on its own, outside a list of people

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Wrap it in a `Button` or a link when it should open a profile.

items: With a `name` the avatar is `role="img"` named from the name, the kind and the presence: "Asha Rao, online", "Ada, agent, busy", "Notes, app". `label` replaces that name. Without a name, or with `decorative`, it is `aria-hidden`; use `decorative` when the name is printed next to it (member lists, chat rows), so it is heard once.
The drawing inside (the svg, the mascot, the app tile) is always hidden; the presence is part of the name, never colour or shape alone.

motion.text: Avatars hold still by default: an agent's mascot is paused at its expression for the presence. With `animated` the mascot moves and a busy agent's bead slides along its thread; `prefersReducedMotion()` (system setting or `<html data-motion>`) keeps the mascot still and the twin blocks in `sutra.css` stop the slide, so the bead stays at its place.

ssr.text: The markup is the same on the server and the client, photo included (an SVG `<image>`, so the initials do not flash). The server assumes left-to-right, so on a right-to-left page the presence moves to the start corner after hydration. A photo that fails to load is swapped for the initials on the client.

slots: `identity-avatar`: the root (`data-kind`, `data-presence`, `data-presence-style`, `data-character`, `data-photo`); its parts carry `data-part` (`disc`, `hairline`, `monogram`, `photo`, `frame`, `mascot`, `app`, `presence`, `thread`, `bead`), each painted in `currentColor` and coloured by the "Identity avatar" section of `sutra.css`.
gotchas: Kinds: `person` (default) draws `src` or the initials; `agent` draws a mascot head in a circle and `machine` the same in a rounded square, with the face following the presence (online awake, busy at work, away asleep, offline asleep and dimmed); `app` draws `SutraAppIcon` for a Sutra `app`, or a tile with the initials of `name` for any other app, always with the mark presence. `seed` (a stable id, defaulting to `name`) picks the stock colour and an agent's mascot (`identityAvatarCharacter(seed)`, any character but the Sutradhar, whose head and shoulders reads as a person without a photo); `character` chooses one, the Sutradhar included, and `color` overrides the seed colour (the paper style draws everything in one ink regardless).

`monogram="drawn"` (default) draws the initials as monoline strokes, A to Z and 0 to 9, with accents folded ("Zoë Åberg" is ZA); any other letter or script falls back to the UI font, as does `monogram="text"`. Under 32 px one initial is shown.

`presenceStyle="mark"` (default) cuts a transparent gap and draws a solid (online), barred (busy), half (away) or hollow (offline) mark at the logical end corner, so it sits on any surface. `presenceStyle="bead"` threads the face (a full thread online, a barred bead busy, half a thread away, a dashed thread and hollow bead offline); the thread follows a machine's square and is left out when there is no presence, so chat rows stay plain.

Sizes are steps from `xs` (20 px) to `xl` (64 px) or any number of pixels; the drawing is in pixel units, so strokes, marks and the mascot's features are tuned for the size rather than scaled. To overlap a group, use negative spacing and a `ring-2 ring-background` (`rounded-full`) on each avatar, as `AvatarGroup` does for `Avatar`.

ImageWithFallback.use: An image that reserves its space, shimmers until it loads, fades in, and shows an "Image unavailable" state when it fails or has no `src`. It can load through your own fetch (for authenticated images).
instead: a person's picture with initials as the fallback

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: The image keeps its `alt` (an empty string for a decorative image). On failure the area becomes a `role="img"` named "<alt> (image unavailable)", or "Image unavailable" with no alt; the visible "Image unavailable" text is `aria-hidden` so it is not read twice.
The shimmer skeleton is `aria-hidden`. There is no live announcement when the image finishes loading or fails.

motion.text: The shimmer has `motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the fade-in is a 300 ms opacity transition that the global net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: With a `src` the server renders the `` at opacity 0 over the shimmer skeleton; it becomes visible only after hydration, when the load (or an already complete image) is detected, so the picture is invisible until the script runs. Reserve the space with `ratio` or `width` and `height` to avoid a layout jump. With no `src` the error state renders on both sides.

gotchas: Pass `width` and `height` (or `ratio`, which wins) so the box has its aspect ratio before the image arrives; without either, it holds a minimum height of 6rem while loading.
`className` goes on the wrapper and `imgClassName` on the ``. `fit` is `cover` by default, `contain` shows the whole image. `loading` defaults to `lazy`.

`fetcher(src)` returns a `Blob` that is shown through an object URL, revoked on unmount; a rejection shows the fallback. Use `fallback` to replace the default icon and text, `onLoad` and `onError` to react.

InfoTooltip.use: A small (i) or (?) icon button that reveals a bold title and a description in a tooltip, placed next to a label or field to explain it.
instead: a label on an existing control
longer help with links or interactive content
a rich preview of a linked thing
help text that should always be visible

head: Key
Action
rows: Focusing the button opens the tooltip after the delay; moving focus away closes it
Activate the button (native `<button type="button">`), which closes the tooltip

keyboard.text: There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing; the bubble text uses `text-start`.

screenReaders.text: The trigger is a `<button>` named by `label`, else by `title` when it is a string, else `"Help"` (icon `help`) or `"More information"`. While open, the tooltip (`role="tooltip"`) is linked to the button by `aria-describedby`, so a `title` that is also the name is read twice. The icon is `aria-hidden`. `children` are rendered inside the bubble after the description.

motion.text: The bubble fades and zooms in from the button and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The icon colour change is a transition and ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: Only the button renders on the server; the bubble is portalled after mount and only opens from hover or focus. Nothing differs between server and client.

gotchas: Touch does not open it (Radix tooltips ignore touch pointers and a tap closes them): do not put the only copy of important help in an `InfoTooltip`.
It uses `Tooltip`, so it follows the nearest `TooltipProvider`'s delay (200 ms by default); there is no `delayDuration` prop, so set the delay on the provider.
Extra props and `className` go to the button, `contentClassName` to the bubble; `side`, `align` and `variant` position and style the bubble.
`size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) changes the icon and the button box; the pointer target is enlarged to at least 24 px by `hitArea`.

InkEmoji.use: Original hand-drawn art for every emoji of the built-in picker set (198 across smileys, people, nature, food, activities, travel, objects and symbols) as an svg in currentColor, readable at 16px, in three variants (solid, tint, outline) with optional motion on named parts, plus EmojiGlyph, the wrapper that makes any emoji read as ink on paper in the paper style.
instead: a reaction pill with a count
a user interface icon, not a character
a character with states, not an emoji

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Put a button around it when it should act, and name that button.

items: Decorative by default: the svg is `aria-hidden`, so say what it means in text next to it.
`title="Approve"` names it (`role="img"` with a `<title>`); `title` set to `true` uses its built-in name (`inkEmojiNames`, "Thumbs up").

`EmojiGlyph` keeps the emoji character as real text in `data-part="glyph"`. When the drawing shows it is clipped, not `display: none`, so copy, find in page and assistive technology that reads text keep working. Add `aria-hidden` when the words beside it already say the same.

motion.text: Still by default (`animate={false}`). With `animate="hover"`, `animate="loop"` or `playKey`, named parts move with CSS keyframes (a wind-up, the move, a settle, about 1 to 1.5 s, then the still drawing). Under reduced motion (the system setting, or `data-motion="reduce"` on `<html>`) the stylesheet removes the animation and the script does not start a play, so the still drawing shows; nothing carries meaning only in motion. The ink treatment is a filter and a swap, not an animation.

ssr.text: The same markup on the server and the client: the solid and tint drawings define their masks inside the svg with ids from `useId`, and `animate="loop"` is in the markup (`data-play="loop"`).
