Hover and `playKey` plays start after hydration. `EmojiGlyph` adds one hidden `svg#sutra-emoji-ink` filter to `<body>` after mount (once per document, `svg[data-slot="emoji-ink-filter"]`), which the paper style uses to turn a colour glyph into one ink.

slots: `ink-emoji`: the drawing svg (`data-variant` solid, tint or outline; `data-animate` hover or loop; `data-play` once or loop while a play runs). Inside a solid or tint drawing, `data-part="all"` wraps the art and named parts carry `data-part` (eye, mouth, hand, tear …) and `data-move`, the keyframes they play (`sutra-emoji-<move>`).
`emoji`: the `EmojiGlyph` wrapper (`data-ink`, `data-art`), also used by `InkEmoji fallback`
gotchas: `InkEmoji` returns `null` for an emoji without a drawing (check `hasInkEmoji`, list in `inkEmojiSet`) unless `fallback` is set, which renders the colour glyph filtered to one ink at the same size. A trailing variation selector does not matter (❤ and ❤️ match).

The drawing uses `currentColor` in a 24 box: colour it with a text colour and size it with `size` (pixels or any CSS length, default `1em`). `variant="solid"` (the default) fills the shapes and cuts the features out as real holes (an SVG mask, so the art works on any background and in dark mode); `tint` adds a light tint of the ink for the secondary parts (tears, blush, cuffs, the core of a flame); `outline` is the monoline drawing with a 1.75 stroke. `hasInkEmoji(emoji, variant)` checks one variant. The masks have ids of their own, so render `InkEmoji` again rather than cloning its markup.

`animate="hover"` listens on the nearest interactive ancestor (a button, link, label, summary, option, menu item, tab or anything with `tabindex`), or the parent element when there is none, and plays once on pointer enter and focus. `playKey` plays once whenever it changes to a truthy value, also on mount, so a parent that remounts the emoji with a new key still gets the play. `playInkEmoji(svg)` starts a play from your own code. `outline` never moves.

`EmojiGlyph` shows the colour glyph by default and the ink in `[data-style="paper"]`; `ink` forces it everywhere, `ink={false}` keeps colour in paper. Glyphs without a drawing are filtered, so detail goes soft below about 20px. The paper-dark ink is the filtered glyph inverted to light on black. A subtree that is light inside a dark page still inverts, so keep the `dark` class where the page is dark.

InlineAlert.use: A contextual message that sits inside content (a form, a panel, a settings page), with an icon, a title and description, an optional action and an optional dismiss button. `layout="strip"` makes it an edge-to-edge bar.
instead: a page-level announcement at the top of the app
a transient message that goes away by itself
the user must answer before going on

head: Key
Action
rows: Reaches the controls you put in `action`, in `InlineAlertActions` or in the text, then the dismiss button
Presses the focused button (Enter follows a link)

keyboard.text: The alert itself is not focusable and has no arrow-key behaviour, so nothing changes in RTL. The dismiss button is on the end edge, and the `accent` appearance puts its coloured edge on the start side (`border-s`), so both flip with `dir`.

items: The root is `role="alert"` for `warning` and `destructive` (announced at once, interrupting) and `role="status"` for every other tone (a polite live region). Pass `role` to override: the strip layout in the tests uses `role="status"` on a warning.
The icon is `aria-hidden`; the colour alone does not carry the meaning, so put the severity in the text.
The dismiss button is named by `dismissLabel` (default "Dismiss"). Give it a more specific label when several alerts are on screen.

`InlineAlertTitle` is a `

`, not a heading, so it adds nothing to the heading outline.

motion.text: Static: nothing enters or animates. Only the close button's hover fade, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so the server and client output match.

slots: `inline-alert-icon`: the wrapper around the icon (not rendered when `icon={false}`)
`inline-alert-action`: the box that holds the `action` node, placed before the dismiss button
gotchas: There is no open state. `onDismiss` only reports the click and the dismiss button appears only when you pass it: unmount the alert yourself (the tests do it with `useState`). `AlertBanner` is the one that hides itself.
`action` sits beside the message, vertically centred; `InlineAlertActions` is the row of buttons under the description. Do not use both for the same buttons.
`variant` is a deprecated alias of `tone` (`brand` is `primary`); `tone` wins when both are set. The default tone is `info`.

`appearance` is `soft` (tinted), `outline` (bordered, on the page background) or `accent` (soft with a 3px coloured start edge); `layout="strip"` also drops the radius and all borders but the bottom one.

InlineEditText.use: A single-line field that appears in place of a title or name so the user can rename it: it focuses and selects on mount, Enter or blur commits the trimmed text, Escape cancels. Mount it when editing starts and unmount it on `onCommit` or `onCancel`.
instead: a field that is always visible in a form

head: Key
Action
rows: Commit: `onCommit` gets the trimmed text when it is non-empty and differs from the starting value; otherwise `onCancel` runs
Cancel: restore the starting text (uncontrolled) and call `onCancel`
Blur commits, the same as Enter
Typed into the field as usual

keyboard.text: Every key press and click on the field stops propagating, so the surrounding row's shortcuts (a list's arrow keys, a hotkey, a row click) do not fire while editing. Enter and Escape are ignored during IME composition. No arrow-key handling of its own, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A native `<input type="text">` named by `aria-label`, else `label` (default "Edit text"). Pass a specific name such as "Rename Quarterly report" when several rows can be edited.

It takes focus and selects its text on mount, so the screen reader moves to the field when editing starts. After `onCommit` or `onCancel` you are responsible for returning focus to the row or button that opened it.
There is no announcement of the commit or the cancel; show your own status if the change needs one.

motion.text: Static: no animation or transition beyond the focus ring.

ssr.text: Renders a plain input from `value` or `defaultValue`. The focus and select happen in an effect after mount, so the server HTML is the same as the client's and nothing is focused until hydration.

gotchas: Blur commits, it does not cancel. Clicking away, or moving focus to a button, saves the text; use Escape to discard. An empty or unchanged draft counts as a cancel, so `onCancel` also runs on those.

The starting value is read once, on mount: later edits are compared with it, and a committed draft is not treated as the new starting text. Unmount the field after `onCommit` instead of keeping it open.

`onValueChange` receives the raw draft on every keystroke; `onCommit` receives the trimmed text. The native `onChange` is removed from the type. With controlled `value` the field does not reset itself on Escape: restore your state in `onCancel`.
`autoFocus` defaults to true and is handled by the component (focus and select on mount); pass `autoFocus={false}` to skip it. A commit or cancel runs once even though Enter is followed by a blur.

Input.use: The single-line text field. It takes every native `<input>` prop and adds `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix`, `suffix` and `clearable`. `PasswordInput` adds a show and hide toggle, `SearchInput` a search icon, a clear button and an optional focus hotkey.
instead: numbers with steppers and locale formatting
addons that are real buttons, selects or other controls
a one-time code split into slots

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves to and from the field and the `PasswordInput` toggle. The `clearable` button is not a tab stop (`tabIndex` -1)
On the `PasswordInput` toggle: show or hide the text
In a `SearchInput` that has text and `clearable`: empty it and call `onClear`
Anywhere on the page: focus and select the `SearchInput`. A plain key typed into another field stays text; a chord with Ctrl or Meta still fires

keyboard.text: Typing is native. There are no arrow-key handlers, and the icons and addons use logical padding, so RTL only mirrors the layout.

items: A native `<input>` named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; a field with no visible label needs `aria-label`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` adds `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required` unless you pass them.
`SearchInput` is `type="search"` (role `searchbox`), sets `aria-keyshortcuts` from `hotkey`, and hides the key hint (`aria-hidden`).

The clear button is named "Clear" (not translatable through a prop). The `PasswordInput` toggle is named "Show password" or "Hide password" and also carries `aria-pressed`. Icons are `aria-hidden`; `leadingIcon`, `trailingIcon`, `prefix` and `suffix` content that you pass is not hidden for you.

motion.text: The clear button pops in with `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-75`, and the border and ring fade with a short transition; the reduced-motion net removes the zoom and ends the transitions in 1 ms.

ssr.text: `Input` and `PasswordInput` render the same markup on both sides, including the clear button when a `value` or `defaultValue` is set. `SearchInput` reads its key hint after mount (`hotkey` is turned into key labels in an effect), so the hint chips are not in the server HTML and appear on hydration.

slots: `input`: the `<input>` element (the root when there are no addons)
`input-wrapper`: the outer `div`, rendered only when an icon, addon or `clearable` is present
gotchas: `className` lands on the inner `<input>` once any addon is present, so layout classes (`w-48`, `flex-1`) do nothing there; put them in `wrapperClassName`. Without addons `className` is the root.
`PasswordInput` defaults to `autoComplete="current-password"` (pass `"new-password"` when setting one), turns off `spellCheck`, and does not accept `type` or `trailingIcon`.
`clearable` fires a real `input` event, so `onChange` runs with an empty value, then `onClear`. `SearchInput` is `clearable` by default.
Pass `prefix` and `suffix` as text addons; for interactive addons use `InputGroup`.

InputGroup.use: One input-like box that hosts a control with addons around it: text, icons, buttons or keys at the start or end, or in a row above or below. `InputGroupInput` or `InputGroupTextarea` is the control; the box takes its focus, invalid and disabled styling from it.
instead: a field whose addons are only an icon, a text prefix or suffix, or a clear button
attached buttons with no text field

head: Key
Action
rows: Follows DOM order through the control and any addon buttons, links or inputs

keyboard.text: The group adds no key handling. Clicking padding or an `InputGroupText` addon focuses the control (a click on a button, link or other control inside an addon is left alone). Visual order comes from `align` through CSS `order`, but tab and reading order come from where you put the parts in the markup, so write them in the order users should reach them. RTL only mirrors the layout: `inline-start` and `inline-end` follow the reading direction.

items: The group and every addon are `role="group"` without a name. Give the `InputGroup` an `aria-label` when its parts need announcing as a unit; the control still needs its own name from a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`.

`InputGroupInput` and `InputGroupTextarea` are native controls that read `id`, `disabled`, `required`, `aria-describedby` and `invalid` (as `aria-invalid`) from a surrounding `Field`. Put `invalid`, `disabled` and `required` on the control, not on `InputGroup`; the box restyles through `has-[...]` on the control.
An icon-only `InputGroupButton` needs `aria-label`. Text that sits in an addon (`https://`, `USD`) is read as plain text before or after the field, so repeat it in the control's label if it matters.

motion.text: Static apart from the border and ring fade on focus, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API or mount state, so server and client output match.

slots: `input-group-text`: muted inline text inside an addon
`input-group-control`: the input or textarea that drives the box styling
gotchas: `InputGroup` `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the height and `variant` the look; it does not size the control. Pass `size` to `InputGroupInput` too when you change the padding.
`block-start` and `block-end` addons stack above or below the control and make the box auto-height; with a textarea the box also becomes auto-height.
`InputGroupButton` is a `Button`: `variant` defaults to `ghost`, `size` to `xs` (`xs`, `sm`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`), and `type` to `button`.
Only the control gets focus styling; a focused addon button does not light the box.

InputOTP.use: A one-time code or PIN field drawn as separate character slots over one real input (the `input-otp` library). Compose `InputOTPGroup`, `InputOTPSlot` and `InputOTPSeparator` yourself, or use `OTPField` for a ready-made row of slots.

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the single underlying input (the slots are not tab stops)
Fill the next slot; a character that fails `pattern` is rejected
Remove characters, as in a normal text input
Move the native caret, which highlights the matching slot
Paste a code; `pasteTransformer` can clean it first

keyboard.text: Everything is native text input behaviour: one `<input>` sits over the slots with transparent text. `onComplete` fires when the value reaches `maxLength` (`length` for `OTPField`). Slots are a flex row, so in an RTL document they run right to left; wrap the field in `dir="ltr"` if a code should read left to right.

items: The real input carries the whole value and is what assistive technology reads. Give it a name with `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required`.

The input defaults to `autoComplete="one-time-code"` (so the browser can offer an SMS code), `inputMode="numeric"` and `spellCheck` off. `OTPField` sets `inputMode` to `text` when you give it a non-digit `pattern`.
Slots are plain `div`s with no role or `aria-hidden`, and the fake caret is `aria-hidden`. `InputOTPSeparator` is a `role="separator"`, so each one is announced when a reader walks the content.

motion.text: A character pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-90`, which the reduced-motion net strips of its movement. The fake caret blinks with `animate-caret-blink`, which the net turns off, so it stays solid.

ssr.text: The input and the slots render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`; the active slot, the fake caret and the library's autofill style rules appear only after mount, because they depend on focus and `document.head`.

slots: `input-otp-slot`: one character cell; `data-active` while it holds the caret, `data-filled` when it has a character
gotchas: `OTPField` is digits only by default (`pattern` is `REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS`); pass `pattern` to allow letters, and `groupSize` and `separator` to split the slots (3 and 3 for a six digit code).
`InputOTP` needs `maxLength` and one `InputOTPSlot index` per character; a missing index leaves a character with nothing to show it. `OTPField` takes `length` instead.
`onChange` receives the string value, not an event. `defaultValue` works because the wrapper owns the uncontrolled state; pass `value` to control it.
`size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg` and applies to every slot through context; `invalid` turns the slot borders red.

Item.use: One list row: media, a title with a description, and trailing actions. Static, or one link or button for the whole row. `ItemGroup` lists rows with placeholders for loading and empty states.
instead: a titled tray with a header and footer around a panel of rows

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves to a row that is a link or a button, and to controls inside a static row's `ItemActions`
Follows the link, or runs the button's `onClick`
Runs the button's `onClick` (not for a link row)

keyboard.text: A static row is not focusable. With `asChild` the child keeps its own keyboard behaviour. No key depends on direction, but the `chevron` mirrors in RTL.

items: `ItemGroup` is a `role="list"` (it cannot be changed) and needs an `aria-label`. A static `Item` inside it has `role="listitem"`; a link or button row keeps its own role and is wrapped in a `listitem` box. Outside a group, a static `Item` is a plain `div`.
A `disabled` link loses its `href` and gets `aria-disabled`; a disabled button row is natively disabled. The `chevron` is `aria-hidden`.
`loading` renders `aria-busy` with sr-only "Loading…"; the placeholder rows are `aria-hidden`.
`ItemTitle` and `ItemDescription` set a `title` tooltip from their text when it is a plain string, because they truncate.
`ItemSeparator` is `role="presentation"`.

motion.text: Static; the hover background and the chevron nudge are transitions, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

slots: `item-separator`: a hairline for a group that is not `divided`
gotchas: The element follows the props: `href` gives an `<a>`, `onClick` (without `href`) a `<button type="button">`, `asChild` renders your child (a router link) as the row, and nothing gives a `div`. With `href` and `onClick`, the link still gets the `onClick`.
A link or button row must hold no other buttons or links (nested interactive content). Put the actions in a static row instead.
`chevron` only shows on an interactive row (link, button or `asChild`), never on a static one; with `asChild` it is appended after the child's own content.

`ItemDescription` truncates to one line by default; pass `lines={2}` or `lines="none"`. `ItemGroup` `divided` draws hairlines, and `emptyState` shows only when there are no children and `loading` is off.
Item.example:
import { Item, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemGroup, ItemMedia, ItemTitle } from "@sutra/ui";
import { RiMailLine, RiSettings3Line } from "@sutra/ui/icons";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <ItemGroup aria-label="Account" variant="outline" divided className="max-w-md">
      <Item href="/inbox" chevron>
        <ItemMedia variant="icon">
          <RiMailLine aria-hidden />
        </ItemMedia>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Inbox</ItemTitle>
          <ItemDescription>12 unread messages</ItemDescription>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
      <Item href="/settings" chevron>
        <ItemMedia variant="icon">
          <RiSettings3Line aria-hidden />
        </ItemMedia>
        <ItemContent>
          <ItemTitle>Settings</ItemTitle>
          <ItemDescription>Profile, notifications and billing</ItemDescription>
        </ItemContent>
      </Item>
    </ItemGroup>
  );
}

KeyValue.use: A description list of facts, a name on one side and a value on the other, in rows, stacked or grid layouts, with an optional copy button per value.
instead: several columns of records to compare or sort
a row with media, title and actions
one number with a label and a trend

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to the copy buttons (only on entries with `copyable`)

keyboard.text: The list and its text are not focusable. No key depends on direction.

items: `KeyValueList` is a real `<dl>`; each `KeyValue` is a `<div>` holding a `<dt>` (the label) and a `<dd>` (the value), so assistive technology announces them as term and definition pairs. Do not put `KeyValue` outside a list.
The copy button is named "Copy <label>" when `label` is a string, and "Copy value" when it is a node. `CopyButton` announces the copied state itself.
A missing value shows the `empty` placeholder ("—" by default) as plain text.

motion.text: Static: no animation. The copy button's own feedback follows `CopyButton`.

ssr.text: Plain markup from the props, with no browser API, so server and client output match. The copy button renders a normal button on the server.

gotchas: `layout="rows"` (default) truncates the value on one line with the full text in `title`; `stacked` and `grid` wrap instead. `truncate` on a single `KeyValue` overrides either way. The `title` is only set for string or number values.
`copyable` copies the value only when it is a string or number: with a node value, pass a string (`copyable="sk_live_123_full"`) to say what to copy. An empty value shows no copy button.
Use either `items` (data) or `KeyValue` children: when `items` is set the children are ignored. `columns` only applies to `layout="grid"` and `dividers` only to `rows` and `stacked`.
`mono` on the list sets the monospace face for every value; an entry's own `mono` wins, including `mono={false}`.

Label.use: A form label for any control: a Radix label with an optional required asterisk and a muted `hint`. Point it at a control with `htmlFor`, or let `FieldLabel` do it inside a `Field`.
instead: a label inside a `Field` that wires itself to the control
the title of a `Fieldset` of related controls
a categorical tag, not a form label

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Clicking the label forwards focus (and a click, for a checkbox or switch) to the control it names.

items: It renders a native `<label>`, so `htmlFor` (or wrapping the control) gives the control its accessible name. The `hint` text is inside the label, so it is part of the name (for example "Email (work)").
The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`: `required` on `Label` is only the visual mark. Set `required` on the control (or on `Field`) to expose `required` to assistive technology and to validation.
A label does not name custom widgets that are not labelable elements (a `div role="combobox"`); those take `aria-labelledby` pointing at the label id, which `FieldLabel` and `Combobox` do for you.

motion.text: Static: no animation or transition.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API or mount state, so server and client output match.

gotchas: Radix cancels text selection on a double click on the label (so a quick double click on a checkbox label does not highlight it), except when the target is a button, input, select or textarea inside it.

The disabled look comes from `peer-disabled:` (the control must be a preceding sibling with the `peer` class, as `Checkbox` is) or from a `group` ancestor with `data-disabled="true"`; otherwise pass your own classes. `FieldLabel` dims itself from the surrounding `Field`.
Extra props go to the `<label>`; `className` merges after the defaults.

Lightbox.use: A full-screen viewer for a set of images or videos: previous and next, a counter, a thumbnail strip, zoom and pan, swipe, optional download. Put `LightboxTrigger`s (your thumbnails) inside it, or open it from code with `useLightbox`.
instead: any other content in a modal
browse in place without a full-screen viewer
previews for pdf, text and other file types
one image that handles loading and errors

head: Key
Action
rows: Previous or next item (stops at the ends unless `loop`). Ignored while a video is focused
Zoom in or out by 1.5 times, or reset to 100%
Cycles through the toolbar buttons, the previous and next buttons, and the thumbnails (focus is trapped while open)
Press the focused button, including a thumbnail

keyboard.text: In RTL the arrows follow reading order: ArrowLeft goes to the next item and ArrowRight to the previous, and a swipe towards the inline start brings the next item. Closing sends focus back to the element that had it when the viewer opened (the `LightboxTrigger`, or a button that called `openAt`), even though the viewer has no Radix trigger; if that element is gone, focus ends on the page body. Pointer extras: double-click toggles 200%, a drag pans a zoomed image, Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel or a trackpad pinch zooms.

items: Radix gives the panel `role="dialog"` named by `label` (default "Image viewer") and hides the page. The counter ("2 / 5") is a polite live region, so it announces each change of item.
The current image has its `alt` (a failed one reads "<alt> (image unavailable)"); videos get `aria-label` from `alt` and native controls. Captions are plain text.

Buttons are named "Zoom out", "Zoom in", "Download", "Close viewer", "Previous" and "Next". Thumbnails are a `group` named "Thumbnails" of buttons "View 2 of 5: <alt>" with `aria-current` on the shown one.
`LightboxTrigger` has `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and defaults to the name "Open <alt>" of its item; give it an `aria-label` when it holds more than an image.

motion.text: The backdrop and panel fade and scale in with `animate-in` (movement stripped under reduced motion), and zoom changes use a 150 ms transform transition that the global net ends in 1 ms, so zoom is immediate. The thumbnail fade is a transition too.

ssr.text: A closed viewer renders only its children (the triggers) on both sides; the panel is portalled. A viewer that is `open` on first render appears after hydration.

slots: `lightbox-stage`: the area that holds the media, the swipe and pan surface
gotchas: Control it with `open`, `index` and their `onOpenChange` and `onIndexChange`, or take `useLightbox()` and spread `{...lb.props}`. Opening through a `LightboxTrigger` sets the index first. `index` is clamped to the items.
The previous and next buttons are hidden below the `sm` breakpoint (swipe and the arrow keys remain); there is no wrap unless `loop`, and the buttons disable at the ends.
Zoom resets whenever the item changes or the viewer opens or closes, and a swipe to the next item is ignored while zoomed in (it pans instead). `maxZoom` defaults to 4.
`download` adds a plain link with the `download` attribute (so it is subject to the browser's cross-origin rule) and `downloadName` names the file. The two neighbouring images are preloaded.

LineChart.use: Cartesian charts over rows of data. `LineChart` draws lines, `AreaChart` filled (optionally stacked) areas, `BarChart` grouped, stacked or horizontal bars; all three take `data`, `index` and `series`, and share axes, legend, tooltip, time axis and reference lines.
instead: a tiny trend inside a row or card, no axes
one number with a small trend
a ranked list with proportional bars
build a chart type that does not exist yet

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the chart frame; leaving it clears the active point
Next point (the first one when none is active); stops at the last
Previous point (the last one when none is active); stops at the first
Clears the active point and its tooltip
On a legend button: hide or show the series. With Alt: show only that series, or restore all

keyboard.text: The frame is a forced `dir="ltr"` island, so ArrowRight always goes toward later points, also on an RTL page; nothing swaps. The legend sits outside the island and follows the page direction.

items: The frame is `role="img"` (focusable) named by `label`, by default "Line chart of Revenue, Cost by day" (also "Area chart", "Stacked area chart", "Bar chart", "Horizontal bar chart"). The SVG is `aria-hidden`; pass your own `label` for a useful name.
The data is a visually hidden `<table>` after the chart: caption is the label, one row per datum, the index as row header, a missing value as "–". Hidden series drop out of the table and the tooltip.
Stepping with the keyboard writes "Fri: Prompt 160, Completion 50" into a polite live region. Hover shows the tooltip but does not announce.

The legend is a `group` named "Toggle series" of buttons with `aria-pressed` (a plain `list` when `legendInteractive={false}`). With `loading`, the root has `aria-busy` and one hidden "Loading line chart…" text.

motion.text: Lines, areas, bars and dots animate data changes with `motion-safe:transition-all duration-500` (the `animate` prop, default true), so with `prefers-reduced-motion` no transition class applies and the chart updates in place. Bar dimming uses `transition-opacity`, which the global net ends in 1 ms. `animate={false}` turns the transitions off for everyone.

ssr.text: The full SVG renders on the server, but at the fixed fallback width of 600 px: the real width is measured after mount (layout effect plus `ResizeObserver`) and the plot is redrawn then. Tick labels and tooltip text use `Intl` with the runtime locale (and time zone on a time axis), so a server with another locale can differ from the browser: pass `valueFormatter`, `yAxis.formatter` or `xAxis.formatter` to pin them.

slots: `chart-line`: the stroke path of a series (`LineChart` and `AreaChart`)
`chart-area`: the filled area of a series
`chart-active-dot`: the marker on the hovered or focused point
`chart-crosshair`: the vertical guide on line and area charts
`chart-hit`: the transparent rectangle that receives pointer and touch events
gotchas: `loading` shows the placeholder only while `data` is empty; with rows it keeps the chart and just sets `aria-busy`. `emptyState` (default "No data") is never shown while loading.

`connectNulls` and `xAxis.type="time" | "linear"` have no effect on `BarChart` (bars are always categories), and `connectNulls` is ignored on stacked areas, where a null counts as 0. `referenceLines` with `axis: "x"` need a time or linear axis.
The legend shows by default only for two or more series. The value axis includes 0 unless you pass `yAxis.min="auto"`.
Series without a `color` take `var(--chart-N, hex)` in order, so a theme can recolour them; a token name or any CSS colour also works.

Markdown.use: Renders a markdown string with GitHub-flavoured extras (tables, task lists, strikethrough) in the design tokens: headings, lists, quotes, links, images, inline and fenced code with a copy button, optional KaTeX math and citation pills. It is memoized per block, so streamed text only re-renders the tail.
instead: one snippet with highlighting, a file name and line numbers
a chat message that wraps this
a few styled lines rather than a document
a code span inside your own text

keyboard.text: There is no keyboard handling of its own. Links are normal tab stops, and so are each code block and each table wrapper while it overflows (scroll boxes, so the arrow keys scroll them), each code block's "Copy code" button and, with `onCite`, each citation pill (a button; Enter and Space activate it).

items: The output is plain semantic HTML: `h1` to `h6`, `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `blockquote`, `table` with `thead` and `th`, `img`. Heading levels are written as in the source and are not shifted. An image without alt text gets `alt=""`.

A fenced block is a header with the language (or "text") and a button named "Copy code", which becomes "Copied" after a copy, then a `pre`. The code is not highlighted. The `pre` and the wrapper around a table are scroll boxes that get `tabindex="0"` while they overflow (arrow keys scroll them), and always have a name through `role="group"`: "ts code" (the language, or "Code") and "Table".
Citation pills: a `button` named "Source 2: Title" with `onCite`, a link with a hover card when the source has `href`, else a plain `sup`.
Task-list items are native checkboxes rendered by GFM.

motion.text: Nothing moves except the copy-check icon, which zooms in with `animate-in` (the global net removes the movement) and link colour fades (ended in 1 ms).

ssr.text: react-markdown and KaTeX produce their HTML synchronously, so the server renders the whole document. The block split and block keys derive from `useId`, which matches on both sides.

gotchas: Raw HTML in the source is shown as text, not rendered (no `rehype-raw`), and link and image URLs go through react-markdown's default filter that drops schemes such as `javascript:`. Add `rehypePlugins` for HTML, and sanitize it yourself.

Keep `components`, `remarkPlugins` and `rehypePlugins` stable (module scope or `useMemo`): each block is memoized on those references, so a new array on every render re-renders every block while streaming. `components` is merged over the defaults.
`math` needs the KaTeX stylesheet loaded once by the app (`import "katex/dist/katex.min.css"`); without `math` dollar signs stay as text. Invalid TeX shows rather than throwing.

`[1]` and `[2, 3]` in prose turn into citation pills only up to `citeCount` (default `sources.length`), and never inside code or links. External `http(s)` links get `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Fenced code does not use `CodeBlock`: override `pre` in `components` to get highlighting.

Marquee.use: An endless, slowly scrolling row of presentational items (logos, chips, short quotes). It repeats the items to fill the width, pauses on hover and focus, and becomes a still, wrapped row under reduced motion.
instead: logos only, with a marquee mode built on this
a list whose items enter and leave

head: Key
Action
rows: Reaches focusable items in the first copy only; the repeats are `inert`. With `pausable` it also reaches the pause button
On the pause button: pauses or resumes the scroll

keyboard.text: Focus inside the scroller pauses it while `pauseOnHover` is on (the default). The pause button sits beside the track, not inside it, so focusing it does not pause by itself. No arrow keys are used. In RTL the track runs the other way with its own keyframes (`sutra-marquee-rtl`); `reverse` still flips whichever direction applies.

items: The first copy is a `ul` with `role="list"` named by `label`, and each child is an `li`. The repeats are `aria-hidden` and `inert`, so the items are read once.
The pause button is a toggle named "Pause scrolling" (`pauseLabel`) whose name does not change: `aria-pressed` flips and the icon swaps.
`label` names the list, not the root. Props you pass go on the root scrolling region.

motion.text: Under `prefers-reduced-motion` (CSS `motion-reduce:` classes, no JavaScript) the animation stops, the repeats are hidden, the items wrap onto centred lines, the edge fade is removed and the pause button is hidden, because the row is already still. The row can become taller than the single line it was.

ssr.text: The server renders two copies. After mount the root and one copy are measured and the number of copies grows to fill the width (at most 10), so the markup gains lists after hydration. The animation itself is CSS.

slots: `marquee-track`: the moving strip that holds the copies
gotchas: Keep the items presentational. Only the first copy is interactive and it moves, and links or buttons in the repeats are `inert`. Items that must be clickable belong in a `Carousel` or a static grid.

`pausable` is off by default, so touch and keyboard users have only the hover and focus pause. Turn it on for any row that moves for more than a few seconds (WCAG 2.2.2). A controlled `paused` pauses the row even without the button, and `pauseOnHover` pauses on top of it.
`duration` is the seconds for one loop of the items (default 30, an invalid value falls back to 30), `gap` a number of pixels or any CSS length (default `3rem`), and `fade` softens both edges.
Each child becomes one `li`; the `key` of a child element is kept.

MeshGradient.use: A decorative background of blurred, slowly drifting colour blobs, with optional film grain. Children render above it, so it works as a hero or panel backdrop.

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The background layer is `pointer-events-none`, so it never blocks clicks on the content above it.

screenReaders.text: The blob layer and the grain are `aria-hidden` decoration; only your `children` are exposed. The gradient adds no contrast guarantee: check that the text you put on it passes against every colour in `colors`.

motion.text: Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the blobs stand still (`motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the `animate-mesh` rule in `sutra.css` stops it too), leaving the static gradient. `animated={false}` does the same on demand.

ssr.text: Plain markup with inline styles and no browser API, so server and client output match. The motion is CSS only.

gotchas: At most five colours are used (one per blob); fewer repeat, and an empty array falls back to the default palette (three brand shades plus the `--chart-2` cyan and `--chart-6` violet, so a style such as paper retunes it). `colors` take any CSS colour, including `var(--color-brand-500)`.

`speed` multiplies the loop (1 is about 18 s, and each blob runs a little slower), `blur` is in px, `intensity` is blob opacity from 0 to 1 (default 0.7), and `grain` with `grainOpacity` adds the noise overlay.

The root is `relative isolate overflow-hidden`, and the layer sits at `-z-10` inside it: give the root a size (`className="h-64"`) and your own padding, since the layer is absolute. `layerClassName` styles the layer.
Large blurred areas cost paint time on low-end devices: a big `blur` over a full screen is the expensive combination.

Meter.use: A labelled usage bar for a level read against limits (CPU, memory, quota), turning warning and destructive past thresholds. Continuous or in discrete segments, with a caption. `MeterGroup` stacks or grids several.
instead: how far a task has got (a determinate bar with start and end)
one bar split into labelled parts
the legend rows of such a split

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: The bar is a `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` (`min`), `aria-valuemax` (`max`) and `aria-valuetext`. It is named by `label` (`aria-labelledby`), or just "Usage" when there is no label, so give every meter a `label`. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` passed to `Meter` goes on the bar (replacing the label as its name), not on the outer div.

The value text is "62.1 / 80 GB" with `unit`, otherwise a rounded percentage ("62%"). A string from `valueText` (or its function) becomes `aria-valuetext` too; `ariaValueText` overrides it, and a non-text `valueText` falls back to the percentage. `value={null}` reads "No data".
`loading` with no value drops the meter role and shows sr-only "Loading CPU…" (or "Loading usage…" without a string label); `loading` with a value keeps the meter and only sets `aria-busy`.
`MeterGroup` is a `role="group"`; pass `aria-label` ("Node").

motion.text: The fill width transition (500 ms), the segment colour fade and the loading pulse all carry `motion-reduce:` variants that turn them off.

ssr.text: Plain markup computed from the props (the label id uses `useId`), so server and client output match.

slots: `meter-fill`: the continuous fill, with an inline `width` percentage
`meter-value`: the value text beside the label
gotchas: Thresholds are percentages of the range, higher is worse, and default to warn 75 and danger 90; `thresholds={false}` turns them off. `data-level` on the root is `ok`, `warn` or `danger`.
Fill colour order: the threshold colour when strained, then `tone` (or the deprecated `color`), then `accent`, then primary. With `thresholds={false}` and no tone you get primary.
`min` and `max` set the scale and the fill is clamped to 0 to 100%, and `aria-valuenow` is clamped to the same range, while the visible and `aria-valuetext` text keep the real value ("130 / 100 GB").
`segments={n}` fills `round(percent * n)` blocks, so small values can show none. For task completion use `Progress`, which has the progressbar role.

MetricReadout.use: A compact menu-bar style reading ("CPU 92%") with an optional icon and tiny trend, turning warning or destructive when the value crosses thresholds. `MetricReadoutGroup` lines several up with separators.
instead: a value shown against a bounded bar
a battery with a glyph and charging state
a large headline figure with a trend

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: The visible parts (icon, label, value, unit, trend) sit in an `aria-hidden` wrapper, and a single sr-only sentence is read instead: "CPU 92%, high", "Fan 2,400 rpm", "GPU no data". The status word is appended under strain: "high" for warning and "critical" for danger. `statusLabels` renames them and `statusText` replaces the word (or `false` for none).
A `label` that is not a string or number needs `labelText`, or the sentence has no name.
`loading` with no value keeps the label, shows a placeholder, sets `aria-busy="true"` and reads "Loading CPU…".
`MetricReadoutGroup` is a `role="group"`; give it `label` ("System readings"). Its separators are `aria-hidden`.

motion.text: Static: no animation of its own (the loading placeholder is a `Skeleton`, which follows the net in `sutra.css`).

ssr.text: Plain markup, but numbers go through `Intl.NumberFormat` in the default locale, so a value of 1,000 or more can print "2,400" on a server and "2.400" in a browser, and hydration warns. Pass `locale` (or `formatValue`) when you server-render such values. Nothing else waits for mount.

gotchas: `thresholds` direction comes from the numbers: when `danger >= warning` higher is worse (CPU 70 and 90), otherwise lower is worse (battery 20 and 10). Only numeric values are classified, and `false` turns it off.
`tone` wins over `thresholds`, but only `destructive` and `warning` count as strain (they add the status word); other tones just colour the reading.
A string `statusText` is appended even when the reading is normal. A string `value` is shown as given and never classified; `null`, `undefined` and `""` show a dash and read "no data".
`variant="pill"` fills the chip (muted, or soft warning or destructive under strain); `plain` only colours the text. The `trend` slot is decorative, so the text must carry the meaning.

Monogram.use: A square letter tile for things that are not people: apps, providers, tools and workspaces. The letters and the colour come from the name, so the same name always looks the same.
instead: a person, with image, status and verified badge
a site's real icon with a fallback
a text label, not a tile

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: Decorative by default: with no `label` the tile is `aria-hidden`, which suits a tile that sits next to the name as visible text. Pass `label` ("Calendar") to make it a `role="img"` with that name, for example when the tile stands alone.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup computed from the props, with no browser API. The seed colour is a pure function of `name`, so server and client output match.

gotchas: Letters come from `monogramInitials(name)`: words split on anything that is not a letter or digit, the first letter of the first two words ("Nimbus AI" gives NA, "github-mcp" gives GM), two letters from a single word ("corvid" gives CO), and "?" for an empty name. `letters` or `children` replace them; `initialsOptions` tunes them.
`name` is required even with `letters`, because it seeds the colour. `color` overrides it, and the `brand` variant ignores both and uses the brand gradient.
`variant` is `solid` (seed colour, white letters; the default), `soft` (a light tint with coloured letters) or `brand`. `size` runs `xs` to `xl` and defaults to `md`.
`ProviderLogo` and `CapabilityMonogram` are presets built on it; use `Avatar` for a user.

Note.use: The quiet line a screen says while working or when there is nothing here: small, grey, optionally with a spinner or an icon, or in the destructive tone for a failure.
instead: a full placeholder with title and actions
a boxed notice with an action

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: A neutral or loading `Note` is `role="status"` (a polite live region); the destructive tone is `role="alert"` (assertive), so use it only for a real failure the user needs to hear.
`loading` adds `aria-busy="true"`. The spinner in it is hidden from assistive technology, so the text must say what is happening ("Loading results…").
Changing the text of a mounted `Note` is what a live region announces. Icons you pass as `icon` are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons.

motion.text: While `loading`, the text breathes with a slow `animate-pulse` that has `motion-reduce:animate-none`, and the net in `sutra.css` stops it too. The ring spinner keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: `loading` wins over the tone: a loading `Note` is never `alert`, whatever `tone` says, and it replaces `icon` with the spinner.
`tone` is `neutral` or `destructive`. The older `default`, `error` and `busy` still work (`busy` as a tone or a prop equals `loading`), but are deprecated.
`align` is `center` by default; `start` left-aligns the icon and text (it follows the writing direction, so it flips in RTL).

NumberInput.use: A numeric field with step buttons, arrow-key stepping, press-and-hold repeat, min and max, and locale-aware formatting and parsing (currency, percent, units). The value is a `number` or `null`, never a string.
instead: free text, or a native `type="number"` where the browser spinner is enough
a coarse value on a range

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves to and from the field; the step buttons are not tab stops (`tabIndex` -1)
Add or subtract `step`, clamped to `min` and `max`
Jump to `min` or `max`; with no bound set they move the caret as usual

keyboard.text: Pressing a step button with a pointer steps once, then repeats every 60 ms after 400 ms until release or a bound. Nothing here reads the Left and Right arrows, so RTL changes only the layout. Keys do nothing while the field is `disabled` or `readOnly`.

items: The field is a text input with `role="spinbutton"` and `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` (the formatted value, such as "$1,234.50"). They follow the committed value, not text still being typed.

The step buttons are named "Increase" and "Decrease" (`incrementLabel`, `decrementLabel`) and point at the field with `aria-controls`; use the arrow keys instead of tabbing to them. Icons are `aria-hidden`.
Name the field with a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`. `invalid`, `required`, `disabled` and `aria-describedby` are inherited from a surrounding `Field` unless you pass them.

motion.text: Static apart from colour transitions on the step buttons and the border, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The field renders on the server, but the display text is formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat` in the runtime's default locale unless you pass `locale`, so a server and a browser with different locales can show "1,234.5" against "1.234,5" and trigger a hydration warning. Pass `locale` to make both sides agree.

gotchas: `onValueChange` fires when a typed entry is committed (blur or Enter), and on each step, Home or End; it does not fire per keystroke. The native `onChange` prop is removed from the type.
`clampOnBlur` is on by default: a typed 42 with `max={10}` becomes 10 on blur. Turn it off to keep out-of-range text; stepping still clamps. Clearing the text commits `null`.

`precision` fixes the number of decimals shown and rounds values to it; without it up to three decimals show (more if `step` has more), and stepping rounds to the step's own decimals, so `0.1` plus `0.2` gives `0.3`.

Typed text is parsed with the locale's separators, native digits (Arabic-Indic, Persian) and currency or percent signs; a `percent` style stores a fraction (50 % is 0.5). `name` posts the raw number, not the formatted text.

Pagination.use: Page navigation for a list or table. Four layouts (`numbered`, `simple`, `dots`, `load-more`), an optional rows-per-page select, an opt-in `pageJump` field in the ellipsis and `PaginationStatus` for the "1–10 of 245" line.
instead: a fixed sequence of steps with progress
showing where the user is in a hierarchy

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves through previous, the page buttons, next and the rows-per-page select; disabled buttons are skipped
Activate the focused button: go to that page, or previous or next
In the jump field (`pageJump`): go to the typed page
In the jump field: cancel and return focus to the ellipsis; leaving the field cancels too

keyboard.text: There are no arrow-key shortcuts, so keys do not swap in RTL; the row flows in reading order and the previous and next arrows are mirrored. After a jump, focus moves to the button of the page it landed on. A disabled previous or next button is a real `disabled` button, so it leaves the tab order.

screenReaders.text: The root is a `<nav>` labelled "Pagination" (override with `aria-label`). Page buttons are named "Page 3" and the current one has `aria-current="page"`; previous and next are named "Previous page" and "Next page" whatever their visible text (pass your own `aria-label` if you change `children`). A plain ellipsis is `aria-hidden`; with `onJump` it is a button named "Jump to a page" (`jumpLabel`), and the field it opens is named "Go to page, 1 to N". In narrow containers the page list is replaced by "Page x of y" in an `aria-live="polite"` region. `PaginationStatus` is a polite live region too (`aria-busy` while `loading`, with an sr-only "Loading…" placeholder), so it announces the new row window after a page change.

motion.text: Mostly static. The `dots` indicator (each dot has a 24px hit area; neighbours are 14px apart, so the boxes overlap and the later dot wins the overlap) grows with a width transition and the button states fade; both end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The `loading` spinner on the load-more button keeps turning.

ssr.text: The pager renders plain markup on the server. Whether the page list or the "Page x of y" label shows depends on a container query (`@lg`) in CSS, not on JavaScript. `PaginationStatus` formats numbers with `Intl.NumberFormat`: without `locale` the server and the browser may use different default locales and print "1,245" and "1.245", so pass `locale` when rendering on a server.

slots: `pagination-ellipsis`: the span wrapping a clickable ellipsis (only with `onJump` or `pageJump`)
`pagination-jump`: the page field that replaces the ellipsis
gotchas: `totalPages` is a page count, not a row count; `page` is 1-based and is clamped to `1..totalPages`, and `onPageChange` is not called for the current page. Controlled use needs `page` and `onPageChange` together; otherwise it starts at `defaultPage`.
The page list is hidden below the `@lg` container width (32rem) and replaced by the "Page x of y" label, so narrow cards do not show page buttons. The `simple` variant always shows the label.
The rows-per-page select appears only with `pageSize` and a non-empty `pageSizeOptions`; `onPageSizeChange` just reports the choice, so update `pageSize` and usually reset `page` yourself.
`PaginationItem isActive` is a deprecated alias of `active`. In `load-more`, `page` is the number of pages loaded: the button advances `page` by one and is disabled on the last page.

Popover.use: A small floating panel anchored to a trigger, for filters, quick forms, pickers and rich details. It does not block the page. `PopoverContent` takes `size`, `padded` and `arrow`.
instead: a preview on hover or focus
the user must finish a task before going on
a single choice for a form field

head: Key
Action
rows: On the trigger (a native button): toggle the popover
Move through the panel; focus is not trapped, and moving it outside the panel closes it
Close and return focus to the trigger

keyboard.text: Focus moves into the panel when it opens and goes back to the trigger on close (not after a click outside). There are no arrow-key or direction-dependent keys, so RTL changes nothing. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `bottom`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the panel on a collision.

screenReaders.text: The trigger gets `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls`. The panel is `role="dialog"`. `PopoverTitle` and `PopoverDescription` (an `h3` and a `p`) name and describe the dialog: inside `PopoverContent` they get ids and the content sets `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby` while they are mounted. An `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` you pass to `PopoverContent` wins, and a popover without a title stays unnamed, so give it an `aria-label`. The arrow is decoration. An icon-only trigger needs `aria-label`.

motion.text: The panel fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade.

ssr.text: A closed popover renders only its trigger on server and client. The panel is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a popover that is `open` or `defaultOpen` on first render appears after hydration. The portalled panel is outside a subtree `dir` or `data-style`: set them on `<html>`, or pass `disablePortal` to keep it inside the subtree.

gotchas: It is non-modal by default (`modal` on `Popover` is false): the page stays interactive, outside clicks close it, and there is no focus trap. Pass `modal` for a trapped, `aria-hidden`-backed panel, but then consider a `Dialog`.
`size` defaults to `md` (18rem), `padded` to true (`p-4`). `PopoverHeader`, `PopoverBody` and `PopoverFooter` bring their own padding, so set `padded={false}` when you compose them.
Use `PopoverAnchor` to position against another element than the trigger; `PopoverClose asChild` closes from inside the panel.
`PopoverContent disablePortal` renders in place, which suits a popover inside a `Dialog` or `Sheet` with its own stacking; the default portal puts it in `<body>` at `z-50`.
Popover.example:
import { Button, Field, FieldLabel, Input, Popover, PopoverBody, PopoverClose, PopoverContent } from "@sutra/ui";
import { PopoverDescription, PopoverFooter, PopoverHeader, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@sutra/ui";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Invite teammate</Button>
      </PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent padded={false} align="start">
        <PopoverHeader>
          <PopoverTitle>Invite a teammate</PopoverTitle>
          <PopoverDescription>They get an email with a link to join.</PopoverDescription>
        </PopoverHeader>
        <PopoverBody>
          <Field>
            <FieldLabel>Email address</FieldLabel>
            <Input type="email" placeholder="name@company.com" />
          </Field>
        </PopoverBody>
        <PopoverFooter>
          <PopoverClose asChild>
            <Button size="sm">Send invite</Button>
          </PopoverClose>
        </PopoverFooter>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}

PortBadge.use: A small monospaced chip for a network port, optionally a link that opens it on localhost. `PortBadgeList` shows a row of them with a "+N" overflow.
instead: a port as one fact among others

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to the link, only when `href` is set (a plain badge is not focusable)

keyboard.text: No key depends on direction, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A linked badge is an `<a>` whose `aria-label` is "Open localhost:3000" (the URL without `http://`), which replaces the visible "3000" as its name. A plain badge is a `<span>` read as its text.

`PortBadgeList` is a `ul` with `aria-label` "Ports" (change it with `label`) and one `li` per badge. The "+N" chip is `aria-hidden`; a visually hidden "N more: 9001, 15672" is read instead, and the same ports are in its `title`.

motion.text: Static, apart from the hover fade on a linked badge, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup built from the props, with no browser API, so server and client output match.

slots: `port-badge`: the badge, which is the `<a>` for a linked badge and the `<span>` otherwise
gotchas: `href` is `true` for `http://localhost:<port>` (change the machine with `host`), or a string used as is. The link is plain HTTP and opens in a new tab (`target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`); `rel` is dropped if you change `target`.
A string `href` that fails `isSafeHref` (such as `javascript:`) is dropped silently and you get a plain, unlinked badge.

`tone` wins over `accent`; with neither, the badge follows the inherited accent or primary. `PortBadgeList` takes `accent` once on the list (a CSS variable that the badges inherit), `tone` on every badge.
`PortBadgeList` renders nothing for an empty `ports` array, and `max={0}` shows only the "+N" chip. A string port such as `":8080"` loses its leading colon, and `colon` adds one back to the text.

Progress.use: How far a task has got: a linear bar (determinate or indeterminate) with optional label and value, plus a ring (`ProgressCircle`) and a stepped bar (`ProgressSegments`).
instead: a level read against thresholds (disk, memory, quota)
work of unknown length with no bar
a placeholder for content that is loading
named stages with their own state

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: `Progress` is Radix's `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow`, plus `aria-valuetext` of the rounded percentage ("40%"). `label` names it through `aria-labelledby`; without a visible `label`, pass `aria-label` (it reaches the bar itself).
With no `value` (or `indeterminate`) there is no `aria-valuenow` and `data-state="indeterminate"`; announce what is happening in the name or nearby text, since no number is exposed.

`ProgressCircle` and `ProgressSegments` are `role="progressbar"` divs with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` (clamped) and `aria-label` from `label`. They have no `aria-valuetext`, so a ring reads its raw value against `max`. `ProgressSegments role="meter"` makes it a level (password strength); add `aria-valuetext` then.
`ProgressRingSvg` is `aria-hidden`; the wrapper that uses it carries the role.

motion.text: The determinate fill slides with a 500 ms transform, the ring arc with a stroke transition, and the segments fade with staggered delays; the first two have `motion-reduce:transition-none` and the net ends transitions in 1 ms. The indeterminate bar does not stop: the net slows its loop to 3 s because it carries meaning.

ssr.text: Renders on the server, but direction is read from the page after mount: the server paints left-to-right (the fill is hidden by a negative `translateX`), so on an RTL page the fill flips to the right side after hydration. `ProgressCircle` and `ProgressSegments` have no direction logic and match exactly.

gotchas: `value` is clamped to 0 to `max`; an out-of-range value never reaches Radix's console error. `max <= 0` reads as an empty bar. `showValue` is `true` (above next to the label, else on the right), `"top"` or `"right"`.

`formatValue` also sets `aria-valuetext` when it returns text or a number ("3 / 8 GB"), so the bar reads what it shows; a JSX result cannot be spoken, so the default percentage stays. Radix's `getValueLabel` or an explicit `aria-valuetext` overrides it.
When there is a `label` or a shown value, the bar sits in a wrapper: `className` then styles the wrapper, not the track (use `indicatorClassName` for the fill).
`ProgressCircle` has no indeterminate state; use `Spinner` for that. Its centre text is `children`, or the percentage unless `showValue={false}`.

RadioGroup.use: Exactly one choice from a few options that should all stay visible. Compose `RadioGroupItem`, `RadioField` (with label and description) and `RadioCard` (a selectable card) inside `RadioGroup`, or pass `options` to `RadioGroupField`.
instead: the list is long or space is tight
two to four options that switch a view

head: Key
Action
rows: Enters the group on the checked radio (the first one when none is checked) and leaves it; the other radios are skipped
`orientation="vertical"` (the default): move to the next or previous radio, loop at the ends, and select it
`orientation="horizontal"`: the same; the other axis does nothing

keyboard.text: Enter does nothing (Radix cancels it). Disabled radios are skipped. In RTL with `orientation="horizontal"`, ArrowLeft goes to the next radio and ArrowRight to the previous; vertical groups do not change. The group reads the direction from its parent, so a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>` all work.

items: The group is `role="radiogroup"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-required` from `required`; each item is a `<button role="radio">` with `aria-checked`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on the group, and a surrounding `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required`.

The group has no name of its own. `RadioGroupField` names it from `label` through `aria-labelledby` and links `description` with `aria-describedby`; for a bare `RadioGroup` pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
`RadioField` and `RadioCard` name each radio through `<label htmlFor>` and announce the description through `aria-describedby`. A bare `RadioGroupItem` needs `aria-label`.

motion.text: The dot scales in with a spring transition (`ease-spring`) and the item scales on press; the reduced-motion net ends both in 1 ms, so the dot appears at once.

ssr.text: Items and the group render on the server, including `value` and `defaultValue`. The group writes a `dir` attribute that is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles to the page direction after hydration, which only shows on an RTL page.

slots: `radio-group`: the group; `radio-group-field`: the wrapper around label, description and group
`radio-field`: the row of radio, label and description
gotchas: Arrow keys select as well as move focus; there is no "focus without selecting". Use `value` and `onValueChange` (a string) to control it, and `name` on the group so a native form posts it.
`RadioGroupField` renders `variant="card"` with auto-fit columns when horizontal; the default variant is a plain list. Both take `size` (`sm` or `md`) for every option.
Each `RadioGroupItem` needs a `value`; an item with no label has no name unless you pass `aria-label`.
`RadioCard` moves the focus ring from the dot to the whole card. `disabled` on the group disables every item.

Rating.use: A star rating input from 0 to `max` with hover preview, optional half steps and radiogroup keyboard support. With `readOnly` or `disabled` it is a static display of a score; `RatingSummary` adds the average, the count and a 5 to 1 distribution.
instead: a value on a continuous range

head: Key
Action
rows: One tab stop: the checked star (the first star when there is no rating)
Add one star (half a star with `allowHalf`)
Remove one star; below the first step it goes to 0, or stops at one step with `allowClear={false}`
Set that rating, up to `max` (0 only with `allowClear`)

keyboard.text: Every key sets the value at once and moves focus to the matching star. Space and Enter do nothing. In RTL the stars run right to left, so ArrowLeft adds and ArrowRight removes (the key towards the inline end always adds); Up and Down do not change. A `readOnly` or `disabled` rating is not focusable.

items: Interactive: a `role="radiogroup"` of `role="radio"` stars with `aria-checked`, each named "N stars out of M" (`getLabel` changes the wording; with `allowHalf` the checked star carries the half value, such as "2.5 stars out of 5"). The group has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
`readOnly` and `disabled`: a single `role="img"` named "Rated N out of M" (a given `aria-label` replaces it), with `aria-disabled` when disabled. The star icons are `aria-hidden`.

`RatingSummary` shows the average as text, a read-only `Rating` rounded to the nearest half, and a list named "Rating distribution" whose rows are `role="meter"` named "5 star" to "1 star" with the percentage as the value.

motion.text: The star under the pointer scales up (`hover:scale-110`), presses down, and the fill width eases over 150 ms; the distribution bars ease over 500 ms. All are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API at render time: the fill comes from `value` or `defaultValue`, the hover preview exists only after a pointer move, and the direction is read from the DOM when a key or click happens. Server and client output match.

gotchas: `allowClear` is on by default: clicking the selected star again sets 0, and so do Delete, Backspace and `0`. With `allowClear={false}` a rating of one or more cannot go back to 0; an unrated control can still be rated.
With `allowHalf`, a click on the half of a star nearer the inline start sets the half value, and that half flips in RTL.
`onValueChange` receives a number (0 for cleared). `name` posts the number through a hidden input; `value` and `defaultValue` are numbers up to `max`.
`icon` swaps the star glyph, and `activeClassName` and `inactiveClassName` replace the amber fill and grey outline colours instead of adding to them.

ReorderableList.use: A list whose rows the user can reorder by dragging a handle, by picking a row up with the keyboard, or with optional up and down buttons, with live announcements. You render each row; the list reports the new order after every move. `Checklist` builds a subtask list on it.
instead: items that appear and disappear but are not reordered by the user
sortable columns rather than a manual order
the move helpers without the list UI

head: Key
Action
rows: Each row's handle is a tab stop (the handle is a button)
On a handle: pick the row up. While it is picked up: drop it where it is
While picked up: move the row one place; it stops at the ends
While picked up: cancel and put the row back
On a move button ("Move X up" or "down", with `moveButtons`): move one place at once

keyboard.text: Leaving the handle (blur) while a row is picked up drops it where it is. The arrows are vertical, so nothing changes in RTL. Move buttons are disabled at the ends, while another row is picked up, and with `disabled`.

items: The list is a `ul` named by `label` (default "Reorderable list"). Each handle is a button named "Reorder <label of the item>" with `aria-pressed` while picked up and `aria-describedby` pointing at hidden instructions ("Press Space to pick up. Use the up and down arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel.").

An assertive `role="status"` region announces each step: "Picked up Bravo. Position 2 of 5. ...", "Moved Bravo to position 3 of 5.", "Dropped Bravo at position 3 of 5." or "Reorder canceled. Bravo returned to position 2 of 5." Buttons announce their move too.
The names come from `getLabel`; the default `String(item)` reads "[object Object]" for objects, so pass `getLabel`. The floating copy shown while dragging with a pointer is `aria-hidden`.

motion.text: With `flip` (default true) rows glide to their new place when the order changes and a dropped row settles from where it was released; under `prefers-reduced-motion` that is off and rows jump. The drag copy fades in with a short `animate-in` that the global net strips of movement.

ssr.text: The list renders from `items` with plain markup (no browser API at render), so the server HTML is the full list. Drag and keyboard state only exist after interaction.

gotchas: `items` is the source of truth: `onReorder(next, { from, to })` is called once, on drop (or per button press), and only if the position changed. Keep `items` in your state and set it from `next`. While a row is picked up the list shows its own working order.
`getKey` must return a stable unique string per item. It is the React key and what the focus and the announcements follow.
`handle={false}` removes the only drag and keyboard control, so combine it with `moveButtons`. `moveButtons` is off by default.
It is a generic function component: `ref` is a plain prop (it reaches the `ul`), not a `forwardRef`. `reorderArray`, `reorderBy` and `useReorder` are exported from the same module for the data side.

SchemaForm.use: A settings form generated from a JSON-Schema-like object: typed controls, nested sections, array fields with add and remove, validation, section navigation with search, and either an explicit Save button or debounced autosave with per-field status. `NestedValueEditor` edits one schema value on its own.
instead: hand-built forms with your own controls and layout
a ready-made form for one known shape

head: Key
Action
rows: Through the controls in document order: the search field and section buttons first (when shown), then each field, array buttons, Save
In a text field: submits the form when `onSubmit` is set (native form behaviour)
Toggles a switch; the other controls keep their own keys (arrows on a segmented control, the select list keys)

keyboard.text: There are no custom keys, and the layout uses logical sides, so RTL changes nothing.

items: Each field has a real `<label>`; a required one adds a hidden-from-AT asterisk and `aria-required`. Descriptions and errors are linked with `aria-describedby`, and an invalid field has `aria-invalid`. Error text and the "Saving…", "Saved" and "Not saved" marks are plain text, not live regions.

Objects are `fieldset`s with a `legend`, arrays are `group`s named by the label (with a count) whose items have "Remove Tag 1" buttons, and top-level sections are `section`s named by an `h3`. The navigation is a `nav` named "Sections", with `aria-current` on the chosen button and a hidden " errors" count after submit.
After a failed submit a `role="alert"` says "Fix 2 fields to continue". A field with `x-disabled-reason` or `disabledFields` is disabled and shows the reason as text with a lock icon.

motion.text: Only the "Saved" tick pops (`animate-pop`), which the global net stops, and the controls carry their own transitions (ended in 1 ms).

ssr.text: The form renders in full from the schema and value, with ids from `useSafeId`; nothing depends on the browser until you type. Autosave timers start on the first edit.

gotchas: Control type follows the schema: boolean is a switch; an `enum` of three or fewer is a segmented control, more is a select; `number` and `integer` use a number input; `format: "password"` or `x-secret` masks; `format: "textarea"` is a textarea; `email` and `uri` set the input type. An emptied field removes its key from the value.

Errors show for a field only after it was blurred, edited under autosave, or after the first submit (or all at once with `validateOnMount`). Empty values skip every rule except `required`, which is a list on the parent object. `uri` accepts only `http(s)` URLs, and an invalid `pattern` never fails.

Autosave (`autosave`, `onSave(value, changedKeys)`) waits `autosaveDelay` (800 ms) after the last edit and saves only the changed top-level keys that are valid; invalid ones are skipped. Throwing from `onSave` marks them "Not saved". Status shows beside top-level fields and arrays, not on a nested object section.

`onSubmit` runs only when the value is valid, and the button shows a spinner while its promise is pending. Without `onSubmit` (or with `autosave`) there is no Save button. Navigation and search appear above `navThreshold` (8) top-level fields or with more than two sections (`x-category`, or an object's title, else "General"). `onChange` is a deprecated alias of `onValueChange`.

ScrollArea.use: A scrolling region with thin overlay scrollbars that match the theme, optional edge fades and a ref to the viewport. Scrolling stays native (wheel, touch, keyboard). A plain `overflow-auto scrollbar-thin` element is enough when only a thin native scrollbar is needed.
instead: paged or snapping content that moves in steps

keyboard.text: No keys of its own: the viewport is the real scroller, so the browser's scrolling keys work whenever focus is inside it (on a focusable child, or on the viewport itself), and the viewport gets `tabindex="0"` while its content overflows (measured after mount and on resize), so a keyboard user can focus it and scroll; content that fits adds no tab stop. The custom scrollbars and thumbs are for the pointer only and are not focusable. Nothing swaps in RTL.

screenReaders.text: Adds no state: the content reads in its normal order and the scrollbars are not exposed. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when the region needs a name: they go on the viewport, which then has `role="region"` (without a name it has no role). The edge fades are a visual mask only.

motion.text: The scrollbar fades in and out (`animate-in` and `animate-out` fades) and the thumb colour is a transition; the reduced-motion net ends the transitions in 1 ms and the fade stays. Scrolling itself is native and not affected. The scrollbar hides after Radix's `scrollHideDelay` of 600 ms, a timer.

ssr.text: The server renders the root and the viewport with the content. With the default `type="hover"` the scrollbars do not exist until the pointer enters after mount, `fadeEdges` shows no fades until the edges are measured in an effect, and the root `dir` is read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so the first server paint of an RTL page has `dir="ltr"` on the area.

gotchas: Give it a bounded size: the root is `overflow-hidden`, so without a height (`className="h-64"`) or a `max-h` (`viewportClassName`) it grows with its content and nothing scrolls.

`orientation` decides which axes scroll at all: Radix sets `overflow: hidden` on the axis without a scrollbar, so `orientation="vertical"` (the default) clips horizontal overflow and `"horizontal"` clips vertical overflow. Use `"both"` for two-way scrolling.

Radix wraps the children in a `display: table; min-width: 100%` div, so long unbroken text or wide content widens the area (that is what makes horizontal scrolling work) instead of wrapping or truncating.

`type` is a Radix prop (default `"hover"`; also `auto`, `always`, `scroll`). `viewportRef` is the element to `scrollTo` or attach scroll listeners to; the root `ref` is not the scroller. `fadeEdges` takes `true`, `"vertical"` or `"horizontal"` and fades only the edges that still have content beyond them.

SearchTrigger.use: A button that looks like a search field, with placeholder text and the shortcut as key chips ("Ctrl K", or the command key on macOS). Clicking it, or pressing the shortcut when `hotkey` is on, calls `onTrigger`, where you open your command palette.
instead: a real text field you type into
a search field that filters a list in place
pick a value from a searchable list

head: Key
Action
rows: Press it: calls `onClick`, then `onTrigger` (not if `onClick` calls `preventDefault`)
With `hotkey`, calls `onTrigger` from anywhere on the page and stops the browser's own handling

keyboard.text: A `mod+` chord also fires while typing in an input, a textarea or an editable element; a plain key such as `/` is ignored there and fires elsewhere. On macOS `mod` is the command key and Ctrl is ignored. Nothing depends on arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing.

items: It is a native `button` named by `label`, else by the placeholder text ("Search…"). The search icon and the key chips are `aria-hidden`, so the shortcut does not become part of the name.
The shortcut is exposed as a description ("Shortcut: Control K", from a single combination, not for key sequences) and through `aria-keyshortcuts` ("Meta+K Control+K").
With `collapseBelow`, an icon-only button named `label` or "Search" replaces the field below that breakpoint; both exist in the page and CSS hides one.

motion.text: Only a colour and border transition on hover, which the global net ends within 1 ms. Static otherwise.

ssr.text: The shortcut chips depend on the platform: the server and the hydrating client render the non-Mac labels ("Ctrl") and a Mac browser switches to the command key right after hydration, before paint, so the markup matches. Inside a `ShortcutProvider` with a `platform` prop that platform is used from the first render on both sides. The hotkey listener is attached in an effect.

gotchas: It opens nothing itself: `onTrigger` (also called by the hotkey) is where you set your palette's `open`. Pair it with `CommandDialog` by setting its `open` in `onTrigger`.
`hotkey` defaults to off, so the chips are only a hint until you turn it on. Inside a `ShortcutProvider` it registers as "Search" in the shortcut registry; otherwise it listens on `document`.
`shortcut` is a keys spec (`"mod+k"`, `"/"`, `"g t"`); the same value draws the chips and sets the hotkey.
The field has `max-w-72` and takes the full width up to it; `size` is `sm` 32 px, `md` 36 px (default) or `lg` 40 px, and `className` is merged last.

SectionRail.use: A table of contents that highlights the section in view, as an "On this page" column or a scrolling row of tabs for a sticky sub-navigation. The links are real anchors; a click scrolls the section to the top. `useScrollSections` is the tracking behind it.
instead: where you are in a site hierarchy
a nested hierarchy you expand and select

head: Key
Action
rows: Each link is a tab stop (there is no roving focus)
Follows the link: scrolls the section to the top, marks it current and updates the address bar

keyboard.text: Space does nothing on a link, and there are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing for the keyboard. A click does not move focus to the section: it stays on the link.

items: A `nav` named by `label` (default "Table of contents") with a list of links. The current one has `aria-current="location"`. The "On this page" title is plain text, not a heading.
With `loading` the nav is `aria-busy` with one hidden "Loading…" and `aria-hidden` placeholder rows: no links exist until the sections are known.
The active mark is the only state; nothing is announced when it moves as you scroll.

motion.text: Clicks scroll smoothly (`smoothScroll`, default true) but jump under `prefers-reduced-motion`, read when you click. The horizontal rail also re-centres the active tab with an instant scroll then. Link colour changes are transitions that the global net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The first render is the same on the server and client: the active section is `value`, `defaultValue` or the first id. Tracking starts in an effect after mount.

gotchas: Each section needs an element with the matching `id` that is already in the page when the rail mounts or when the ids change; missing ones are skipped. Add `scroll-margin-top` to the targets when a fixed header covers them, and pass `root` when the sections scroll inside a container rather than the page.

Tracking marks the first listed section that is in the top third of the scroller (`offset` shifts it down by a header's height, `rootMargin` replaces the rule) and keeps the last one while none is. `value` makes it controlled and turns tracking off, yet a click still scrolls and calls `onValueChange`.

A plain click scrolls with `scrollIntoView` and writes the link to the address bar with `replaceState`, so Back does not undo it; use `getHref` to give router URLs where `#id` is taken. Modified clicks (Ctrl, Cmd, Shift, Alt, middle button) and `smoothScroll={false}` leave the browser's own anchor jump.
`level` (2 to 4) indents deeper entries relative to the shallowest one, in the vertical rail only. With no sections it renders nothing unless you give `emptyState`.

SegmentedControl.use: One choice from two to four short options that switch a view or a mode, drawn as a pill with a sliding thumb. Pass `options`, or compose `SegmentedControlItem` children; icon-only segments are square.
instead: options need descriptions or must read as a form field
more than a handful of options
the choice swaps panels of content
loose on/off buttons that can all be off

head: Key
Action
rows: One tab stop: the selected segment (the first one when none is selected)
