Move focus to the next or previous enabled segment, looping at the ends
Focus the first or last segment

keyboard.text: Arrow keys move focus only; selecting needs Enter or Space. In RTL the horizontal arrows swap (ArrowLeft goes to the next segment), because Radix roving focus reads the `dir` that the control passes down: a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`, or a `dir` you set yourself.

items: The root is `role="radiogroup"` and each segment is a `role="radio"` button with `aria-checked`. The group has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
A segment is named by its label text. An icon-only segment has no text, so give it `aria-label` (an `options` entry takes `"aria-label"`). The sliding thumb is `aria-hidden`.
Disabled segments are skipped by focus.

motion.text: The thumb slides with a 300 ms transform transition and the label colours fade in 200 ms; the reduced-motion net ends both in 1 ms, so the thumb jumps. The thumb never animates on the first frame, it appears in place.

ssr.text: The segments render on the server with the selected one marked, but the thumb behind it is measured after mount, so the server HTML shows the selection by text colour only and the pill appears on hydration. The group's `dir` is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL page.

gotchas: It is a single-select that never deselects: clicking the selected segment keeps it, and `onValueChange` does not fire for it (it receives a string, never an empty one).
With `options` and no `value` or `defaultValue` the first option is selected; with `SegmentedControlItem` children and no `defaultValue` nothing is selected until the user picks.
The root has `overflow-x-auto` and `max-w-full`, so many options scroll sideways in a narrow column instead of overflowing. `fullWidth` stretches the root and splits the segments evenly.
Extra props (including `dir`, `disabled`, `loop`) go to the Radix root; a `dir` you pass overrides the detected direction.

Select.use: A single choice from a short list, shown as an input-like trigger and a floating listbox. `SimpleSelect` takes an `options` array, the compound parts give full control.
instead: the list is long, searchable or loaded from a server
two to four options that switch a view

head: Key
Action
rows: On the trigger: open the list
On the closed trigger, selects the next matching option; in the open list, moves to it
Highlight the first or last option
Pick the highlighted option and close
Does nothing while the list is open (Radix blocks it), so close first

keyboard.text: The list is vertical, so the arrow keys do not swap in RTL. The `dir` of the root follows the document or the nearest `DirectionProvider`, so the popover opens on the correct side.

screenReaders.text: The trigger is a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox` of `option`s with the selected one marked. `SelectGroup` plus `SelectLabel` announce the group name. `SimpleSelect` forwards `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` to the trigger and reads `invalid`, `disabled`, `required` and `id` from a surrounding `Field`, which also sets `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`. A select with no visible label needs an `aria-label`.

motion.text: The popover fades and zooms in from the trigger with the `animate-in` utilities and the chevron turns with `chevron-turn`; under reduced motion the net removes the zoom and slide (the fade stays) and the chevron turn ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The trigger renders on the server, but the option list lives in a fragment created after mount, so a select that starts with a `value` or `defaultValue` shows an empty trigger (or the placeholder) in the server HTML and the selected label appears after hydration. Reserve the trigger width with `className` to avoid a jump.

gotchas: Radix Select needs a non-empty string for every item `value`; an empty string is reserved for clearing back to the placeholder.
`SelectContent` uses `position="popper"`, `sideOffset` 6 and the trigger width by default; pass `position="item-aligned"` for the native-style overlap, which then ignores `sideOffset`.
`SelectItem description` shows only in the list: the trigger shows the item's own text (and `icon`).
Inside a `<form>`, give the root a `name` so Radix renders its hidden native `<select>`; `required` and `disabled` go on the root or on `Field`.

Separator.use: A horizontal or vertical rule, solid or dashed, optionally with a label in the line ("OR", "Section"). `ContentDivider` is the deprecated alias of the same component.

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: Decorative by default: `decorative` is `true`, so the element is `role="none"` and assistive technology skips it. This is the opposite of the Radix default. Pass `decorative={false}` for a real `role="separator"` between regions of content; a vertical one then also gets `aria-orientation="vertical"` (horizontal is the implicit default and is not written).
A `label` (or `children`) is ordinary text and is read by screen readers whether or not the line is decorative.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: A vertical separator has no height of its own: it stretches to the row it sits in (`self-stretch`), so put it in a flex row. A `className` with an `h-` or `size-` class switches it to a fixed height centred in the row instead.
With a label, `labelPosition` is `center` (default), `start` or `end`; the short side of the line is a stub (1rem, or 0.5rem when vertical). A vertical labelled separator is at least 4rem tall.
`variant="dashed"` only changes the line style. The line colour is the `border` token; override with a `border-*` class.
`ContentDivider` is the same object as `Separator`; use `Separator` in new code.

Sheet.use: A modal panel that slides in from an edge (right by default) and keeps the page visible behind a scrim, for detail, filter, settings and navigation panels. Sizes, `detached` and `blur` looks, logical `start` and `end` sides, and stacked nested sheets.
instead: a centred modal for one decision or task
a touch-first bottom sheet you drag with snap points
a small panel that does not block the page
content that expands in the page instead of overlaying it

head: Key
Action
rows: Cycle focus inside the sheet (trapped while open)
Activate the focused button, including the close button

keyboard.text: Focus moves into the sheet on open and returns to whatever had it before, even when it was opened without a `SheetTrigger` (a hotkey, controlled `open`). There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. With stacked sheets Escape closes only the topmost.

screenReaders.text: The panel is a Radix dialog: `role="dialog"` with `aria-labelledby` from `SheetTitle` and `aria-describedby` from `SheetDescription`, and the page behind is hidden from assistive technology while it is open. Always render a `SheetTitle` (it may be visually hidden). The built-in close button is labelled "Close" and appears when `dismissible` is true (or with `showClose`).

motion.text: The panel slides in from its edge and the sheet underneath a nested one scales down and fades; the reduced-motion net removes the slide, keeps the fade and ends the scale and opacity transition in 1 ms.

ssr.text: A closed sheet renders only its trigger on the server and the client. The panel is portalled into `<body>` after mount, so a sheet that is `open` on first render appears after hydration. Being portalled, it does not sit inside a subtree `dir` or `data-style`: the `start` and `end` sides and the `rtl:` flips read `<html dir>`, so set it there.

slots: `sheet-content`: the panel (`data-side`, plus `data-detached` and `data-nested` when set)
gotchas: `side` accepts `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom` (fixed edges) and `start`, `end` (follow the document direction, so `start` is the right edge in RTL). Prefer `start` and `end` for side navigation.

`size` is a width for side sheets and a height for `top` and `bottom` (`auto`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `half`, `full`); without it a side sheet is 24rem wide (up to 85vw) and a top or bottom sheet is as tall as its content. `className` still wins over it.

`dismissible={false}` ignores Escape and outside clicks and hides the close button, so give users another way out (`showClose` brings the button back; a `SheetClose` or controlled `open` also closes it).

Nested sheets stack only when the inner `Sheet` is rendered inside the outer `SheetContent`; the one underneath gets `data-nested`. `Sheet` is the Radix Dialog root, so `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` and `modal` work as in `Dialog`.
Sheet.example:
import { Button, Field, FieldLabel, Input, Sheet, SheetBody, SheetClose, SheetContent } from "@sutra/ui";
import { SheetDescription, SheetFooter, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@sutra/ui";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Sheet>
      <SheetTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Filters</Button>
      </SheetTrigger>
      <SheetContent side="end" size="md">
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle>Filter orders</SheetTitle>
          <SheetDescription>Narrow the list down to one customer.</SheetDescription>
        </SheetHeader>
        <SheetBody>
          <Field>
            <FieldLabel>Customer</FieldLabel>
            <Input placeholder="Name or email" />
          </Field>
        </SheetBody>
        <SheetFooter>
          <SheetClose asChild>
            <Button>Apply filters</Button>
          </SheetClose>
        </SheetFooter>
      </SheetContent>
    </Sheet>
  );
}

ShortcutKeys.use: Renders a key spec ("mod+k", "shift+?", "g t") as platform-aware key chips, with "then" between the steps of a sequence. It is display only.
instead: a single key chip you write yourself
a help sheet listing the live shortcuts
the hint at the end of a command item

keyboard.text: Not focusable, and it does not listen for the keys it shows: pair it with `useShortcut` or `ShortcutProvider` to make the shortcut work.

screenReaders.text: The chips are `aria-hidden` and a visually hidden sentence is read instead, spelled out per platform: "Shift Command K" for `mod+shift+k` on a Mac, and a sequence reads "G then T". The glyphs (command, shift, option) are therefore never read aloud. The root is a plain `span` with `data-shortcut` set to the spec.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: The server has no `navigator` and uses the non-Mac labels ("Ctrl", "Shift"). The hydrating client render uses the same default, so the markup matches, and a Mac browser switches to the glyphs (command, option) right after hydration, before paint. A client-only render detects the platform at once. Pass `platform` (or set it on a `ShortcutProvider`, which `ShortcutKeys` reads) to make the first render already right.

gotchas: `keys` is a spec, not display text: `mod` means Command on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, a space separates the steps of a sequence ("g t"), and `+` joins keys that are held together. A string of ready-made glyphs ("⌘K") is not a spec; render it in `Kbd` yourself.
`platform` is `mac` or `other`; without it the platform comes from the nearest `ShortcutProvider`, else from the browser. `size` is `sm` or `md`, and `kbdClassName` styles each chip.
Each chip is a `Kbd`, so it renders a real `<kbd>` element; it is hidden from assistive technology here only because the spoken sentence replaces it.

Skeleton.use: A loading placeholder shaped like the content to come: text lines, a circle or a rectangle, with a shimmer sweep or a pulse.
instead: a short wait with no content shape
a level that is not loading

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: Every skeleton is `aria-hidden`, so it is invisible to assistive technology. Announce the wait yourself: set `aria-busy="true"` on the region being loaded, and add visually hidden text ("Loading profile…") or a status message, as the loading states of `Meter` and `BatteryLevel` do.

motion.text: The shimmer (`animate-shimmer`) and the pulse both carry `motion-reduce:animate-none`, so a skeleton is a still muted block.

ssr.text: Plain `div` markup with no browser API, so server and client output match, which makes skeletons the right fallback for streamed content.

gotchas: `shape` defaults to `"rect"` (96 px tall, full width). `"circle"` is 40 px unless you pass `width` (the height follows the width); `"text"` is one line high.
`lines` only applies to `shape="text"` and makes a stack with a shorter last line (60 percent wide); the wrapper takes `width`, the lines take `height`.
`shimmer={false}` swaps the sweep for `animate-pulse`.
`width` and `height` accept a number (px) or any CSS length, and they win over `className` sizes because they are inline styles.

SlideToConfirm.use: Confirms an irreversible or deliberate action by sliding a thumb along a track. A `role="slider"` with arrow, Home, End, Enter and Space keys, a drag that follows the finger, and a spring back when released early.
instead: the action can be reversed for a few seconds
a plain yes or no in a dialog

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the thumb (the slider). It is skipped when `disabled`
Move forward by `step` percent (default 10); reaching 100 confirms
Move back by `step` percent, down to 0

keyboard.text: Keys with Alt, Ctrl or Meta held are ignored, and so are all keys once the control is `disabled`, `loading`, busy or confirmed. In RTL the thumb starts at the right and travels left, and ArrowLeft is the forward key and ArrowRight the back key (the test pins it); ArrowUp and ArrowDown do not swap.

items: The thumb is the `role="slider"` (`aria-valuemin` 0, `aria-valuemax` 100, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-orientation="horizontal"`), named through `aria-labelledby` by the visible hint, "Slide to confirm" unless `label` changes it. The hint text switches to `loadingLabel` and then `confirmedLabel`, so the name follows the state.
At the end it sets `aria-valuetext` to `confirmedLabel` or `loadingLabel`. The root gets `aria-busy` while loading and `aria-disabled` when disabled.
A visually hidden `role="status"` says `confirmedLabel` once the control is confirmed and no longer busy.
The fill and the thumb icon are `aria-hidden`; the spinner in the thumb is decorative.

motion.text: There are no CSS transitions: the thumb and the fill follow a CSS variable that the drag writes, and the settle after a release or a key press is a spring from `useDrag`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` that spring is skipped and the thumb snaps straight to its place.

ssr.text: The server renders the track and the thumb at the start edge, because the width is measured after mount and the position is applied in an effect. `defaultConfirmed` or `confirmed` marks it confirmed in the markup (value 100, check icon) while the thumb jumps to the end after hydration. Direction is read as `ltr` on the server.

slots: `slide-to-confirm-fill`: the tinted fill behind the thumb
`slide-to-confirm-label`: the hint text, which fades as the thumb moves
gotchas: Only the thumb starts a drag; pressing on the track does nothing. A release confirms from 90 percent of the travel, and speed alone never confirms. Vertical scrolling is left to the browser (`touch-action` is set for you).

`onConfirm` may return a promise: the control stays busy until it settles and slides back if it rejects. A synchronous throw also slides it back and then rethrows. A resolved promise leaves it confirmed.

Once confirmed it is locked at the end (keys and drags are ignored) until you pass `confirmed={false}`; `onConfirmedChange` reports both changes. `loading` shows the end position and a spinner without calling `onConfirm`.
With a controlled `confirmed` that stays `false`, `onConfirm` still runs on a confirm gesture and then the thumb slides back home.

Slider.use: Pick a number, or a range with two thumbs, by dragging along a track. The value is always an array (`[40]`, or `[10, 80]` for `RangeSlider`). It has an optional value bubble, tick marks, `accent` and `tone` colours, and a vertical orientation.
instead: an exact number is typed or stepped
a slider with a mute toggle and level readout
a level the user cannot change

head: Key
Action
rows: Each thumb is a tab stop
Raise the focused thumb by one `step`
Move ten steps (PageUp raises, PageDown lowers)
Set the first thumb to `min` and the last thumb to `max`, whichever thumb has focus

keyboard.text: In RTL on a horizontal slider ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers, and the track fills from the right; Up and Down do not change. The direction is read from the parent (a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`), and a `dir` you pass wins. Thumbs keep a minimum gap of `minStepsBetweenThumbs` steps (1 for `RangeSlider`).

items: Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-orientation`. A single thumb is named by `thumbLabels` (such as `["Volume"]`), else by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on the `Slider`, else by a surrounding `FieldLabel`; two thumbs are named "Minimum" and "Maximum" by default (an `aria-label` on the `Slider` then becomes a `role="group"` around them), more are "Value 1 of 3" and so on. `getValueText` sets `aria-valuetext` per thumb, for example `(v) => v + "%"`.

`id` stays on the Radix root `span` (which has no role), so a `FieldLabel` click does not focus a thumb. The slider reads `Field`: its id, `disabled`, invalid state and description, hint and error ids (`aria-describedby`, also on every thumb); an explicit prop wins.

The value bubble and the tick marks and their labels are `aria-hidden`; put what matters in `getValueText`. `invalid` (or an invalid `Field`) sets `aria-invalid` on the root and on each thumb and turns the range red.

motion.text: The thumb ring, press scale and value bubble use short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The track and range render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`, but each thumb is `display: none` until Radix has mounted and located it, so the thumbs appear after hydration. The direction is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration on an RTL page.

gotchas: `value` and `defaultValue` are arrays, and `onValueChange` receives the whole array. `onValueCommit` fires when a drag or key press ends.

`ref` and `className` go to the outer wrapper (which also holds the marks); every other prop, including `disabled`, `step`, `name` and `orientation`, goes to the Radix root inside it. `name` posts one hidden input per thumb (named `name[]` for a range) inside a form.
`showValue` shows the bubble on hover, focus and drag; `"always"` keeps it. `marks` take numbers or `{ value, label }` and only mark; they do not snap the value (use `step`).
A given `tone` beats `accent`, and `invalid` beats both.

SocialButton.use: A sign-in button with the logo of an identity provider. `provider` picks one of eleven (google, apple, github, microsoft, x, facebook, linkedin, discord, slack, figma, gitlab) and the label defaults to "Continue with <Provider>".
instead: a normal action with your own label and icon
sign in with kunji, which has its own brand rules
the sign-in is a link in running text

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` or `loading` button is not focusable

keyboard.text: With `asChild` the child keeps its own keyboard behaviour: a link activates on Enter only. No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

items: A native `<button>` with `type="button"` unless you pass `type`; the name is its text, "Continue with GitHub" by default, or your `children`.
`variant="icon"` shows only the logo and ignores `children`: its `aria-label` defaults to "Continue with <Provider>" and you can pass your own.
The provider logos are `aria-hidden`.
`loading` sets `aria-busy="true"` and disables the button. The spinner keeps its own default "Loading" status label.

motion.text: The press effect (`active:scale-[0.98]`) and the colour fades are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms. The `loading` spinner keeps turning, as a progress indicator does.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The logos are inline SVG or icon components.

gotchas: With `asChild`, `disabled` and `loading` cannot set the native `disabled` on the child (often a link), so, like `Button asChild`, the child gets `aria-disabled="true"`, `data-disabled`, `tabindex="-1"` and its clicks are swallowed in the capture phase; `loading` also sets `aria-busy` and swaps the logo for a spinner.

`variant="brand"` paints the provider's own colours as fixed values (white for Google, black for Apple, and so on), so it does not follow the theme or `data-style`; the `default` (outlined) and `icon` variants do. `fullWidth` is ignored for `variant="icon"`.
`children` replaces the whole label, including the provider name: the default text is only used when there are no `children`. The label is English unless you pass `children`.
The element carries `data-provider` with the provider key, which is handy for tests and analytics.

Sparkline.use: A tiny inline trend with no axes, as a line, a filled area or bars, for a table cell, a stat tile or a list row. `SparkBar` is the bar form on its own; `type="bar"` hands over to it.
instead: a chart with axes, tooltip and a data table
a number with a built-in trend
a level against a limit rather than a history

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. There is no tooltip or point selection.

items: The SVG is `role="img"` with an `aria-label`: `label` when given, otherwise "Trend from 3 to 9" (first and last value; "No data" for an empty array). `SparkBar` defaults to "5 values, latest 9".
That is all a screen reader gets: there is no data table. Pass a `label` that says what the numbers are ("Requests per minute, last hour") and show the current value as real text beside it.
The `highlightLast` dot is `aria-hidden` decoration.

motion.text: Line and area charts do not animate. `SparkBar` bars change height and position with a 300 ms transition when data changes, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Pure SVG computed from `data`, `width` and `height`, with an id from `useId` for the area gradient; the server and client markup are the same.

gotchas: A line or area scales to the range of its data (`min` and `max` override), so a flat series fills the box and a tiny change looks large. `type="bar"` always includes 0 on its scale, so the same data looks different; set `min` and `max` on both to compare them.

Colour precedence is `tone`, then `color`, then `accent`; `trend` (green when the last value is at least the first, red otherwise) only applies when none of the three is set. A token name such as `"success"` works in `color`.

With `responsive` the SVG stretches to the container width (`preserveAspectRatio="none"`, strokes keep their width) and `width` only sets the viewBox; without it the box is `width` by `height` (default 120 by 32). Both charts are left-to-right islands (`dir="ltr"` on the wrapper, like the other charts): the series starts at the physical left and the `highlightLast` dot sits on the last point, also on an RTL page.

`type="bar"` ignores `smooth`, `strokeWidth` and `gradient`; `mutedColor`, `gap` and `radius` are props of `SparkBar` only, so render it directly to set them. `highlightLast` is the dot on a line and the full-colour bar on bars.

Spinner.use: The loading indicator. Five looks (`ring`, `dots`, `bars`, `pulse` and `glyph`, a cycling text character) in five sizes, drawn in the current text colour.
instead: a placeholder in the shape of content that is loading
the text-glyph look as a component of its own, with `variant` instead of `frames` names

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: Every variant is a `role="status"` named "Loading" (`label` changes it). The `ring`, `dots`, `bars` and `pulse` variants put it in `aria-label`; `glyph` renders the label as visually hidden text and hides the changing character with `aria-hidden`, so the frames are never read out.
`label=""` makes the spinner decorative: no role and `aria-hidden`. Do that when the surrounding text already says what is loading (a Button with `loading` does it with its own label).
Several spinners on one page are several `status` regions with the same name: label them by what is loading.

motion.text: `ring` keeps spinning, because it carries meaning (the net in `sutra.css` keeps `animate-spin`). `dots`, `bars` and the halo of `pulse` use looping utilities that the net stops, leaving a still row of dots, a still row of full-height bars, or a still disc with a dot in it. `glyph` checks `usePrefersReducedMotion` and holds its current frame.

ssr.text: Plain markup, and the glyph variant always starts on frame 0 (the reduced-motion hook reads `false` on the server), so server and client output match and the cycling starts after mount.

gotchas: The box variants are `text-primary` by default (they use `currentColor`): recolour with a `text-*` class. The `glyph` variant has no colour class and inherits it, and takes its font size from the parent unless you pass `size`.
`size` is `xs` 12px, `sm` 16px, `md` 20px (default), `lg` 24px or `xl` 32px for the box variants; they scale with their box, so `className="h-1.5 w-6"` gives a compact row of dots.

`frames` (glyph only) takes a set name (`dots`, `line`, `arc`, `circle`, `bounce`, `star`, `pulse`) or your own array of strings; an empty array or an unknown name falls back to `dots`. `interval` is clamped to at least 16 ms, and `paused` holds the frame.
`frames`, `interval` and `paused` are ignored by the other variants.

SplitButton.use: A primary action fused with a chevron button that opens a menu of secondary actions, such as Save with Save as draft or Publish with Schedule. Takes Button's `variant` and `size`, an `actions` array and optional custom `menuContent`.
instead: a menu with its own trigger and no default action
choosing a value rather than running an action

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves to the main button, then to the chevron button; a disabled or `loading` half is skipped
On the main button: run the primary action
On the chevron button: open the menu
In the menu: move the highlighted action
Highlight the first or last action
Run the highlighted action and close the menu
Close the menu and return focus to the chevron

keyboard.text: Menu rows are vertical, so no arrow keys swap in RTL. The two halves use logical corners, so in an RTL page the chevron sits on the left of the main button.

screenReaders.text: The pair is wrapped in a `role="group"` with no name; pass `aria-label` to name the main button (extra props go to it, not to the group). The chevron is a `<button>` named "More options" (`menuLabel`, also used as its `title`) with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` while open, and its arrow icon is `aria-hidden`. The menu is the `DropdownMenu`: `role="menu"` with `menuitem` rows, the optional `menuHeading` as a label, and `aria-disabled` rows.

motion.text: The press scale is switched off on both halves (`active:scale-100`) so they stay visually joined. Colour fades end in 1 ms under reduced motion and the menu loses its movement and keeps its fade. The `loading` spinner on the main button keeps turning.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API at render. The menu is closed, so only the two buttons render on the server; the menu is portalled after mount.

gotchas: The chevron and the menu only exist when there are `actions` or `menuContent`; with neither, the component is a plain `Button` in a group.

`disabled` and `loading` disable both halves (the chevron is disabled while `loading`), and `loading` shows the spinner on the main button only. `onClick` and other button props belong to the main button.

Each action needs `id`, `label` and `onSelect`; the menu closes after `onSelect` runs. An action's `variant: "destructive"` colours the row red, and `shortcut` is a display-only hint that binds nothing.

`menuContent` renders after `actions` and should be `DropdownMenuItem` or other menu parts; `align` defaults to `end`, so the menu lines up with the chevron end of the button. `size` follows Button's scale (`xs` to `xl`) and `variant` any Button variant, with a matching divider between the halves.

SplitPane.use: Two resizable panes with a draggable, keyboard-operable divider, an optional saved size, and a narrow-width fallback that stacks the panes or shows one at a time. Use it for editor and preview, list and detail, or a sidebar next to content.
instead: more than two panes, nested splits and tab groups
a panel that overlays the page
switch between views rather than see both

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the divider (the only tab stop in the component)
Horizontal split: move the divider left or right by `step` percent (Shift doubles it)
Vertical split: move the divider up or down
Shrink the first panel to `min`, or grow it to `max`
Collapse the first panel, or restore it (unless `collapsible={false}`)

keyboard.text: The divider follows the arrow you press in both directions: in RTL the first panel sits on the right and the two horizontal arrows swap their effect on its size. Dragging with a pointer also measures from the right edge in RTL.

items: The divider is a focusable `role="separator"` (the window-splitter pattern) with `aria-orientation` (`vertical` for side-by-side panes), `aria-valuenow` as the first panel's percent (0 when collapsed), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-controls` pointing at the first panel. Its name is "Resize panels"; pass `aria-label` on `SplitPaneHandle` to say which panes ("Resize editor").

A collapsed first panel gets `hidden`, so it leaves the accessibility tree. In `collapseMode="primary"` a group "Show panel" of `aria-pressed` buttons (named by each panel's `label`) switches panels; when stacked the divider is not rendered.
The panels are plain `div`s with no role: add landmarks or labels yourself.

motion.text: Nothing moves except a colour fade on the divider, which the global net ends in 1 ms. Resizing follows the pointer or key presses directly with no animation.

ssr.text: The panes render on the server and on the hydrating client render at `defaultSize` (or `size`), so the markup matches. With `storageKey` the saved size is read right after hydration, before paint, and applied without calling `onSizeChange`; `collapseBelow` is judged from a measured width, so stacking only happens after mount.

gotchas: It is built for two panels: the first is sized (`size` percent, clamped to `min` 15 and `max` 85) and the second fills the rest. If you render no `SplitPaneHandle`, one is inserted before the second panel.
Give the pane a height (for example `className="h-96"`): sizes are percentages of the container, the root clips overflow and each panel scrolls itself.

`defaultSize` is the starting size and the double-click reset value. Controlled use is `size` with `onSizeChange`, which is called on every move, as is the write to `localStorage` when `storageKey` is set (a saved value beats `defaultSize` on mount; a blocked storage is ignored).

`collapseBelow` is a container width in px: below it the divider is removed and the panes stack (`collapseMode="stack"`) or show one at a time (`"primary"`). Any resize, even from the keyboard, restores a collapsed first panel.

Stack.use: A flex layout on the spacing scale: a column by default, with gap, alignment, justify and wrap props. `HStack` is the same in a row, centred on the cross axis.
instead: centre content and cap its width

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: A plain `div` with no role, so it is invisible to assistive technology and the DOM order is the reading order. `direction="row"` and `justify` change only the layout, not the order, so keep the source order meaningful. With `asChild` the child element (a `ul`, `nav`, `section`) keeps its own semantics.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: `gap` takes the steps 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 12 (4 is 1rem) and defaults to 4: other numbers have no class. `direction` defaults to `column`.
`HStack` is `direction="row"` with `align="center"` as default; pass `align` to change that. It takes every other `Stack` prop except `direction`.
Row direction and `justify` follow the writing direction, so a row flips in RTL without changes.
`wrap` is only the flex-wrap flag. Children of a column that should not stretch need `align="start"`, because the cross-axis default is the browser's stretch.

StackedMeter.use: One bar split into coloured parts with a legend, for a breakdown against a capacity (storage by kind, time by phase). The legend is inline chips or a `BreakdownList` with values and percentages.
instead: only the legend rows, next to a chart you draw yourself

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. The `legend="list"` rows are static here (they are not toggle buttons); use `BreakdownList` directly for a legend that hides series.

items: The root is a `role="group"` named by `label` (through `aria-labelledby`); without `label` the group has no name, so pass `aria-label`.

The bar is a `role="img"` whose label summarises the parts: "Models 50 GB, Datasets 20 GB of 100 GB". Override it, or turn the bar into a real meter, with `trackProps` (for example `role: "meter"` plus the `aria-value*` attributes).
The legend is a real list of the parts with their values; the colour swatches are `aria-hidden`.
`loading` with no `parts` replaces the bar and legend with `aria-hidden` placeholders and an sr-only "Loading Storage…"; with parts it only sets `aria-busy`.

motion.text: Part widths animate over 500 ms, and the loading track pulses; both have `motion-reduce:` variants that switch them off.

ssr.text: Plain markup computed from the props (the label id uses `useId`), so server and client output match.

gotchas: `max` is the capacity: without it the bar is the sum of the parts and always full. The header text defaults to "used / max" (or just the sum); `valueText` replaces it and `showValue={false}` hides the header.

Parts without `color` take the chart palette in order; a `color` is a token name (`primary`, `success`, ...) or any CSS colour. Parts with a value of 0 or less draw nothing but still appear in the legend. Each drawn part has `data-slot="stacked-meter-part"` (change it with `partSlot`) and a `title` tooltip.

`legend` is `true` or `"inline"` for chips, `"list"` for rows with a percent column (`showPercent` defaults to true for the list, false for chips), or `false` for none. Percentages are of `max`, otherwise of the total.
Keep `key` stable: it defaults to `label`, so two parts with the same label collide.

StatCard.use: A metric tile: label, big value with unit, optional delta, hint, sparkline, progress bar, stat row and body. With `href` or `onClick` the whole card is one link or button. `StatGroup` lays tiles out in a row, `TopItemCard` is the preset for "the biggest item right now", `StatValue` is just the number.
instead: the page-header metric with a live chart

head: Key
Action
rows: Without `href` or `onClick` the card is not focusable. With either, the label is the one tab stop and the focus ring is drawn around the whole card
Follows the link or presses the button
Presses the button (a link does not react to Space)

keyboard.text: Nothing depends on the arrow keys, so RTL changes only the chevron, which mirrors.

items: The card is a plain `div` with no role. The label, value, unit and delta are read as text in order; a delta adds hidden "Increased", "Decreased" or "Unchanged" before it.

With `href` or `onClick` the label is an `<a>` or a `<button>` stretched over the card, and `aria-describedby` points at the value block (caption, value, delta), so the link is announced with its value.
`trend` is an image named "<label> trend" ("Trend" when the label is not a string) with no values: show the number as text too. `progress` is a `progressbar` named by the label.
With `loading` the root has `aria-busy`, there is one hidden "Loading CPU…", and the label, caption and stat labels stay visible.

motion.text: Hover only tints the card and nudges the chevron, both transitions the global net ends in 1 ms. The digit roll of `animate` (opt-in, numbers only) is a transition too, so under `prefers-reduced-motion` the value changes at once. The sparkline does not animate, except bars (`trendType="bar"`).

ssr.text: Plain markup from props with a `useId` id; the same on server and client. `animate` and the default number text use the runtime locale: pass `valueLocale` and `valueFormat` when the server and the browser may differ.

slots: `stat-card`: the root; `stat-body`: caption, value row and delta; `stat-value`: the number
`stat-link`: the label link or button; `stat-chevron`: its arrow
`stat-stats`, `stat-content`, `stat-trend`: the stat row, the `children` body and the footer trend
gotchas: `loading` always shows placeholders for the value, hint, delta, stat values, progress, trend and `children`, even when a value is present (there is no refresh state); pass it only until the first value arrives.

Delta direction comes from the sign of a number or a leading `+`, `-` or `−` in a string; colour comes from `deltaIntent` (default `positive-is-good`: up is green; `negative-is-good` flips it, `neutral` greys it). `deltaSuffix` ("%") is added to numbers only.
A linked card covers its content with the stretched link: other buttons inside (in `children` or `status`) need `relative z-10` to stay clickable.

`tone` tints the value only for `warning` and `destructive`; the trend follows the delta quality unless `accent` or `trendColor` is set. In a `StatGroup variant="divided"` the cards lose their own border and shadow.

StatusBadge.use: A status pill with a coloured dot, spinner or icon and a label, from 13 preset statuses or any `tone`. `StatusDot` is the same indicator on its own.
instead: a category or tag with no status meaning

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

items: `StatusBadge` is a plain `<span>`. The label is visible text (the status name, `label`, or `children`), and the indicator inside it is always `aria-hidden`: the text carries the meaning, so never pass an empty label with a coloured dot.

`StatusDot` on its own is a `role="img"` named by `label`, which defaults to the status name ("Busy"). With only `tone` and no `status` or `label` it is `aria-hidden`, so a bare dot is silent. `label=""` hides it on purpose.
`icon="spinner"` renders a `Spinner` with an empty label (decorative); the node you pass as `icon` is wrapped in `aria-hidden`.

motion.text: The `pulse` halo uses `motion-safe:animate-ping`, so it never runs under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The pop of a changed custom icon (`animate-pop`) is stopped by the net in `sutra.css`, and the colour fade ends in 1 ms. The `spinner` icon keeps spinning, as it carries meaning.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The icon pop is skipped on the first render and only plays when the status changes later.

gotchas: `tone` wins over the colour of `status`, and `status` still supplies the default label. Statuses: online, offline, busy, away, active, inactive, pending, success, error, warning, info, draft, processing (`processing` is primary and pulses by default).

`pulse` only affects the dot: it does nothing with `icon="spinner"` or a custom icon node. In `StatusBadge`, `variant` is the pill style (`soft`, `outline`, `plain`); the dot's own fill (`solid`, `hollow`, `dashed`) exists only on `StatusDot`.
`icon={null}` or `false` removes the indicator on `StatusBadge`; on `StatusDot` any `null` or boolean icon draws the plain dot.
`children` replace the default label, and `label` is ignored when `children` are present.

StepWizard.use: A multi-step flow in one place (onboarding, checkout, setup): a progress bar or step indicator, the current step's content that slides in the direction of travel, validation before moving forward, and Back, Next and Finish buttons.
instead: only the progress indicator, with you owning the content
sections the user may open in any order
a single focused task without stages

head: Key
Action
rows: Through the completed-step buttons of the indicator, the step content, then Back and Next
In a text input inside a step: presses Next, or Finish on the last step. Not in a textarea or a button-type input, and not while an IME is composing
On Back, Next or Finish, and on a completed step in the indicator: activates it

keyboard.text: Back is disabled on the first step, and both buttons wait while a check or `onComplete` is pending (Next shows its spinner). Upcoming steps in the indicator are not buttons, so you cannot jump ahead. Nothing uses the arrow keys; in RTL the Back and Next arrows mirror and the slide-in comes from the other side.

items: Every step panel is a `group` named "Step 2 of 4" (`labels.step` changes it). When the step changes, focus moves to the new panel (not on first render), so it is announced. With `keepMounted`, the other panels are `hidden` and `inert`.

The indicator is an ordered list named "Progress" with `aria-current="step"` on the current item and hidden "(completed)" text on finished ones. The progress bar is a `progressbar` named by the same "Step n of m" text, next to the step title.
With `indicator="auto"` both exist, and the container width (28rem) hides one with `display: none`, so only one is exposed. The root is `aria-busy` while a check or completion is pending.
Showing the error is yours: `onBlocked` and `onError` tell you where, and the wizard does not render a message.

motion.text: A step change slides and fades in (`animate-in`, from the end side going forward and the start side going back) and the area animates its height. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` no slide class is added and the height transition ends in 1 ms. The preference is read when a step changes, not live.

ssr.text: The first step renders in full on the server (the first render has no entrance animation). The viewport height is measured after mount and then set as an inline style, and the choice between the step indicator and the bar is a container query in CSS, so the markup does not mismatch.

slots: `step-wizard-viewport`: the clipped, height-animated area; `step-wizard-panel`: one step (`data-state` current or hidden)
gotchas: `canAdvance(step, index)` runs before leaving a step forward (Next, Finish) and may be async; return `false` to stay, and `onBlocked` fires. Going back is never checked, and `onValueChange` and `onComplete` run only after the check passes.
Only the current step is rendered, so local state of other steps is lost on the way back. Pass `keepMounted` to keep every step in the tree.

`value` is the step id and a missing id shows the first step. A custom `footer` (or `footer={false}`) removes the built-in buttons: drive the wizard with a controlled `value`, which `canAdvance` does not guard (only the buttons, the indicator and Enter go through it).

`onComplete` only reports Finish (and may return a promise: the button shows loading until it settles); it does not navigate. A throw or rejection from `canAdvance` or `onComplete` goes to `onError` and keeps the step.

Steps.use: Shows progress through a multi-step flow as numbered circles, thin bars or dots, horizontal or vertical. Optional clickable steps, per-step `status`, `description`, `content` and (vertical) `action`.
instead: where the user is in a site hierarchy
switching between panels of equal rank
the whole wizard with panels, navigation and validation

keyboard.text: Not focusable by default: no keyboard interaction. With `onStepClick`, each completed and current step is a native `<button type="button">` and its own tab stop; Enter and Space activate it. Upcoming steps stay plain `div`s (not focusable) unless `restrictToCompleted={false}`. There are no arrow keys, so nothing swaps in RTL.

screenReaders.text: The root is an `<ol>` named "Progress" unless you pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. The current step's `<li>` has `aria-current="step"`; completed steps get an sr-only "(completed)" after the title (English text, not translatable through a prop); upcoming steps carry no extra text. The marker number is real text, so a step reads like "2 Profile", while the check icon and the connector lines are `aria-hidden`. The `bars` variant adds a visible "Step N" line. `data-status` on each `<li>` reflects `complete`, `current` or `upcoming`.

motion.text: The marker colours, connector fill and bar fill are transitions that end in 1 ms under reduced motion. The check mark that replaces a number on completion pops in with `animate-in zoom-in-50 fade-in-0`, and the reduced-motion net removes the scale and keeps the fade.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API or measuring, so the server and the client render the same list.

gotchas: `current` is the zero-based index of the current step; `steps.length` marks every step complete. A step's own `status` overrides what `current` implies, including `aria-current` and the "(completed)" text, which suits checklists finished out of order.
The step label field is `title`. The `steps` prop description in the generated reference says `label`, but only `title`, `description`, `icon`, `status`, `content`, `action` and `itemProps` exist.

`content` renders under the step but outside the clickable area, so inputs and links inside it are not nested in the step button; `action` shows only for the vertical `circles` and `dots`. The `bars` variant ignores `icon`, `action`, `size` and `connector`.
`StepIndicator` is a deprecated plain alias of `Steps` (and `StepIndicatorProps` of `StepsProps`); use `Steps`.

SutraMascot.use: The Sutra mascot, a friendly character with eight states (idle, listening, thinking, working, speaking, happy, sleeping, error), in eight characters a user can choose from (`mascotCharacters`: bead, pendant, mala, bindu, knot-pendant, bow, bun, sutradhar). Use it as the assistant or agent avatar, an empty state, or a loading companion.
instead: a plain wait with no personality
the voice assistant visual driven by a live audio level
a one-off logo animation, not a status

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. Put a button around it when it should act, and name that button. For a "Choose your Sutra" setting use `RadioGroup` with `RadioCard`s (arrow keys move the choice) named by `mascotCharacterLabels`.

items: Decorative by default: the svg is `aria-hidden`, so say what Sutra is doing in live text next to it (a `role="status"` line).
`title="Sutra"` names it (`role="img"` with a `<title>`); `title` set to `true` uses the label of the current state (`mascotStateLabels`: "Sutra is listening").
Do not name it when the same words are beside it: the name would be read twice.
The state and the character are also in `data-state` and `data-character` for tests and styling.

motion.text: Each state has its own face and extras in the markup (eyes, mouth, rings, thought dots, sparks, stars, z marks, a bang), so a still mascot still tells the states apart. The bead moves with CSS keyframes on `data-part` started by `data-state`; under `prefers-reduced-motion` or `data-motion="reduce"` the twin blocks at the end of `sutra.css` remove them. The other characters are drawn frame by frame, because their motion is geometry CSS cannot express (a pendulum with a knot a beat behind, beads riding a spline, two-bone arms and legs, a winding curl): each is a pure function of time, the still pose is the markup, and while motion is allowed one shared `requestAnimationFrame` for the whole page writes only the attributes that changed (no React render per frame). A mascot joins that frame only while it is on screen and not `paused`; under reduced motion it requests no frame and shows the still pose. `paused` freezes any character where it is. A change of state is smooth: the frame-drawn characters blend the pose on screen into the new state over about a third of a second and blink on the way, so the face changes behind shut eyes, and the bead's new face opens from a blink; under reduced motion the change is instant.

ssr.text: The same markup on the server and the client: the frame-drawn characters render the still pose of their state. The mask ids come from `useSafeId`, so two mascots never share one.

gotchas: `happy` and `error` are one-shot (a jump, a swing, a shake) and then rest. Set the state again after another one, or change `replayKey`, to play them again; the svg is never remounted.

Faces and gaps are cut out with masks, so they show whatever is behind. `shape="circle"` or `"squircle"` adds a paper tile with the brand inks and clips the art (`sutradhar` becomes head and shoulders, the best avatar form for it). `tone="dyed"` with an `app` fills the beads with its dye; threads stay ink.

The bead's jump may leave its box (`overflow: visible`); the other characters are clipped to theirs, and the pendants' thread runs off the top edge, so give `pendant`, `knot-pendant` and `bun` room above the bead.

`bindu` differs from the review design to stay clear of Dragon Quest's Slime (a squat drop with a short pointed tip and a wide grin): a taller, narrower body (radius 14.2, tip 29.5 above the belly), a longer, more prominent thread curl (scaled 1.18) and a smaller mouth (0.72).

SutradharSting.use: A short logo sting with Sutradhar (the full-figure mascot) and the Sutra mark, the crescent bead on its thread. `mark`: he walks in with a bare thread, the bead drops onto it and becomes the mark, he plants it and smiles. `astra`: he summons a hand astra (the crescent bead on a short thread), charges it until ink lightning crackles round the bead, swings it into the aim and fires an ink wave into empty space. Both end on a still lockup. `astra-endless`: the same astra on a wide stage that never stops once fired: the lightning keeps crackling, arcs and beads flow out along the wave, and the wave streams across the whole stage. Use it on a splash screen, an onboarding step or a launch moment.
instead: a status character that shows what the assistant is doing

keyboard.text: Not focusable. Offer your own button to replay it (change `replayKey`) and to skip a splash that waits on `onComplete`.

items: Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`). `title` names it (`role="img"` with a `<title>`), for example "Sutradhar plants the Sutra mark".
The sting carries no information; never make a task wait on it without a way to skip.

motion.text: `autoPlay` (default) plays once when it first comes on screen; `false` shows the lockup until `replayKey` changes; a play ends on its last frame, which is the lockup, so it settles without a jump; `loop` plays again after a short hold, fading out and back in instead of cutting, and never calls `onComplete`; `astra-endless` keeps streaming for as long as it is on screen (it calls `onComplete` once, when its stream reaches full length) and holds the stream still under reduced motion. It runs on the mascot's shared frame driver (one `requestAnimationFrame` for the page, attribute writes only, no React render per frame) because the sequence is geometry CSS keyframes cannot express: a walk, two-bone arms, a bead dropping onto a turning thread, a wave of five layered sines. It pauses off screen, and draws its first frame before paint so the lockup never flashes first. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` or `data-motion="reduce"` only the lockup is shown, no frame is requested, and `onComplete` is called at once.

ssr.text: The final lockup is the markup, the same on the server and the client; mask ids come from `useSafeId`.

slots: `sutradhar-sting`: the svg root (`data-variant`, `data-playing` while it plays)
gotchas: `size` is the height; the width follows the drawing (6:5 for `mark`, 16:13 for `astra`, 32:13 for `astra-endless`). The drawing is clipped to its box, and the wave is sized to stay inside it at every aim; add `h-auto max-w-full` to let a wide one shrink on a phone.

`aim` is in protractor degrees: 90 straight up, 180 level to the left, 270 straight down, clamped to 30 to 330 (default 150 for `astra`, 172 for `astra-endless`). Aimed to the right he turns round; aimed steeply up or down the view pulls back just enough to keep the whole wave on the stage, and for a downward shot he rises off the ground as he swings. The astra is held in one hand and fires into empty space: there is no target.
The figure and the mark are ink in `currentColor`, so they follow the text colour on paper, dark and the paper style.

SwipeDeck.use: Triage cards one at a time. Drag the top card to either side (or press Skip and Keep, the arrow keys or Enter) and it flies away, with the cards behind stepping up and Undo bringing the last one back.
instead: browse slides with no decision per card
swipe actions on a list row

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the deck, then the Skip, Undo and Keep buttons below it
On the deck: swipes the top card to the right, which is the `end` side in LTR and the `start` side in RTL
Swipes it to the left: `start` in LTR, `end` in RTL
Takes the last swipe back (not with Shift)

keyboard.text: The arrows are physical (the card flies the way the arrow points) while `start` and `end` follow the reading direction, so in RTL ArrowLeft is the `end` side (the test pins it). Keys only count when the deck itself has focus, not when focus is on an input or button inside a card, and are ignored while `disabled` or `loading`.

items: The focusable stage is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="card deck"`, named "Card deck" (`label`) and described by a hidden hint that lists the keys. The top card is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="card"` named "Card n of N".
Cards behind and flying cards are `aria-hidden` and `inert`. The Skip and Keep stamps on a card are `aria-hidden`.

A polite live region announces each swipe, for example "Keep: Invoice 12. 2 left" or "No cards left", and "Undid Skip" for an undo. `getLabel` supplies the item name; without it only the side and the count are said.

Skip, Undo and Keep are real buttons (`startLabel` and `endLabel` rename them and the announcements). `loading` sets `aria-busy`, hides the controls and adds hidden "Loading cards…" text. The hint, "Undo" and the empty text are English and not in a prop.

motion.text: The tilt, the stamps and the follow-the-finger offset are written while you drag, with no animation. The flight of a dismissed card and the fly-in of an undone one are springs that `useDrag` skips under `prefers-reduced-motion`: the card is simply replaced. The cards behind move up through a transition that the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The server renders the top card and the cards behind it (at most `stack` + 1), the controls and the hint, with no browser API at render. Direction, measuring and the drag are all read in handlers and effects.

slots: `swipe-deck-stage`: the focusable group that holds the cards
`swipe-deck-stamp`: the Skip or Keep stamp on a card (`data-side`)
`swipe-deck-empty`: what shows when no cards are left
`swipe-deck-actions`: the row with the Skip, Undo and Keep buttons
gotchas: `getKey` must return a stable id per item: cards, their flights and Undo are tracked by it. Undo only takes back the latest swipe, and only while that card is still directly before the current index and still the same item.
`renderCard` also runs for the cards behind the top one (the deepest is hidden), so keep it cheap. The deck draws the card surface; give it a height through `cardClassName`.

`onSwipe(side, item, index)` reports the side by reading direction (`start` is left in LTR). `index` is the top card, `items.length` means none left; controlled, a swipe asks for the new index through `onIndexChange`.

`actions={false}` removes the buttons, leaving drag and keys only, so keep them unless you provide another path. Only the top card can be dragged, and a drag commits past `distance` (default 90 px) or on a flick.

SwipeRow.use: A list row you drag sideways to reveal action buttons at its start or end, or swipe all the way to run the outermost one. The actions are real buttons that Tab reaches, with arrow and Escape keys on the row as a keyboard path.
instead: the actions fit a menu button on every device
rows the user reorders by dragging
the row content you put inside it (inside an `ItemGroup` the SwipeRow becomes the list item)

head: Key
Action
rows: The action buttons are always in the tab order: focusing one opens its side, and leaving the group closes it
On the row in left-to-right text: opens the `startActions` and moves focus to their first enabled button
In left-to-right text: opens the `endActions` the same way
The arrow of the other side
While a side is open: closes it and returns focus to where it was
Closes an open row and returns focus to where it was

keyboard.text: The row itself is not focusable, so the arrows work from a control inside it (a link or button in the content) or from an action. They are ignored in text fields and with Alt, Ctrl or Meta held. In RTL the arrows swap with the drag direction, so ArrowLeft opens the `startActions` and ArrowRight the `endActions`; this follows from the source (`direction.test.tsx` does not cover SwipeRow).

items: Each side is a `role="group"` named "Actions" (`actionsLabel`), with plain `<button>`s named by their `label`; icons are `aria-hidden`. The actions are in the accessibility tree even while the row is closed, and both sides share one name when both are given.
Inside an `ItemGroup` the row has `role="listitem"`, and the `Item` inside it is not a second list item. Outside one the row has no role.
There is no live announcement when the row opens or an action runs: put the result in your own live region or a toast.

motion.text: The drag follows the finger with no animation. The settle after a release (open, close, or the fly-out of a full swipe) is a spring that `useDrag` skips under `prefers-reduced-motion`: the row jumps to its place and a committed swipe does not visibly fly out. The button colour fade ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The server renders the row and both action groups at rest with a left-to-right direction. The widths are measured and the position is applied after mount, so `defaultValue` or `value` set to a side starts open only after hydration, and in RTL the signs settle after mount.

slots: `swipe-row-content`: the sliding layer that holds your content
`swipe-row-actions`: one side's group of buttons (`data-side` is `start` or `end`)
gotchas: `commit` defaults to true: a swipe past half the row (or a fast flick) runs the outermost action, which is the one marked `commit: true` or the one at the row's edge. Pass `commit={false}` for destructive actions you only want revealed, otherwise one long swipe deletes.

`startActions` and `endActions` are logical: `startActions` are revealed by dragging toward the inline end (right in LTR, left in RTL). `onAction` runs for a button, a key and a swipe alike, after the action's own `onSelect`, and never for a `disabled` action.

The content layer must stay opaque (`bg-background` by default) or the buttons show through; set `contentClassName` when the row sits on another surface. Taps on an open row close it instead of activating the content, and so does a press outside.

`actionWidth` (default 72) fixes the reveal distance without measuring: wider labels truncate rather than widen. Drags that start on inputs, textareas, selects, sliders or `data-swipe-no-drag` elements are ignored.

Switch.use: An on or off setting that takes effect at once, drawn as a sliding switch. `SwitchField` adds a label and description for forms, and `SwitchGroup` stacks switch rows in a fieldset with a `value` map.
instead: a yes or no answer submitted with a form, or a choice in a list
a settings page row (whole-row target, icon, `disabledReason`)

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between switches; every switch is its own tab stop. A disabled switch is skipped
Toggle the focused switch (native button behaviour)

keyboard.text: No arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing except that the thumb slides the other way. Clicking the label of a `SwitchField` toggles the switch.

items: A `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked` and `aria-required` from `required`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and a surrounding `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled`, `required` and `invalid` when you do not pass them.

`SwitchField` names the switch through `<label htmlFor>` and adds the description to `aria-describedby`; `label` is required. A bare `Switch` has no name: pass `aria-label`, or put it under a `FieldLabel`.
`SwitchGroup` is a native `<fieldset>` named by its `legend`, described by `description`. Disabling the group disables every switch natively.
`checkedIcon` and `uncheckedIcon` are shown in the thumb exactly as you pass them, so pass `aria-hidden` icons.

motion.text: The thumb slides with a 300 ms spring transform, and the track colour and thumb icons fade; the reduced-motion net ends all of them in 1 ms, so the thumb jumps.

ssr.text: Plain markup: the state comes from `checked` or `defaultChecked`, and the ids come from `useId`, so server and client output match.

slots: `switch-field`: the row of switch, label and description
gotchas: `labelPosition="left"` moves the switch to the end visually with CSS `order`; the markup order, and so the tab and reading order, stays switch then label.

`SwitchGroup` keeps a `Record<string, boolean>` keyed by option `value`, and `onValueChange` receives the whole map. Each generated switch gets `name` equal to its option value, so a form posts the checked ones under their own names.
Use `checked` with `onCheckedChange` (a boolean) to control a switch; the Radix `value` prop is the string a form posts when it is on.
`size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg` (28, 36 and 44 px wide); the hit area is padded to at least 24 px.

TabDropdown.use: A tab bar that measures its width and moves the tabs that do not fit into a "More" dropdown. It renders only the tab strip: you render the panel for the selected `value`.
instead: the tabs fit and each has a panel
a menu of actions, not a selection that stays visible

head: Key
Action
rows: The selected visible tab is the only tab stop (the first enabled one when the selected tab is in the overflow or disabled); then the More button
Focus and select the next or previous enabled tab, wrapping around
Focus and select the first or last enabled tab
On the More button: open the overflow menu; ArrowUp and ArrowDown then move through it, Escape closes it

keyboard.text: The arrow keys follow the reading direction: in RTL ArrowLeft goes to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one (the nearest `dir`, else `<html dir>`). Arrow keys select as they move, there is no manual activation mode.

screenReaders.text: The strip is `role="tablist"` with `aria-orientation="horizontal"` and an accessible name from `label` (default "Tabs"); each tab is a button with `role="tab"` and `aria-selected`. There is no `tabpanel` and no `aria-controls`: give your own panel `role="tabpanel"` and `aria-labelledby` if you want that relationship. The overflow button is named "More tabs" (`moreLabel` plus " tabs"), or "More tabs, current: Billing" when the selected tab is in the overflow, and its menu is a group of `menuitemradio` rows. A hidden measuring copy of all tabs is `aria-hidden` and not focusable.

motion.text: Static layout: the only motion is colour fades on the tabs, which end in 1 ms under reduced motion. There is no sliding indicator.

ssr.text: The server renders every tab (`visibleCount` starts at the item count and no More button), and the widths are measured after mount with a layout effect and a `ResizeObserver`. A bar that overflows the container therefore collapses into More at hydration, and it re-measures when the container resizes or `items` changes.

slots: `tab-dropdown-measure`: the invisible, `aria-hidden` copy of every tab and the More button used to measure widths
gotchas: It does not render panels or own your content: read `value` (or `onValueChange`) and show the matching panel yourself.
Overflow rows show text only. A `label` that is not a string needs `textValue`, otherwise the menu and the More button fall back to the item `value`. Icons and badges appear only in the visible tabs.
Tabs collapse from the end: the items that fit stay in order, the rest go to More, and a selected overflow tab is shown on the More button instead of among the tabs.
Uncontrolled it starts on `defaultValue`, else the first item. The root needs a width of its own (it is `min-w-0` and measures `offsetWidth`), so put it in a container that can shrink.

Table.use: A native HTML table in a bordered, scrollable box with density, striping and a sticky header, for composing tables by hand. `TableHead` can be a sort button, `TableCheckbox` a selection box.
instead: columns and rows from data, with sorting, selection, loading and empty states built in
a list of rows with media and actions

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves to sort buttons in headers, checkboxes and any control in a cell
On a sortable header, calls its `onSort` (native `<button>`)
On a `TableCheckbox`, toggles it (native checkbox with a 24px hit area)

keyboard.text: There is no arrow-key navigation between cells and rows are not focusable; this is a plain table (only the scroll box around it takes focus, and only while the table is wider or taller than it). No key depends on direction, but `align` is logical: `left` and `right` mean start and end, so they flip in RTL.

items: Real `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th` and `td` elements, so row and column navigation comes from the browser. `TableHead` sets `scope="col"` unless you pass another `scope`. `TableCaption` is a real `<caption>` that names the table, even though it is drawn under it.

A header is sortable when it has `onSort` or `sortDirection`: it then holds a button named by the header text, and `aria-sort` is `ascending`, `descending` or `none` (`sortDirection={false}`). Without either it has no `aria-sort`. The arrow icon is `aria-hidden`.
`TableCheckbox` is a native checkbox with the `checkbox` role and no label of its own: pass `aria-label` ("Select row Ada"). `indeterminate` sets the DOM mixed state.

The scroll container around the table has `tabIndex="0"` and a focus ring while the content overflows it (measured after mount and on resize; not on the server), so a keyboard user can scroll it; a table that fits adds no tab stop. It becomes a `role="region"` named like the table when the `Table` has an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; otherwise it has no role. `DataTable` takes the same two props.

motion.text: Row hover, the sort button and the checkbox tick are transitions, which the reduced-motion net in `sutra.css` ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Plain table markup with no browser API, so server and client output match. The `indeterminate` state of a `TableCheckbox` is a DOM property set after mount.

gotchas: `TableHead` is stateless about sorting: you pass `sortDirection` and flip it in `onSort`. For a sort that manages itself, use `DataTable`.

`className` styles the `<table>`; `containerClassName` styles the scroll box around it, and `bare` removes that box's border and shadow. `stickyHeader` needs a height limit (`maxHeight`) to have anything to stick against.
`density` is `compact`, `normal` or `relaxed` (`comfortable` is a legacy alias of `relaxed`). A row shows as selected with `data-state="selected"`.

`TableCheckbox` stops click propagation, so it does not trigger a click handler on its row, and `checked` and `defaultChecked` follow the controlled and uncontrolled rules (`onCheckedChange` receives a boolean).

Tabs.use: Switches between panels of related content in place, with a sliding active indicator. Four looks (`pill`, `underline`, `solid`, `ghost`), three sizes, horizontal or vertical, optional `accent` colour, trigger `icon` and `badge`.
instead: too many tabs for the width, the rest go into a More menu
navigation between pages (links with `aria-current`, no panels)
a compact switch of a view or a setting
stacked sections that can be open together

head: Key
Action
rows: Enters the tab list on the active tab (the only tab stop), then moves on to the panel
Move to the next or previous tab and wrap around; with the default automatic activation the tab is also selected
The same for `orientation="vertical"`; ignored in a horizontal list
Select the focused tab (what matters with `activationMode="manual"`)

keyboard.text: In RTL the horizontal keys swap: ArrowLeft goes to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous one (the direction comes from `<html dir>` or the nearest `DirectionProvider`). Vertical lists do not swap.

screenReaders.text: `TabsList` is `role="tablist"` with `aria-orientation`; each trigger is `role="tab"` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; each panel is `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its trigger and is itself a tab stop (`tabindex="0"`). A `badge` is part of the tab's name ("Inbox 4"). The sliding indicator is `aria-hidden`. An `icon` you pass is not hidden for you, and an icon-only tab needs `aria-label`. Pass `aria-label` to `TabsList` when the page has more than one tab list.

motion.text: The indicator slides over 300 ms (`motion-reduce:transition-none` makes it jump) and the trigger colour fades are transitions that end in 1 ms. The active panel fades in with `animate-in fade-in-0`; the net removes any movement and the short fade remains.

ssr.text: The server renders the tabs, the selected panel and a plain filled active tab. The sliding indicator is measured after mount (`data-indicator="ready"` on the list), and until then the active trigger paints its own fill, so the look shifts slightly at hydration. The root `dir` is also read after mount (the server writes `ltr`), so in an RTL document the first server paint has `dir="ltr"`.

gotchas: Activation is automatic: moving focus with the arrows selects the tab and calls `onValueChange`. For panels that are costly to render or fetch, set `activationMode="manual"` so only Enter or Space selects.
Inactive `TabsContent` is unmounted (state inside is lost); pass `forceMount` to keep it in the tree, hidden. `value` on `Tabs` and on each trigger and panel must match.
`accent` on `Tabs` colours every active trigger and the indicator; `TabsTrigger accent` overrides it for one tab and inactive tabs stay neutral. `variant="ghost"` has no sliding indicator.
`TabsList` scrolls horizontally (`overflow-x-auto`, no scrollbar) when the tabs do not fit; use `TabDropdown` if they should collapse instead. `fullWidth` stretches the triggers.
Tabs.example:
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@sutra/ui";

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="overview" variant="underline" className="max-w-md">
      <TabsList aria-label="Project sections">
        <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="members" badge={12}>
          Members
        </TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value="settings">Settings</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>
      <TabsContent value="overview" className="pt-4 text-sm">
        Atlas has 3 active sprints and 48 open issues.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="members" className="pt-4 text-sm">
        Twelve people can edit this project.
      </TabsContent>
      <TabsContent value="settings" className="pt-4 text-sm">
        Rename, archive or delete the project.
      </TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  );
}

TagInput.use: A text field that turns what you type into removable tag chips. It takes a `string[]`, with duplicate, `max` and `validate` checks, optional `suggestions` in a dropdown, and paste that splits on separators.
instead: the choices come from a fixed list and need labels (`multiple` mode)
a standalone label, not an editor

head: Key
Action
rows: Commit the typed text as a tag. With empty text Enter is left to the browser (a form submits)
With text, commits it and keeps focus; if the tag is rejected, or the text is empty, focus moves on
In an empty field, remove the last tag. With `confirmBackspace` the first press marks it and the second removes it
With `suggestions`: open the list and highlight the first match; then ArrowUp and ArrowDown move through it, Home and End jump (while an option is highlighted)
With a highlighted suggestion: add it

keyboard.text: The chips are not focusable and their remove buttons are not tab stops (`tabIndex` -1), so the keyboard way to remove a tag is Backspace. Left and Right are not handled, so RTL changes only the layout. While the user is composing text with an IME, none of these keys fire.

items: A native text input named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; `invalid`, `required`, `disabled` and `aria-describedby` come from a surrounding `Field` unless you pass them. Chips are plain text; each remove button is named "Remove" plus the tag.

With `suggestions` the input becomes a `combobox` with `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"` and `aria-activedescendant`; the popover holds a `listbox` named "Suggestions" whose options mark the highlighted row with `aria-selected`. Focus stays in the input.

`showCount` renders "3" or "3 / 5" with a screen reader suffix ("tags") and ties it to the input through `aria-describedby`. `confirmBackspace` adds a polite live region that says "Press Backspace again to remove ...".

motion.text: Each chip fades and zooms in with `animate-in zoom-in-95`, and the dropdown does the same; the reduced-motion net removes the movement and ends the rest in 1 ms. Existing chips animate on mount too.

ssr.text: The chips, the input and the count render on the server from `value` or `defaultValue`, so server and client match. The suggestions popover is portalled and opens only after focus, so it is never in the server HTML.

slots: `tag-input`: the outer box; `tag-input-tag`: a chip (`data-pending-remove` while marked)
gotchas: Duplicates are rejected case-insensitively unless `allowDuplicates`. At `max` the input turns read-only and shrinks away. `onReject(tag, reason)` reports `"duplicate"`, `"invalid"` (from `validate` or `restrictToSuggestions`) and `"max"`.
Pasting text that contains a separator or a line break splits it into tags (up to `max`); plain text with no separator lands in the field. Typing a separator splits the same way.
`separators` lists extra characters; Enter and Tab always commit, and the key names `"Enter"` and `"Tab"` in the list are not treated as characters.

`name` posts one hidden input per tag under the same name. `addOnBlur` commits the pending text on blur, and `normalize` (default trim) runs before every check. `emptyText` is a deprecated alias of `emptyState`.

Text.use: Body text with size, tone and weight steps, plus the small typographic pieces: `Eyebrow` (an all-caps label above a heading), `Kbd` (a key hint) and `InlineCode`.
instead: a heading with the display scale
a whole key combination from a shortcut string

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction. `Kbd` only shows a key; it does not listen for it.

items: `Text` renders a `p` by default; `as` takes `p`, `span`, `div`, `small`, `strong` or `em`, and `asChild` styles your own element. Use `span` inside a line of text so you do not nest paragraphs.
`Eyebrow` is a plain `p`, not a heading: it is read as a paragraph in front of the heading it labels.

`Kbd` renders a native `<kbd>`, which screen readers read as its text. A symbol such as the command key may be read as nothing or as a name, so for combinations that matter use `ShortcutKeys` (it carries spoken text) or add visually hidden words.
`InlineCode` renders a native `<code>`.

motion.text: Static: no animation.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: `tone` is `default` (foreground), `neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive` or `info`; `muted` is the old name of `neutral`. `neutral` is the muted grey, so it is quieter than `default`; `warning` uses the darker readable shade.
`size` is `xs` to `xl` with `md` being `text-base`; `Text` sets no line-height or margin, so spacing comes from the parent (a `Stack`) and line-height from the surrounding styles.

`Eyebrow` is always `text-primary`, uppercase and tracked; override with `className`. `Kbd` and `InlineCode` take only the HTML props of their element plus `className`; they have no size or tone variants.

TextLink.use: An inline link that reads as part of a sentence, with underline styles, an optional external indicator and a button mode for in-sentence actions. With `onClick` and no `href` it renders a `<button>`.
instead: a standalone action (`variant="link"` gives the look)

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from it. A disabled link or button is skipped
Follows the link, or presses the button

keyboard.text: No arrow keys are used, so nothing changes in RTL.

items: Link mode is a native `<a>`; button mode is a `<button type="button">` unless you pass `type`. The name is the text.
`external` adds target `_blank`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a visually hidden " (opens in a new tab)" after the text; the arrow icon is `aria-hidden`.
A disabled link has no `href`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `tabindex="-1"` and `role="link"`, so it is still announced as a link, as unavailable. A disabled button is natively disabled.

motion.text: The colour and underline fades and the nudge of the external arrow on hover are transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms: the effects still happen, without the glide.

ssr.text: Plain markup with no browser API, so server and client output match.

gotchas: The element is chosen for you: a `<button>` when there is an `onClick` and no `href`, otherwise an `<a>`. Pass `as="a"` or `as="button"` to force one. `as="a"` without `href` is not focusable. `ref` is typed as an anchor in both cases, and `external` does nothing on a button.

`underline` defaults to `hover`: inside running text the link shows only its colour until the pointer is over it, so use `underline="always"` there. `size` defaults to `inherit`, which takes the surrounding font size.
`target="_blank"` on its own gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` but not the screen reader hint; only `external` adds the hint. An explicit `target` or `rel` always wins over what `external` would set.

With `asChild`, `external` still sets `target` and `rel` on the child and adds the arrow and the hidden " (opens in a new tab)" text, as the plain link does. A disabled `asChild` link keeps the child's `href`, with `aria-disabled`, `tabindex="-1"` and clicks blocked in the capture phase, so a router link does not navigate.

TextShimmer.use: Text with a light sweep moving across it, for "Thinking…" style status lines. It renders a `span` (or the element in `as`), sets the shimmer through CSS variables and keeps the text itself plain.
instead: a live "agent is working" line with verbs and a timer
a loading indicator that is not text
a placeholder shape for content that is loading

keyboard.text: Not focusable: no keyboard interaction.

screenReaders.text: The text is ordinary text in a `span` (or `as`), read as written. The shimmer is a background gradient clipped to the text, so it adds nothing to the accessibility tree.
