It is not a live region and has no role: for a status that changes, wrap it in your own `role="status"` or put it inside one.

motion.text: The component adds `motion-reduce:animate-none` itself, because the global net does not cover the shimmer animation (the motion guard test lists it as self-guarded). Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the text stops on a static gradient: muted text that brightens towards its right edge.

ssr.text: Plain markup and inline CSS variables, no browser API, so server and client output match. The animation is pure CSS.

gotchas: `duration` is in seconds (default 2) and `spread` is the half-width of the bright band as a percentage of the gradient, clamped to 1 to 50 (default 12). The gradient is twice as wide as the text, so the band covers about twice that share of the text.

The text is `color: transparent` with the gradient clipped to it, and the gradient reads `--muted-foreground` and `--foreground`. A `text-<colour>` class in `className` (`text-foreground`, `text-primary`) is dropped by the class merge so the shimmer keeps working; colour the two ends of the sweep with `--muted-foreground` and `--foreground` instead. Size classes such as `text-sm` are kept.

It is `inline-block`, so it does not wrap with the surrounding line like inline text; give it a block parent for long text. `style` you pass is merged after the shimmer variables, so you can override them.

Textarea.use: The multi-line text field. A native `<textarea>` with the shared input look, optional auto-resize between `minRows` and `maxRows`, and a character counter that uses `maxLength` as its limit.
instead: a textarea that needs addons around it inside an `InputGroup`

keyboard.text: Native textarea behaviour: Enter inserts a new line, Tab moves focus on, and the text keys and selection shortcuts work as in any text field. The component adds no key handlers and nothing is direction dependent, so RTL changes nothing.

items: A native `<textarea>` named by a `<label>`, `aria-label` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`; a textarea with no visible label needs `aria-label`. `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `Field` supplies `id`, `aria-describedby`, `disabled` and `required` unless you pass them.

The `showCount` counter is plain text ("12/280" with a hidden " characters used", or "12" with " characters" when there is no `maxLength`). It is not a live region and is not added to `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader finds it by reading the page but is not told as the count changes. Native `maxLength` stops typing at the limit.

motion.text: Static apart from the border, ring and counter colour transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. The auto-resize height change is applied directly, with no transition.

ssr.text: The textarea renders on the server with `rows` set to `minRows` and the value or `defaultValue`. With `autoResize` the height is measured in a layout effect after mount, so a long value is `minRows` tall in the server HTML and grows when the page hydrates. Without `autoResize` nothing is measured and the output matches.

gotchas: `minRows` defaults to 3 and is both the initial height and, with `autoResize`, the smallest height; `maxRows` defaults to unlimited, and taller content scrolls inside once it is set. A `rows` prop sets the attribute but `autoResize` still sizes from `minRows`.
`autoResize` turns the manual resize handle off (`resize-none`); otherwise the textarea is `resize-y`. It re-measures when the value changes and when the width changes.
`className` is always on the `<textarea>`; `wrapperClassName` applies only when `showCount` adds the wrapper.
The counter turns red when the length reaches `maxLength`, not only when it passes it, and with `showCount` the textarea gets extra bottom padding for it.

ThemeToggle.use: A light, dark and system theme switch, as one icon button that cycles through the modes or as a segmented control showing them all. It toggles the `dark` class and `color-scheme` on `<html>` and remembers the choice in `localStorage`.
instead: any choice between a few options
a plain on or off setting
a long list of options (such as a palette)
another header control, a search field button
theme and other preferences in one menu

head: Key
Action
rows: Focuses the button (`icon`), or the selected segment (`segmented`, one tab stop)
`icon`: switch to the next mode. `segmented`: select the focused segment
`segmented` only: move focus between the segments (Radix roving focus)

keyboard.text: The `segmented` variant is a `SegmentedControl`, so in RTL its horizontal arrows swap the same way. The icon button has no direction-dependent keys.

items: `icon` is one button named "Theme: Light. Switch to Dark" (the current mode and the next one), which changes after each press. There is no live region, so a screen reader may not announce the new name until focus returns to it. The three icons are `aria-hidden` and `title` shows the current mode.
`segmented` is a `radiogroup` named "Theme" with a `radio` per mode ("Light", "Dark", "System"). With `showLabels={false}` each radio keeps its name through `aria-label`.

motion.text: The sun, moon and computer icons turn and fade into each other over 500 ms; `motion-reduce:transition-none` makes them switch at once under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The segmented thumb follows `SegmentedControl` (jumps).

ssr.text: The server and the hydrating client render `defaultValue` or "system" (or "light" when `modes` has no system), so the markup matches. Right after hydration, before paint, an uncontrolled toggle reads the saved mode from `localStorage` (or a dark `<html>` when `modes` has no system and there is no `defaultValue`) and switches to it: that restore does not call `onValueChange`, and nothing is written to storage or `<html>` until it is done. The `dark` class on `<html>` is set in an effect after mount, so the first paint shows the page's own theme: set the class early with a small inline script that reads the same key.

gotchas: Uncontrolled, it stores the mode under `storageKey` (default `"sutra-theme"`; `null` turns it off) and a saved value that is in `modes` wins over `defaultValue`. Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, it stores nothing: you persist.

`applyToDocument` (default true) toggles `dark` on `<html>` and sets `color-scheme`; set it to false when the app applies the theme itself. It writes only the mode, through the same store as `useTheme`, so a `useTheme` caller follows the toggle at once and the toggle never rewrites the brand, neutral, radius or style. Two toggles do not sync with each other.

`modes` is the cycle order (default `light`, `dark`, `system`); `["light", "dark"]` makes a two-state toggle. With no saved or default value the start is `system` when offered, else whatever `<html>` shows.
`system` follows the operating system live and resolves to light or dark (exposed as `data-resolved` on the icon button); its icon is always the computer, not the resolved sun or moon.

TimePicker.use: A typed time of day made of hour, minute, optional second and AM/PM segments, each a spinbutton. The value is a 24-hour `"HH:mm"` string (`"HH:mm:ss"` with `granularity="second"`) whatever clock is shown.
instead: a touch-first scrolling picker (`TimePicker wheel` puts those wheels in a popover)

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves between the segments, then the clear button (with `wheel` on, the clock button comes first)
Previous or next segment (unfinished digits are committed first)
Step the segment by 1, wrapping at the ends without carrying into the next segment; the minute segment moves by `step` and snaps to its multiples; AM/PM toggles
Set the segment to its lowest or highest value
Type into the segment; a complete entry moves focus to the next segment
In the AM/PM segment (or from the hour or minute on a 12-hour clock): set AM or PM
Clear an hour, minute or second segment (AM/PM stays)

keyboard.text: Focusing a segment selects its text. With `wheel` the clock button opens the wheels: each is a listbox (arrows, Page keys, Home, End, type-ahead), Tab reaches Done, Escape closes and returns focus to the button. Ctrl, Meta and Alt chords are left to the browser. The segments sit in a `dir="ltr"` row in any reading direction, so Left and Right keep their physical meaning and nothing swaps in RTL.

items: The wrapper is a `role="group"` named by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or a surrounding `FieldLabel`. Each segment is a text input with `role="spinbutton"`, a name ("Hour", "Minute", "Second", "AM/PM"), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` ("Empty" when unset).
`labels` replaces the segment names, the clear button ("Clear time") and the spoken empty value, for translation.

`invalid`, `required` and `readOnly` set `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and `aria-readonly` on each segment; `disabled` also sets `aria-disabled` on the group. The clock icon and the separators are `aria-hidden`. With `wheel` the clock icon becomes a button named "Choose time" (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`) that opens a dialog of that name with one listbox per wheel (named like the segments) and Done; `labels.wheel` and `labels.done` translate them. On a coarse pointer the segments use `inputmode="none"`, so a tap opens the wheels, not the keyboard.

motion.text: Without `wheel` nothing moves; only the border and focus colours transition, which the net ends in 1 ms. With it the panel fades in like a popover, and a wheel glides to a row it was sent to (a click, an arrow key), which becomes a jump under reduced motion.

ssr.text: Without `hourCycle` and `locale` the clock convention and segment order come from the runtime's default locale, so a server and a browser with different locales can render a 24-hour field against a 12-hour one (an extra AM/PM segment) and trigger a hydration warning. Pass `locale` or `hourCycle` to make the first render deterministic.

slots: `time-picker`: the group element that wraps the segments
gotchas: `onValueChange` receives `undefined` whenever the time is incomplete, for example after clearing one segment; typing a digit that can still grow ("3" in the minute) waits until focus leaves or another digit completes it. `min` and `max` clamp the value when it is committed rather than blocking keys, and they are `"HH:mm"` strings.

With `value` and no `onValueChange` the segments show what was typed but nothing is committed upstream. `name` posts the 24-hour value through a hidden input (empty when incomplete). `step` applies to minutes only and is rounded and limited to 1 to 59.

`wheel` is opt-in: `true` adds the clock button everywhere, `"touch"` only on a coarse primary pointer. The wheels list every hour, minutes in multiples of `step` (a typed minute that is not one stays while it is the value), seconds with `granularity="second"` and AM/PM on a 12-hour clock, in the locale's order but always left to right; rows that `min` and `max` rule out are disabled. `readOnly` and `disabled` turn them off, and `DateTimePicker` does not take `wheel`.

The wheels report through `onValueChange` as they move, like a typed time; a controlled parent that refuses a time keeps the old one. An empty field starts the wheels at `min` (or midnight) and stays empty until a wheel moves or Done is pressed.

Toaster.use: Transient notifications through sonner. Mount `Toaster` once, then call `toast()` or `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.promise` from anywhere. `snackbar()` shows the compact dark `Snackbar`; `Snackbar` also works as a plain inline bar.
instead: a message that stays next to the content it concerns
ask from code and wait for the answer

head: Key
Action
rows: Anywhere on the page: expand the stack and move focus to the notifications region (sonner's default `hotkey`, changeable with `hotkey`)
Moves through the focusable toasts and their action, cancel and close buttons once the region is focused
While focus is inside the region: collapse the stack (it does not dismiss a toast)

keyboard.text: The region is not in the normal tab order (`tabindex="-1"`), so keyboard users reach it only through the hotkey. Toasts can also be swiped away with a pointer. The hotkey has no arrow keys. Sonner reads the document direction (`dir="auto"`) and mirrors its buttons and icons, but `position` is physical: `bottom-right` stays on the right in RTL.

screenReaders.text: The Toaster renders a `<section aria-label="Notifications alt+T" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text" aria-atomic="false">` on first render, so new toasts are announced politely without moving focus (`containerAriaLabel` and `customAriaLabel` rename it). Toasts are focusable list items with no role of their own; the close button is named "Close toast" (`closeButtonAriaLabel`). The success, info, warning and error icons are `aria-hidden`. `Snackbar` is `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` (pass `role="alert"` for errors), its dismiss button is named "Dismiss" (`closeLabel`), and its `icon` sits in an `aria-hidden` span. A snackbar shown through `snackbar()` sits inside the Toaster's live region and carries its own `status`.

motion.text: Sonner's own stylesheet turns off the toast transitions and animations under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so toasts appear and leave without sliding or stacking motion. The loading icon is Sutra's `Spinner`. Auto-dismiss timers are not affected.

ssr.text: The server renders the empty live-region `<section>` only: toasts exist only after `toast()` is called on the client. The colour theme is read from `<html>` in an effect (light first), which cannot show before a toast appears.

gotchas: `toast()` is sonner's own function (re-exported from this module), callable outside React, and shows nothing until a `Toaster` is mounted. Mount exactly one near the root.

Toasts last 4 seconds, pause while hovered, focused or expanded, and have no close button unless you pass `closeButton` to `Toaster`. Without it a keyboard user can only wait or press the hotkey; give actionable toasts `duration: Infinity` and a close button.

`Toaster` follows `.dark` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` unless you set `theme`; it defaults to `position="bottom-right"` and `gap={10}`, shows `visibleToasts` (3) at once, and applies Sutra classes with `unstyled` on. `toastOptions.classNames` are merged with the Sutra ones.

`snackbar(message, options)` returns the toast id and closes after its action runs; `closable` (default true) shows a dismiss button whose `onClose` fires only for that button, so use sonner's `onDismiss` to catch timeouts and swipes. `Snackbar onClose` is a deprecated alias of `onDismiss`.

ToggleGroup.use: A row of toggle buttons that stay pressed, in `type="single"` (at most one) or `type="multiple"` mode, with roving focus. `ToggleButton` is one standalone pressable button (bold, mute, pin).
instead: an exclusive choice that must always have one selected
attached action buttons or an attached radio-role choice
a yes or no answer in a form
a setting that applies at once

head: Key
Action
rows: One tab stop for the whole group: the first pressed item, else the first item. A standalone `ToggleButton` is its own stop
Move focus to the next or previous enabled item, wrapping at the ends (turn off with `loop={false}`)
Focus the first or last item
Press or unpress the focused item (native button)

keyboard.text: Arrow keys move focus only; they never change the value. Disabled items are skipped. In RTL the horizontal arrows swap: the group reads the direction from its parent (a `DirectionProvider`, a `dir` container or `<html dir>`), and its `dir` prop overrides it. With no `orientation` set the Up and Down arrows also move focus; set `orientation` to restrict the axis.

items: The group is `role="group"` (not Radix's radiogroup or toolbar) and has no name of its own: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Every item is a plain `<button>` with `aria-pressed` in both modes, not a radio.
An icon-only item or `ToggleButton` needs `aria-label`. Icons are not hidden for you: pass `aria-hidden` icons next to text.
Pressed state is announced as "pressed" or "not pressed"; the visual tint comes from `data-state="on"`.

motion.text: Only colour, background and border transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends in 1 ms. Nothing slides; for a sliding thumb use `SegmentedControl`.

ssr.text: Plain markup: pressed state comes from `value`, `defaultValue` or `defaultPressed`, so server and client output match. The group writes a `dir` attribute that is `ltr` in the server HTML and settles after hydration, which only shows on an RTL page.

gotchas: In `single` mode, pressing the pressed item clears the value: `onValueChange` receives `""`. If one item must always stay on, use `SegmentedControl`. `multiple` mode gives and takes a `string[]`.
`variant` (`default`, `outline` or `soft`) and `size` set on the group flow to the items through context; an item's own `variant` or `size` wins.
`ToggleGroupItem` needs `value`; a `ToggleButton` is controlled with `pressed` and `onPressedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultPressed`.
The group wraps onto several lines (`flex-wrap`) instead of overflowing a narrow container.

Tooltip.use: A short text label that appears when an element is hovered or focused, for icon buttons and truncated text. `SimpleTooltip` is the one-line form with an optional keyboard `shortcut` chip.
instead: interactive or rich content the user can click into
a help icon with a title and description
anything the user must read or act on

head: Key
Action
rows: Focusing the trigger opens the tooltip after the delay; moving focus away closes it
Close the tooltip while its trigger has focus

keyboard.text: The tooltip has no focusable content and the trigger keeps its own keyboard behaviour. There are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. In RTL, `side="start"` and `side="end"` swap left and right (read through `useDirection()`: a `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else `<html dir>`; a plain `dir` attribute on a container is not seen); the default is `top`, `left` and `right` stay physical, and Radix still flips the bubble on a collision. Pressing the trigger (click, Enter or Space) also closes the tooltip.

screenReaders.text: The content is `role="tooltip"` and, while open, the trigger gets `aria-describedby` pointing at it, so it is read as the trigger's description, not its name. Give icon-only triggers an `aria-label`: the tooltip alone does not name them. If you pass `aria-label` to `TooltipContent`, Radix hides the visual content from assistive technology and exposes that label in a visually hidden `role="tooltip"` copy. The arrow is decoration. Keep tooltip text short and plain; no links or buttons.

motion.text: The bubble fades and zooms in from its trigger and slides slightly from its side; the reduced-motion net removes the slide and the scale and keeps only the fade. The open delay is a timer and stays.

ssr.text: Only the trigger renders on the server; the bubble is portalled after mount and only opens from pointer hover or focus. Nothing differs between server and client.

gotchas: The default open delay is 200 ms (`TooltipProvider` and a provider-less `Tooltip` both fall back to 200, not Radix's 700), and `skipDelayDuration` is 300 ms. Mount one `TooltipProvider` near the root so moving between tooltips skips the delay; without one each `Tooltip` makes its own provider.
Touch does not open it: Radix ignores touch pointers and a tap closes it, so never keep essential information only in a tooltip.

`SimpleTooltip` wraps `children` in `TooltipTrigger asChild`, so the child must accept a ref and forward props to a focusable element. It renders just the children when `disabled`, or when `content` is `null`, `undefined` or `false`.
`SimpleTooltip shortcut` is display only: a spec like `"mod+k"` renders platform-aware chips, a glyph string or an array renders one `Kbd` per entry. Nothing is bound to the keys.

TransferList.use: A queue of uploads, downloads and background jobs: each row has a file icon, name, progress bar, bytes, speed, time left and a status, with per-row actions and a summary header ("3 active · 1 failed · 12.4 MB/s"). `TransferTray` is the floating, collapsible version pinned to a corner, and `TransferItem` is one row.
instead: pick and validate files before they upload
a single blocking task in a modal
one attachment tile in a conversation

head: Key
Action
rows: Through each row's action buttons, then "Clear completed" (and, in the tray, the minimize and close buttons)
Press the focused button: pause, resume, cancel, retry, open, remove, minimize, close

keyboard.text: Rows are not focusable themselves, and there are no arrow keys, so RTL changes nothing. The tray is not modal: it does not trap focus or react to Escape.

items: The list is `role="list"` named by `title` (default "Transfers"); a row's status is spelled out as text ("In progress", "Paused", "Completed", "Failed", "Queued", "Canceled"), so it never depends on colour. Icons are `aria-hidden`; the direction badge is an image named "Upload", "Download", "Move" or "Process".

A progress bar named "<name> progress" shows for active, paused and queued rows that have progress (indeterminate for an active row of unknown size). The percent, bytes, speed and "15s left" are plain text.
A failed row with an `error` renders it in a `role="alert"`, so it is announced when it appears. Action buttons are named with the file ("Pause photos.zip", "Retry track.flac").

The summary line is plain text, not a live region. `TransferTray` is a `region` labelled by its heading ("Uploading 3 items"); its toggle is "Minimize transfers" or "Expand transfers" with `aria-expanded`, and the body is `hidden` while minimized.

motion.text: The component has no motion of its own besides the progress fill's transition, which the global net ends within 1 ms.

ssr.text: Markup is computed from `items`. Speed and time left use `Date.now()` at render when they come from `startedAt` alone, so the server and client can differ by the time between them; give `speed` or `samples`, or pass `now`, to make it deterministic. The tray is fixed to the viewport unless `inline`.

gotchas: It moves no data and does not tick: you update `items` as bytes arrive and the display follows. Speed comes from `speed`, else the last five seconds of `samples`, else `startedAt` with `bytes`; ETA from the speed and the bytes left. A value derived from `startedAt` changes only when you re-render.

A button appears only when the status allows it and you passed the handler: Pause (active), Resume (paused), Retry (failed, canceled), Open (completed), Cancel (queued, active, paused), Remove (completed, failed, canceled). List handlers receive the item `id`. "Clear completed" shows with `onClearCompleted` when completed or canceled rows exist (failed ones do not count).

`status` also accepts `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `canceled` and "cancelled"; `paused` has no TaskStatus equivalent. `progress` (0 to 100) wins over `bytes` and `total`, and a completed row always reads 100%.

`TransferTray position` is physical (`bottom-right` or `bottom-left`) and does not mirror in RTL; `inline` renders it in the flow for previews, and `minimized` can be controlled with `onMinimizedChange`.

TreeView.use: A data-driven tree of nodes you can expand, select (one, many or none) and optionally check with tri-state checkboxes, with the full WAI-ARIA tree keyboard model, type-ahead and indent guides. Use it for file trees, nested settings and category pickers.
instead: a few stacked sections with free content
one value from a flat list

head: Key
Action
rows: One tab stop (roving): the focused node, else the first selected visible node, else the first
Next or previous visible node. With Shift in `multiple` mode the destination is added to the selection
On a closed parent: open it. On an open parent: focus its first child
On an open parent: close it. Otherwise: focus the parent
Select the node (Ctrl or Cmd+Enter toggles in `multiple`) and call `onNodeAction`
Toggle the checkbox when `checkable`, otherwise select (toggle in `multiple`)
Open every closed sibling of the focused node
Select every enabled visible node (`multiple` only)
Jump to the next visible node whose text starts with what you typed (500 ms buffer; the same letter repeated cycles)

keyboard.text: In RTL the two horizontal arrows swap (`logicalArrow`): ArrowLeft opens and ArrowRight closes. Disabled nodes can be focused but not selected, opened or checked.

items: The list is `role="tree"` and needs `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; it has `aria-multiselectable` in `multiple` mode. Nodes are `treeitem`s with `aria-level`, `aria-posinset`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-expanded` (parents only), `aria-selected` (not with `selectionMode="none"`), `aria-disabled`, and, when `checkable`, `aria-checked` including `mixed`. Child lists are `role="group"`.
The chevron, the visual checkbox and the icons are `aria-hidden`: the state is on the item. Collapsed children are not in the DOM.
Type-ahead reads `label` when it is a string or number; use `textValue` for any other label.

motion.text: The chevron turns with the `chevron-turn` transition and child lists open and close with `animate-collapsible-down` and `-up`. The global net ends the transition and the animation in 1 ms, so the list opens at once.

ssr.text: The whole tree is plain markup from `nodes` and the expanded ids; only expanded branches are rendered. Nothing depends on browser APIs until a key is pressed (the direction is read then).

gotchas: A click on a row selects it and, on a parent, also toggles it (`expandOnClick`, default true). The chevron and the checkbox toggle only themselves. Parents are selectable too, and `onNodeAction` runs on click and Enter, not on Space or arrow movement.

`expanded`, `selected` and `checked` are arrays of node ids with `onExpandedChange`, `onSelectedChange` and `onCheckedChange`. Checked state is derived from the leaves: `checked` lists every fully checked node, parents included, and a parent with a disabled unchecked leaf can only ever be `mixed` (toggling it checks the enabled leaves, toggling again clears them).

`selectionMode` defaults to `single`; with `none` rows do not select (and omit `aria-selected`) but still expand and fire `onNodeAction`. With `checkable`, selection and checking are separate: Enter selects, Space checks.
Row height is `size` (`sm` 28 px, `md` 32 px) and nesting indents by 14 or 16 px per level; `indentGuides={false}` and `showIcons={false}` remove the lines and the default folder and file icons.

Treemap.use: Tiles sized by value to compare many parts of a hierarchy at a glance (disk usage, bundle size, spend), with drill-down into groups, a tooltip and a screen-reader table. `StorageMap` wraps it for disks, with a used and free header and macOS, App data, Yours and Other categories.
instead: a handful of parts of one whole
compare values on a common axis
a legend with values and shares
browse a hierarchy by name rather than by size

head: Key
Action
rows: One tile holds the tab stop (the last active one); Tab then leaves the map
Move to the nearest tile in that direction on screen
Open a tile that has items inside; on a leaf it only fires `onSelect`
Go up one level (only while drilled in); focus lands on the tile you came from

keyboard.text: The root is a forced `dir="ltr"` island and the arrows are spatial, so nothing swaps in RTL; the breadcrumb sits inside the island too.

items: The map is a `group` with `aria-roledescription="treemap"`, named by `label` (default "Treemap") and described by a hidden hint on the arrow, Enter and Backspace keys.
Each tile is a `button` named "Documents, 30, 30%, 3 items" (name, formatted value, share, child count); the visible text is `aria-hidden`, so tiles too small for a label are still named.

A hidden table lists the tiles on screen (Name, `valueLabel`, Share) with the path as row header. The breadcrumb is a `navigation` named "<label> location" and a polite live region says "Showing Applications" after drilling. The tooltip is `aria-hidden`.
With `loading` the root has `aria-busy` and one hidden "Loading <label>…".

motion.text: Only tile hover and dim use a 150 ms opacity and background transition, which the global net ends in 1 ms. Drilling swaps the tiles with no animation.

ssr.text: The layout needs the width: the server and the first client render lay the tiles out at `defaultWidth` (600 px), then the real width is measured after mount and the tiles are recomputed, so tile positions move on hydration. Values are formatted with `Intl` in the runtime locale unless you pass `valueFormatter`.

gotchas: Size comes from `value`, or the sum of the children; zero, negative and non-finite values are not drawn, and when nothing has a size `emptyState` (default "No data") shows.
`path` is the list of child ids from the root (the root's own id is not in it) and is controlled with `onPathChange`. `onSelect` runs on every tile activation, leaves included, before drilling.

Backspace and Escape that go up also stop propagation, so Escape inside a Dialog first climbs a level, and closes the dialog only at the top. `depth` above 1 draws framed parents with a header (`StorageMap` uses 2).
Colour is `colorFor`, then the node's `color`, then its top-level group's colour from `palette`; a prop `dir` on the root replaces the LTR island, as props are spread after it.

UndoAction.use: A destructive button that, once pressed, turns into a counted "Undo" for a few seconds and only then commits. The countdown follows the wall clock, shows a ring and a number, and the focus stays on the same button.
instead: the action needs an explicit yes or no first
the action is deliberate and cannot be undone
show the undo as a toast (pair it through `onArm` and a controlled `armed`)

head: Key
Action
rows: Moves focus to and from the button. A `disabled` button is skipped
Idle: starts the countdown (`onArm`). During it: undoes (`onUndo`). The focus never leaves the button

keyboard.text: It is a single native button, so there are no arrow keys and nothing changes in RTL. Once committed it is `aria-disabled` and presses do nothing, but it stays focusable. `pauseOnFocus` holds the countdown while the button has keyboard focus (focus from a click does not count).

items: The name is the visible label of the current phase: `label` ("Delete"), then `undoLabel` ("Undo"), then `committedLabel` ("Deleted"). The other two labels are `aria-hidden`, and so are the ring and its number, so the changing digit is not read.

A sibling visually hidden `role="status"` announces the transitions, nothing on first render: "Undo available for N seconds" when armed, "Undone" after an undo, "Done" after the commit. `messages` replaces any of the three (`armed` is a function of the seconds).
`aria-busy` is on the button while a promise from `onCommit` runs (it is a `Button` with `loading`).

motion.text: The label cross-fade and the ring's progress are short transitions, which the reduced-motion net ends within 1 ms, so the ring steps instead of gliding. The countdown is wall-clock time, not an animation, so it runs the same.

ssr.text: No browser API at render: the deadline starts in a layout effect after mount, and before that the ring shows the full window. A `defaultArmed` button renders armed and begins counting after hydration.

slots: `undo-action-ring`: the ring with the seconds left
gotchas: Unmounting during the window drops the action: `onCommit` never runs (the test pins it). Keep it mounted until the countdown ends, or commit on unmount yourself.

After the commit the button stays on `committedLabel` and is inert; it does not reset on its own. Re-arm it from outside with a controlled `armed`, or remount it. A promise from `onCommit` shows a spinner, and a rejection brings the button back to idle.

With a controlled `armed`, setting it to `false` from outside cancels silently (no `onUndo`), and setting it to `true` starts the countdown. `onArmedChange(false)` fires at the commit too, not only on undo.

`pauseOnHover` ignores touch pointers. `seconds` is at least 1 (default 8). `variant` is the idle look (default `destructive-soft`) and `armedVariant` the counting one (default `secondary`); `onClick`, `children`, `asChild` and `loading` are not accepted.

VolumeSlider.use: A volume control made of a mute toggle with a level-aware speaker icon, a `Slider` from 0 to 100 and a level label ("64%" or "Muted"). Muting keeps the level, so unmuting restores it.
instead: a pressed state with no level
playback or loading position the user does not drag

head: Key
Action
rows: The mute toggle, then the slider thumb
On the toggle: mute or unmute (native button)
On the thumb: raise by `step` (default 1); moving while muted also unmutes

keyboard.text: The thumb follows `Slider`, so in RTL ArrowLeft raises and ArrowRight lowers; the toggle has no direction dependent keys. With `orientation="vertical"` the toggle, slider and level stack in a column.

items: The thumb is a `role="slider"` named by `label` (default "Volume") with `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 100 and `aria-valuetext` set to the level text: "64%", or "Muted" while muted (the value stays at the kept level).

The toggle is a native button. By default it keeps one name, "Mute" plus the label, and reports the state with `aria-pressed`. With `muteToggle="label"` there is no `aria-pressed` and the name swaps to `unmuteLabel` ("Unmute Volume") while it would unmute. Set `muteLabel` and `unmuteLabel` to translate them.
The visible level text is `aria-hidden` because the thumb already announces it; the speaker icon is `aria-hidden`. `hideMuteButton` removes the toggle.

motion.text: The toggle colour fades and the slider's thumb ring and press scale use short transitions; the reduced-motion net ends them in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The toggle, level text and slider track render on the server from `value`, `defaultValue` and `muted`. The slider thumb is `display: none` until Radix mounts and locates it, so it appears after hydration, and the direction settles after hydration on an RTL page.

slots: `volume-slider`: the root; `data-muted` and `data-orientation` are set on it
gotchas: Muting does not change the value: the slider stays at the kept level (it turns neutral grey) unless `zeroWhenMuted` shows it at 0. Moving the slider while muted unmutes and sets the value.
At a level of 0 the icon is muted but `muted` is false. With `restoreOnUnmute={30}` the toggle then reads as "unmute" and sets 30 on press.
`value` is a number from 0 to 100, rounded and clamped; `onValueChange` receives a number and `onMutedChange` a boolean. `muted` and `value` are controlled independently.
`renderSlider` wraps the slider element (for a reveal-on-hover container or a popover); `disabled` disables both the toggle and the slider. `dir` is not accepted: the direction comes from the page.

WheelPicker.use: An iOS-style wheel for one list of values (hour, minute, duration, amount) that you scroll or flick, with one row snapping into the centre band. `WheelPickerGroup` puts several wheels side by side under one band, with one value per column.
instead: a desktop dropdown from a list

head: Key
Action
rows: The wheel is one tab stop (a group has one per column)
Move the selection one row, skipping disabled rows, without wrapping
Type-ahead: select the next row whose text starts with what you typed (a 600 ms pause starts a new query; a repeated letter cycles)

keyboard.text: Space and Enter do nothing; moving the selection is the choice. Alt, Ctrl and Meta chords are left alone. With the mouse or a finger, scrolling snaps one row at a time and clicking a row selects it. The wheel is vertical, so RTL swaps no keys.

items: One wheel is a `role="listbox"` that keeps focus; the selected row is `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-selected` on its `role="option"`, and disabled rows are `aria-disabled`. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`: a bare `WheelPicker` has no name.
`WheelPickerGroup` is a `role="group"` (pass it an `aria-label`) of listboxes named by each column `label`, such as "Hours". Separators and the highlight band are `aria-hidden`.
With `loading` there is no listbox, only placeholder rows, `aria-busy` and the text "Loading…" for screen readers; with no options the `emptyState` text shows instead.
The value is reported when scrolling settles, not for every row that passes the centre.

motion.text: Under `prefers-reduced-motion` a key press jumps to the row; otherwise it glides with a smooth scroll. A parent changing `value` also glides only when motion is allowed, and the row colours fade in a short transition that the net ends in 1 ms.

ssr.text: The listbox and all rows render on the server, but the scroll position is set after mount, so the server HTML is scrolled to the first row and the centre row's bold, foreground style is applied by script after hydration. The box height is set inline from `visibleCount` and `itemHeight`, so only the scroll position changes on hydration.

slots: `wheel-picker-band`: the highlight behind the centre row
gotchas: `options` take strings or `{ value, label, disabled, textValue }`; `textValue` is what type-ahead matches when `label` is not a string. Values must be unique strings.
`visibleCount` (default 5) is raised to the next odd number so there is a centre row, and `itemHeight` (default 36) is in pixels.
`onValueChange` receives a string once the scroll stops. A scroll that stops on a disabled row moves to the nearest enabled one. In a group it receives all values plus `{ columnId, index }`.
`wheelRange` (exported from the same module) builds padded numeric options such as `00` to `59`.
